# Long-Term Care Subsidies

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/Sucth2ke*

Provides means-tested subsidies for long-term care services by MOH-funded long-term care providers.

## Highlights
- For home and community long-term care services provided by MOH-funded providers: Means-tested subsidies of up to 80%
- For institutional long-term care services provided by MOH-funded providers: Means-tested subsidies of up to 75%
- Additional subsidies of up to 15% for Singapore Citizens born in or before 1969

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors
**Keywords:** Budget 2025, Seniors, Subsidies

## About this support
**For home and community long-term care services (e.g. Day Care, Community Rehabilitation services, Home Nursing, Home Medical)**

- Means-tested subsidies of up to 80%
- Additional 15% subsidies for Singapore Citizens born in and before 1969

**For institutional long-term care services (e.g. Nursing Home)**

- Means-tested subsidies of up to 75%
- Additional 5% subsidies for Singapore Citizens born in and before 1969

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents
- Monthly per capita household income (PCHI) of less than or equal to $4,800 (or property annual value (AV) of less than or equal to $21,000 for households with no income)
- Receiving long-term care services from MOH-funded providers

## How to apply?
Persons who require long-term care services can approach their doctor at the hospital, polyclinic, or Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) for assistance in applying for admission to a subsidised long-term care service.

## Where to go
[Find nearest AIC Link](https://www.aic.sg/about-us/aic-link-locations/)

## Agency website
- [Non-residential long-term care services](https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/schemes-and-subsidies/subsidy-framework-for-non-residential-long-term-care-services)
- [Residential long-term care services](https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/schemes-and-subsidies/subsidies-for-residential-long-term-care-services)

## Email / Form
[Submit your enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg)

## Phone number
AIC Hotline: [1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060)

# Healthier SG

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/HEALTHIERSG*

A national strategy focused on preventive care to empower individuals to take steps toward better health, with the support of their Healthier SG clinic and community partners.

## Highlights
- Receive dedicated care from your preferred Healthier SG clinic
- Prevent or manage chronic conditions and complications
- Create your Health Plan with your family doctor
- Receive healthcare and medication subsidies and benefits

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Health screenings, Subsidies, Vaccination

## About this support
Benefits after enrolment include:

- Fully subsidised first Health Plan consultation and subsequent annual Health Plan check-ins with your enrolled Healthier SG clinic
- Healthpoints (worth $20) via Healthy 365 app after the first Health Plan consultation
- One-off Healthpoints (worth $10) via Healthy 365 app upon completing both an in-person annual Health Plan check-in and viewing of Health Plan on HealthHub within the qualifying period of 1 July 2026 to 31 December 2029.
- Special subsidies for Healthier SG screening tests and vaccinations (for eligible Singapore Citizens)
- Healthier SG Chronic Tier subsidy at Healthier SG clinics for CHAS cardholders with high medication requirements (for selected chronic medications at prices comparable to polyclinic prices)
- Full MediSave coverage for treatment of chronic conditions listed under the Chronic Disease Management Programme (CDMP), up to the relevant MediSave withdrawal limit

## Who is this for?
Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents aged 40 years old and above to enrol with a Healthier SG clinic or polyclinic

## How to apply?
**Self-enrol via HealthHub**

If you are eligible, you will be invited via SMS to enrol in Healthier SG. You can do so in three simple steps:

1. Use the HealthHub app, which can be downloaded from Google Play or Apple App Store.
2. Choose your preferred Healthier SG clinic from the [list of more than 1,000 Healthier SG clinics](https://gowhere.gov.sg/healthiersg).
3. Book an appointment for your fully subsidised first Health Plan consultation.

For a detailed step-by-step guide on how to enrol, click [here](https://www.healthiersg.gov.sg/enrolment/guide/).

If you have not received an SMS invitation, you can:

1. Request one by submitting your details at https://go.gov.sg/healthiersg-sms-invite
2. Contact the MOH hotline at 6325 9220

**Enrol with caregiver's assistance**

You can grant your caregiver/family member/loved one access to your HealthHub, so they can use their smartphone to help you enrol in Healthier SG. Follow the step-by-step guide at these links:

- [Grant your caregiver/family member access](https://safe.menlosecurity.com/https:/www.healthiersg.gov.sg/enrolment/addcaregiver/)
- [Assist your family member’s enrolment](https://safe.menlosecurity.com/https:/www.healthiersg.gov.sg/enrolment/caregivers/)

**Other assisted enrolment**

- Visit any ServiceSG Centre or AIC Link for enrolment assistance. To find an enrolment station near you, visit [HealthierSGGoWhere](https://www.gowhere.gov.sg/healthiersg/)

## Where to go
To find a Healthier SG clinic or enrolment station near you, visit [HealthierSGGoWhere](https://www.gowhere.gov.sg/healthiersg/)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.healthiersg.gov.sg/)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://www.moh.gov.sg/feedback/)

## Phone number
MOH Hotline: [6325 9220](tel:63259220)

title: Severe Disability Assessment (SDA)
description: Provides an assessment of your disability status conducted by a Ministry of Health (MOH)-accredited severe disability assessor.
embedding_text:
Domains: Caregiving support, Disability support

# Severe Disability Assessment (SDA)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SDA*

Provides an assessment of your disability status conducted by a Ministry of Health (MOH)-accredited severe disability assessor.

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities
**Citizenship:** SG, PR
**Keywords:** Caregiver support, PWDs

## About this support
SDA is required if you are:

- Applying for the following long-term care severe disability financial assistance schemes administered by the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC):
  - CareShield Life
  - ElderShield
  - ElderFund
  - Interim Disability Assistance Programme for the Elderly (IDAPE)
  - MediSave Care
- Applying for supplement schemes of CareShield Life and ElderShield administered by private insurers – Great Eastern, Income and SingLife
- Undergoing a disability review to ascertain continued scheme eligibility
- Undergoing an underwriting to enroll into selected schemes

## Who is this for?
Anyone who require an SDA to determine your ability to perform each of the 6 Activities of Daily Living, as certified by an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor.

These 6 activities are:

- Feeding
- Dressing
- Toileting
- Washing
- Walking or moving around
- Transferring from bed to chair and vice versa

## How to apply?
To find a severe disability assessors near you, you may visit the [AIC's website](https://aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Severe-Disability-Assessment) and search using a postal code, address, or your device's current location.

If a service provider listed informs you that they do not conduct SDA, please [reach out to AIC with their details](mailto:apply@aic.sg).

For further assistance, you can contact AIC via the hotline[1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060).

- Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines in Singapore.
- Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.

You can also visit the nearest [AIC Link](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)[ ](#_msocom_1)or [submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg).

## What to expect?
- **Assessments are strictly by appointment only**. Please call ahead to make an appointment with the clinic or assessor before going to the clinic.
- You will need to bring along relevant medical reports or discharge summaries related to your assessment when you go for your SDA appointment.
- If your care recipient requires a mental capacity assessment to be completed to obtain certification for the purpose of applying for AIC schemes, please explicitly request for it when making the appointment. Do note that mental capacity assessments can only be completed by doctors.
- A typical SDA will last about 45 minutes or longer.
- SDA fees are as follows, if:
  - You visit an assessor’s clinic: $100
  - An assessor visits your house: $250
- You will be reimbursed the assessment fee which you have paid if you are assessed to be severely disabled.
- For CareShield Life claims, the assessment fee for the first disability assessment will be waived, regardless of whether you are assessed to be severely disabled, or whether the claim is successful.

# Home Medical

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-HM*

Check-ups, prescriptions and consultations by a doctor for seniors who are not able to leave their homes.

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Home Care, Referral required

## About this support
Home visits by doctors to provide house-bound seniors with medical care, such as:

- Physical examinations
- Review and prescription of medications
- Medical advice
- Management of stable medical condition(s)
- Minor medical procedures
- Caregiver education

## Who is this for?
Seniors who are frail, homebound and require help with medical needs at home.

## How to apply?
You can apply:

- Through the hospital, polyclinic or GP who is familiar with your loved one’s condition and needs
- At any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)

If you are interested to view the list of service providers, visit the [AIC’s website](https://www.aic.sg/Care-Services/Home-Medical)[.](#_msocom_2)

For further assistance, you can contact AIC via the hotline[1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060) or [submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg).

- Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines in Singapore.
- Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.

## What to expect?
Subsidies are available depending on the [means-test](https://aic.sg/care-services/home-medical#faq) result.

- Only applicable to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents

# Centre-based Nursing

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-CBN*

Basic nursing care for seniors at a centre near their homes.

**Who it targets:** Seniors
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Day Care, Referral required

## About this support
Offers basic nursing services at centres close to where seniors live, such as:

- Wound care
- Changing of feeding tube
- Caring and dressing of feeding tube (PEG)
- Caring and dressing of tracheostomy tube
- Caring and dressing of kidney drainage tube
- Helping with bowel movements (as prescribed by doctor)
- Stoma care – colostomy and ileostomy care
- Caring and changing urinary catheters
- Post-procedure medication (as prescribed by doctor)

## Who is this for?
Senior who requires basic nursing care.

You can apply:

- Through the hospital, polyclinic or GP who is familiar with your loved one’s condition and needs

# Strengthening Elderly Parent-Adult Child Bonds Programme

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/C46c4FeP*

A 3-year pilot initiative aimed at strengthening relationships between elderly parents and their adult children.

**Who it targets:** Seniors
**Citizenship:** PR, SG, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Families, Seniors

## About this support
This proposed programme will be implemented through activities targeting the elderly parent-adult child dyad to promote quality interactions to help the dyad navigate ageing transitions together. The programme will complement existing active ageing programmes funded by MOH and family bonding programmes funded by MSF.

## Who is this for?
Elderly parents and their adult children.

## How to apply?
Montfort Care will recruit eligible seniors and their adult children through their AACs.

## What to expect?
This proposed programme will be implemented through activities targeting the elderly parent-adult child dyad to promote quality interactions to help the dyad navigate ageing transitions together. The programme will complement existing active ageing programmes funded by MOH and family bonding programmes funded by MSF.

Domains: Caregiving, Caregiving support, Disability support, Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits

# Caregivers Training Grant (CTG)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/CAREGIVERS_TRAINING*

Subsidy for caregivers to offset the training fees of approved courses to equip themselves with the necessary skills to care for their loved ones.

## Highlights
- $400 subsidy for the first year
- $200 annual top-up, with a total CTG balance cap of $400 at any given time
- Contact the service provider at least two weeks before the course starts

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors
**Keywords:** Caregiver support, Subsidies, Trainings

## About this support
- $400 grant for eligible care recipients in their first year of tapping on CTG
- CTG balance can be used to subsidise their caregivers attending approved caregiver training courses
- Co-payment of at least $10 for every course attended by the caregiver
- $200 annual top-up in subsequent years, with total CTG balance capped at $400 at any given time
- If multiple caregivers of the same care recipient wish to attend training, they can tap on the same CTG balance available to offset the course fees

## Who is this for?
Care recipient must be:

- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- Aged 65 and older

OR

- Have a disability assessed by an approved healthcare practitioner

Caregiver must be:

- Main person caring for the care recipient (e.g. family members and foreign domestic workers)

## How to apply?
- [Choose an approved course here](https://training-healthcare.vertis.digital/)
- Contact the training provider to confirm course details
- Register for the course
- Inform the trainer about using CTG at least two weeks before the course starts
- Your trainer will give you the CTG application form to fill out, and will submit it on your behalf
- [You can also visit the AIC’s website to download the CTG application form](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Caregivers-Training-Grant)

## Where to go
[Visit the AIC Link branch nearest to you](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Caregivers-Training-Grant)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg)

## Phone number
AIC Hotline: [1800 650 6060](tel:1800-650-6060)

Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.

# grovve

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/34sPdG1b*

An integrated, youth-centric wellness centre offering a safe space where young people aged 12 to 25 can seek mental health support.

**Who it targets:** Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Resources and Support, Social-emotional Support, Students

## About this support
- A welcoming space where youths aged 12 to 25 can hang out and access mental health support.
- An on-site concierge manages basic support needs for youths and their caregivers.
- For those requiring more in-depth support such as counselling or case management, a range of services are available through on-site partner organisations.
- Scheduled activities are also organised within the space to engage youths and caregivers.

## Who is this for?
Youths aged 12 to 25 and their caregivers

## How to apply?
Walk in during opening hours or get in touch with grovve via WhatsApp at https://mindline.sg/grovve/about/visit.

## What to expect?

embedding_text:
Domains: Caregiving support

# Gift of A Lifetime Plus (GOAL+)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/4JyHzRKo*

The programme aims to provide eligible caregivers of Person with Disabilities (PWDs) with an initial capital of $5,000 to set up Trust accounts with Special Needs Trust Company (SNTC)

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities
**Citizenship:** SG, PR
**Keywords:** Subsidies

## About this support
The initiative aims to encourage caregivers from low-to-middle income households to proactively plan for longer term needs of PWDs through structured and accessible mechanisms by lowering the upfront costs required to establish Trust accounts and top up the trust account to receive the matching grant (up to $10,000) under GOAL+.

## Who is this for?
1. Applicants should be Singapore citizens or permanent residents of Singapore.
2. Applicants have per capita household income of not exceeding $3,600 or Annual value of property ≤$21,000 if PCHI is zero.
3. PWD has a Disability Verification Form (DVF).

## How to apply?
Applicants may request their social worker to refer them to SG Enable or they can contact SG Enable directly via phone or email.

## What to expect?
1. Screening will be carried out to determine Service User’s eligibility and suitability.
2. Case Managers will develop care plans tailored to meet the strengths, needs, abilities and preferences of the service users and/or their families with the families.

title: HCSA SPIN

embedding_text:
Domains: Caregiving support, Family, parenting and relationships

# HCSA SPIN

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-HDSSPIII*

SPIN supports single parents and lone caregivers through casework and counselling, social support network such as befriending, practical support and an online portal of information and resources.

**Who it targets:** Families
**Citizenship:** SG, PR
**Keywords:** Free, Resources and Support

## About this support
SPIN aims to empower single parents and lone caregivers to be resilient and self-reliant, and to help them attain increased capacity in caregiving/parenting, improve their social support, psychological well-being and increase their access to practical resources.

Services include:

- Needs assessment by social workers and co-creation of individualised care plans with single parents/lone caregivers to address identified needs.
- Counselling for single parents and children who have been assessed to be in need for emotional and mental health support.
- Befriending and peer support for single parents to build social support and trust amongst other parents and volunteers
- Counselling, tuition and homework support for the children (aged 7 to 17) of the clients
- Workshops and events to empower single parents with essential life and career skills
- Practical support such as referrals to resource channels to support clients in meeting identified needs, disbursement of grocery vouchers and food items

## Who is this for?
- Single parents or lone caregivers of children below 18 years old, and these children
- No income criteria and no geographical boundaries

## How to apply?
You may

1. Approach any Family Service Centre (FSC) for referral, or
2. Sign up online at https://crm.hcsa.org.sg/spin-member-application-form/ to fill up the online registration form, or
3. Call or email the programme for assistance in signing up.

## What to expect?
A social work associate will respond to the enquiry/referral within 3-5 working days and arrange for intake assessment. Thereafter, a social worker will be assigned to the parent, and trained befrienders will be matched to the parent. The programme is for a maximum period of 12 months. After the programme ends, the parent will be invited to join the Alumni Chapter to continue staying connected with a community and contribute to a supportive network of single-parent families.

embedding_text:
Domains: Caregiving support, Education and learning, Family, parenting and relationships

# CARENIGHTS

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/KXiQ9o1l*

Supports children aged 6 to 14 from vulnerable families with structured evening care services.

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Caregiver support, Free

## About this support
The CareNights programme is a structured evening care for children aged 6 to 14 from vulnerable families, including those referred through ComLink+ or other community partners. It addresses a critical gap in after-school support, particularly helping caregivers who are working, attending training, or managing caregiving responsibilities.

## Who is this for?
- Caregivers with children aged 6 to 14 and are experiencing caregiving challenges
- Low income (gross household income not exceeding $4,500 per month or per capita income not exceeding $1,125 per month) and/or ComLink+ families
- Families coping with extenuating circumstances beyond those described above will be admitted on a case-by-case basis

## How to apply?
- Referral through schools, social service agencies, and government agencies
- Submission of enquiries through Morning Star Community Services' Website

## What to expect?
- Structured evening care
- The agency provide safe and nuturing environment during evening hours.
- The agency aims to strengthen parent-child through facilited bonding activities and workshops.

# MediSave Care

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/MEDISAVE_CARE*

Allows Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents with severe disability to make monthly cash withdrawals from their and/or their spouse’s MediSave Account for long-term care.

## Highlights
- Withdraw up to $200 cash per month
- Processing time will take between 6 to 8 weeks
- Apply through AIC eServices for Financing Services (eFASS)

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities
**Keywords:** Cash payouts, Long-term care, Severely disabled

## About this support
- Supports severely disabled Singapore Citizens or Permanent residents with monthly cash withdrawals to support long-term care needs
- Withdraw up to $200 per month from care recipient’s and/or their spouse's MediSave account
- [Withdrawal amounts are dependent on the care recipient and/or their spouse’s MediSave account balance](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/healthcare-financing/medisave-care-for-long-term-care-needs)

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- Aged 30 and above
- MediSave account balance of at least $5,000 for both the care recipient and their spouse
- Assessed by an MOH-accredited assessor to be unable to perform at least 3 out of the following 6 Activities of Daily Living (ADLs):
  - Washing
  - Dressing
  - Feeding
  - Toileting
  - Walking or moving around
  - Transferring

## How to apply?
You can apply:

- Online at the [AIC eServices for Financing Schemes (eFASS)](https://efinance.aic.sg/)
- Via assistance from the nursing home your loved one is staying in
- At any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)

You will need to contact an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor for a Severe Disability Assessment (SDA) as part of the application. Visit the [AIC’s website](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Severe-Disability-Assessment) for a list of assessors.

## Where to go
[Visit the AIC Link branch nearest to you](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/MediSave-Care)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg)

## Phone number
AIC hotline: [1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060)

Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.

# Migrant Domestic Worker Levy Concession

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/MDW_LEVY_CONCESSION*

Provides concessionary levy at $60 per month if there is an eligible person residing in the household.

## Highlights
- Concessionary rate of $60 per month, compared to standard levy of $300 for 1st MDW and $450 for subsequent MDWs
- Each household is eligible for one MDW levy concession per eligible person, up to two MDW levy concessions per household

**Who it targets:** Families, Persons with disabilities, Seniors
**Keywords:** Caregiving expenses, Subsidies

## About this support
- Pay a lower levy of $60 per month if you live with an eligible person
- Levy concession can only be granted for one MDW per eligible person and is capped at two levy concessions per household

## Who is this for?
If you live with any of the following eligible person who is a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident:

- Child below 16 years old
- Elderly person who is at least 67 years old
- Person with disabilities (PWD) who must be certified by Singapore-registered doctor or an approved healthcare professional to permanently require some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living (ADLs):
  - Washing
  - Dressing
  - Feeding
  - Toileting
  - Walking or moving around
  - Transferring

## How to apply?
Before hiring an MDW, you are required to obtain an approval from the [Ministry of Manpower (MOM)](https://www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/work-permit-for-foreign-domestic-worker/eligibility-and-requirements/employer-requirements) to hire an MDW.

If the eligible person is a PWD, you will also need to apply for the scheme:

- Online at the [AIC eServices for Financing Schemes (eFASS)](https://efinance.aic.sg/)

- At any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)

No application for the scheme is further needed if:

- You or your spouse is at least 67 years old
- Your child is below 16 years old

The levy concession will automatically start once you meet the eligibility criteria and complete the required steps listed on [MOM’s website](https://www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/work-permit-for-foreign-domestic-worker/foreign-domestic-worker-levy/levy-concession).

If you were not automatically granted the levy concession, you can submit a form to check why:

Form

[Check why levy concession for a child was not granted](https://go.gov.sg/check-lc-child)
Elderly or PWD
[Check why levy concession for an elderly or PWD was not granted](https://go.gov.sg/check-lc-elderly-pwd)

## Agency website
For more information that are PWD related: [View more details](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Migrant-Domestic-Worker-Levy-Concession)

For more information that are non-PWD related: [View more details](https://www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/work-permit-for-foreign-domestic-worker/foreign-domestic-worker-levy/levy-concession#who-can-qualify)

For enquiries that are non-PWD related: [Submit an enquiry](https://www.mom.gov.sg/contact-us/feedback-and-enquiries)

For enquiries that are PWD related: 
AIC Hotline: [1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060)

For enquiries that are non-PWD related: 
MOM Hotline: [6438 5122](tel:64385122)

# Interim Disability Assistance Scheme for the Elderly (IDAPE)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/IDAPE*

Provides monthly cash payout for elderly Singapore Citizens with severe disabilities who are not eligible for ElderShield.

## Highlights
- Receive $150 or $250 monthly cash payout for up to 72 months
- Processing time take between 6 to 8 weeks
- Apply through AIC’s eService for Financing Schemes (eFASS)

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors
**Keywords:** Cash assistance, PWDs, Seniors

## About this support
Supports severely disabled seniors who are not eligible for ElderShield due to age or pre-existing disabilities, with monthly cash payouts of $150 or $250 for up to 72 months.

## Who is this for?
- Born on or before 30 September 1932 or
- Born between 1 October 1932 and 30 September 1962 (both dates inclusive), with pre-existing disabilities as of 30 September 2002
- Singapore Citizen living in Singapore
- Monthly household income per person of $3,600 or less (annual value of property under $21,00 for households with no income)
- Monthly payout depends on the monthly household income per person:
  Monthly Household Income Per Person
  Payout Amount
  $0-$2,600
  $250
  $2,601 - $3,600
  $150
- Not be a [CareShield Life](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/CareShield-Life) or [ElderShield](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/ElderShield) policyholder/ supplement plan policyholder, or have made any claims before

## How to apply?
You can apply:

- Online at the [AIC eServices for Financing Schemes (eFASS)](https://efinance.aic.sg/)
- Via assistance from the nursing home your loved one is staying in
- At any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)

You will need to contact an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor for a Severe Disability Assessment (SDA) as part of the application. Visit the [AIC’s website](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Severe-Disability-Assessment) for a list of assessors.

## Where to go
[Visit the AIC Link branch nearest to you](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)

Domains: Caregiving support, Disability support, Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits

# Enabling Transport Subsidy (ETS)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/ETS*

Supports eligible Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents with disabilities who need to use dedicated transport provided by the Social Service Agencies (SSAs) to access the Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children (EIPIC), Special Education (SPED) schools, Day Activity Centres (DACs), Sheltered Workshops (SWs), Special Student Care Centres (SSCCs), Enabling Skills for Life Programme (ESLP), Enabling Business Hubs (EBHs) and Enabling Service Hubs (ESHs).

## Highlights
- Up to 80% means-tested subsidy for transport fees
- From July 2026, additional 15% subsidies for Singapore Citizens born in 1969 or earlier

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities
**Keywords:** Lower-income, PWDs, Subsidies

## About this support
Up to 80% means-tested subsidy for transport fees

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizen (SC) and Permanent Resident (PR)
- Monthly household income per capita of $4,800 and below for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents
- Annual Value (AV) of residence reflected on NRIC of $21,000 and below for households with no income
- Persons with disabilities on transport services provided by SSAs and attending Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children (EIPIC), Special Education (SPED) schools, Day Activity Centres (DACs), Sheltered Workshops (SWs), Special Student Care Centres (SSCCs), Enabling Skills for Life Programme (ESLP), Enabling Business Hubs (EBHs) and Enabling Service Hubs (ESHs).

From Jul 2026, SCs and PRs with monthly household income per capita of up to $4,800 will qualify for ETS.

## How to apply?
Apply through SPED schools or SSAs that are arranging your transportation services. They will assist in conducting a means test for you and submit the subsidy request to SG Enable on your behalf.

## Where to go
[Enabling Village](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)
[20 Lengkok Bahru](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)
[#01-01, Singapore 159053](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/transport/enabling-transport-subsidy)

## Email / Form
[contactus@sgenable.sg](mailto:contactus@sgenable.sg)

## Phone number
SG Enable Hotline: [1800-8585-885](tel:18008585885)

Domains: Caregiving support, Disability support, Financial support and benefits

# Taxi Subsidy Scheme (TSS)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/TSS*

For persons with permanent disabilities who are medically certified as unable to take public transport and totally dependent on taxi for travel to school, work or SG Enable-supported training.

## Highlights
- Up to 80% means-tested subsidy for taxi travel for the purpose of school, work or employment-related training supported by SG Enable
- From July 2026, additional 15% subsidies for Singapore Citizens born in and before 1969
- Application will be processed within 15 working days upon complete document submission 

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities
**Keywords:** Lower-income, PWDs, Subsidies

## About this support
Persons with disabilities can apply for the means-tested subsidy for taxi travel for the purpose of school, work or employment-related training supported by SG Enable. The approved subsidy percentage* applies to the total fare for each trip (which covers additional charges such as booking fees, peak period surcharges and ERP charges).

The subsidy amounts will depend on:

- Whether applicants are Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents
- Per capita monthly household income (PCHI)

* subjected to means testing and meeting eligibility criteria

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents
- Have a permanent disability based on any one of the following:
  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment
  - A visual impairment: Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye
  - Intellectual disability
  - Autism
  Proof of disability must be provided using the [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification) completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional.
- Certified as unable to take public transport and totally dependent on taxi for travel
- Currently schooling, working, or attending employment-related training supported by SG Enable
- Monthly Per Capita Household Income (PCHI) of $4,800 and below
- Annual Value (AV) of residence reflected on NRIC of $21,000 and below for households with no income
- Currently not owning any motor vehicles

From July 2026, individuals with monthly per capita household income of $3,601 to $4,800 will also qualify for TSS.

## How to apply?
For more information on the application process, please visit the [Enabling Guide](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/transport/taxi-subsidy-scheme).

## Where to go
[Enabling Village  20 Lengkok Bahru  #01-01, Singapore 159053](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/transport/taxi-subsidy-scheme)

## Email / Form
[contactus@sgenable.sg](mailto:contactus@sgenable.sg)

## Phone number
SG Enable hotline: [1800-8585-885](tel:1800-8585-885)

embedding_text:
Domains: Caregiving support, Disability support, Financial support and benefits, Housing and shelters

# Equipment Rental Scheme (ERS)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/QEAKpruj*

Subsidises the rental of essential care equipment for patients with serious illnesses.

## Highlights
- Subsidised weekly rental fees for essential medical equipment
- Covers up to two-way transport and essential consumables

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors
**Keywords:** Home healthcare, Palliative care

## About this support
The Equipment Rental Scheme (ERS) provides patients with serious illnesses who have a prognosis of less than a year with the following subsidies:

- Weekly rental fees for approved equipment such as wheelchair/pushchair, hospital bed, oxygen concentrator, pressure relief mattress and commode
- Cost of two-way transport for delivery and collection of rented equipment

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- Currently receiving care from a palliative care provider, whether home-based or in a public healthcare institution (PHI).
- Diagnosed to have a serious illness with a prognosis of less than a year.
- Assessed by a qualified assessor on the type(s) of equipment required.
- *Must not be receiving subsidies for the same or similar equipment through other Government assistance schemes.

*If you have previously received Government assistance or subsidies for same or similar type of equipment prior to your ERS application, eligibility to rent equipment(s) under ERS will be assessed on a case-by-case basis.

## How to apply?
Approach the [home palliative care provider](https://www.aic.sg/Care-Services/Home-Palliative-Care) or PHI you are receiving care from to apply for ERS.

If you are currently not under the care of any home palliative care provider or PHI, you can reach out to [Singapore Hospice Council](https://www.singaporehospice.org.sg/#contact-pop).

## Where to go
[Visit the AIC Link branch nearest to you](https://www.aic.sg/about-us/aic-link-locations/)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Equipment-Rental-Scheme)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg)

## Phone number
AIC Hotline: [1800 650 6060](tel:1800-650-6060)

Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.

Domains: Caregiving support, Disability support, Family, parenting and relationships, Healthcare and well-being

# Day Activity Centre (DAC)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-DACD*

Community-based facilities that provide care and skills training to persons with disabilities aged 18 and above to maximise their independence.

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities
**Citizenship:** SG, PR
**Keywords:** Day Care, Fees payable, Referral required

## About this support
- The DACs' programme is designed to equip persons with disabilities with daily living skills and community living skills to maximise their independence.
- The activities also aim to meaningfully occupy persons with disabilities with social and recreational activities.
- Therapeutic and behavioural intervention services may be provided at some centres.
- DACs also provide a form of respite for caregivers during the day.

## Who is this for?
Applicants should be:

- 18 years old and above*^#
- Singapore citizens or Permanent Residents^^
- Have a permanent disability based on any one of the following:
  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment
  - A visual impairment: Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye
  - A hearing impairment: Moderate hearing loss or worse in the better ear
  - Intellectual disability
  - Autism

Proof of disability must be provided using the [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)** completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional.

- Applicants should not be suffering from any untreated infectious disease.

*Students of Government and community-funded SPED schools should be encouraged to remain in school until graduation. Parents of SPED graduands may approach their School to discuss the transition plans of the children prior to graduating from School.

^Applicants who are below age 21 will need consent of parents or legal guardians for their application.

#Applicants who are aged 21 and above with no mental capacity, will need the consent of the appointed deputy(s)/donee(s) on behalf of the applicant.

^^For Permanent Residents, at least one immediate family member must be a Singapore Citizen. Immediate family members refer to spouses, parents, children or the applicant, including stepparents and stepchildren.

**From 8 September 2025, the [Disability Verification Form (DVF)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification) is the standardised proof of disability required to verify an individual’s disability status when applying for selected MSF disability schemes and services and other selected Government schemes. Applicants can check if their disability status is already verified via their Touchpoints, SupportGoWhere, or call SG Enable at [1800-8585-885](tel:1800-8585-885)

## How to apply?
- Please approach a social service professional from a touchpoint (e.g. Social Service Agency (SSA), hospitals etc.) for assistance in submitting a DAC application. If you are currently not receiving support from any social service or medical touchpoints, you may [approach SG Enable for assistance](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/child-adult-care/information-and-referral-services).
- Before meeting your Touchpoints, all applicants are encouraged to check if your disability status has already been verified by logging into [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/pwdr/apply) with your Singpass. If you do not have a verified disability status, the Touchpoint will guide you to the relevant registered healthcare professionals to assist with DVF.

**Submission of applications to SG Enable by Social Service Professional (Online or Hardcopy)**

**Step 1:**

All applicants should check if they have a verified disability status by logging into [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/pwdr/apply) with their Singpass. If the applicant already has a verified disability status, a DVF is not required.

**Step 2:**

If the applicant does not have a verified disability status or has a new disability condition which has not been verified previously, registered Touchpoint Assessor/Admin must submit a copy of the DVF completed by a relevant registered Healthcare Professional together with the AD application.

**Step 3:**

Registered touchpoints’ Assessor/Admin may submit clients’ AD application and completed DVF online via CorpPass (recommended) or via hardcopy.

1. **Online submission (Recommended)**
  Log into e-Services using your CorpPass
2. **Hardcopy submission**
  Download the [AD application form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/ad-application-form.pdf?sfvrsn=71d5f444_3), print and send together with the required documents. If required, you may download sections of the AD application form and DVF below for use:
  - [Client Assessment Form (Revised)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/final-caf-r-form.pdf?sfvrsn=c2d096c3_1)
  - [Medical Information Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/final-interim-medical-information.pdf?sfvrsn=c4f804d4_1)
  - [Declaration Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/declaration-form.pdf?sfvrsn=a7fa3568_2)
  - [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)

## What to expect?
- SG Enable will contact you within 10 working days upon receiving the completed application together with the required supporting documents from the touchpoint. SG Enable will also update the social worker who assisted in the application on the status of the application.
- Acceptance into the programme at the preferred centre is subject to the availability of vacancies and approval of the centre management.

title: Community Mental Health Services
description: Community mental health teams located across Singapore provide support and access to mental health care for those in need.
embedding_text:
Domains: Active Ageing, Caregiving, Caregiving support, Counselling and crisis support, Disability support, Mental health

# Community Mental Health Services

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/oWweAQMH*

Community mental health teams located across Singapore provide support and access to mental health care for those in need.

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Counselling, Intervention and Therapy, Social-emotional Support

## About this support
Mental health support services are offered by over 100 community mental health teams islandwide, with at least 1 team in every neighbourhood. These teams serve as the first stop for in-person mental health support.

## Who is this for?
Anyone aged 12 and above, and in need of mental health support.

## How to apply?
- Visit the [AIC’s website](https://www.aic.sg/Care-Services/Community-Mental-Health-Services) to search for service providers by** **postal code, address or your device’s current location.
- Contact the team directly for an appointment.

For further assistance, you can contact AIC via the hotline[1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060) or [submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg).

- Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines in Singapore.
- Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.

## What to expect?
- Every visit is strictly confidential.
- Trained care professionals in each team will help identify your needs, develop a personalised care plan and provide support such as counselling and therapy.
- They can also help to escalate and make necessary referrals if needed.

Acceptance of mental capacity assessment reports from SPED Schools, DACs, SWs, or the MSF-appointed ADAP Agency
embedding_text:
Domains: Caregiving support, Disability support

# Assisted Deputyship Application Programme (ADAP) 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/ddXZpncg*

ADAP supports caregivers of children without mental capacity to apply to be court-appointed deputies, through the simplified deputyship process. As a deputy, the caregiver can make legal decisions for the child when he/she turns 21.

## Highlights
- Guidance provided for simplified deputyship applications for caregivers of persons with disabilities and without mental capacity
- Acceptance of mental capacity assessment reports from SPED Schools, DACs, SWs, or the MSF-appointed ADAP Agency

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities
**Keywords:** Caregiver support, Referral required, Special needs

## About this support
- Programme provides guidance/facilitation, for caregivers of persons with no mental capacity to manage their own matters in adulthood, to apply to Family Justice Courts to be appointed as legal deputies for their child. This is a simplified process that is also more affordable, compared to application for deputyship under standard route.
- Courts may accept mental capacity assessment reports prepared by psychologists from Special Education Schools (SPED Schools), selected Day Activity Centres (DACs), Sheltered Workshops (SWs), or the MSF-appointed ADAP Agency in lieu of a medical report. This applies only when the child is enrolled in a SPED school, DAC, or SW that is onboard the ADAP programme. In all other cases, the mental capacity assessment must be conducted by a medical capacity assessment must be conducted by a medical doctor or psychiatrist.

## Who is this for?
- Your child is:
  - between 18 and 21 years old as well as in the graduating cohort in a Special Education (SPED) school; or
  - above 18 years old and enrolled in an MSF-funded Day Activity Centre (DAC) or Sheltered Workshop (SW).
- You agree to use the standard list of powers/orders available under the Integrated Family Application Management System (iFAMS) when filing a simplified Deputyship application.
- All family members and any other caregivers agree for you to make the application (i.e. it is an uncontested case).

## How to apply?
Caregivers can approach the relevant staff in the SPED school, Day Activity Centre or Sheltered Workshop to indicate interest to apply for Deputyship. The school or centre will work with an MSF-appointed ADAP Agency to guide the parent/caregiver in their Deputyship application.

For Caregivers whose child with disability is not enrolled in a service, please contact ADAP Agency directly via phone or email for enquiries on deputyship application.

## Where to go
MINDS
Caregivers Support Services Centre

[11 Jalan Ubi Kembangan-chai Chee Community Hub 409074](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=409074)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/child-adult-care/assisted-deputyship-application-programme-(adap))

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](mailto:fcp@minds.org.sg)

Referral is required for application.

## Phone number
ADAP Agency Hotline: 6547 8503

sections.About this support:
- Programme provides guidance/facilitation, for caregivers of persons with no mental capacity to manage their own matters in adulthood, to apply to Family Justice Courts to be appointed as legal deputies for their child. This is a simplified process that is also more affordable, compared to application for deputyship under standard route.
- Courts may accept mental capacity assessment reports prepared by psychologists from Special Education Schools (SPED Schools), selected Day Activity Centres (DACs), Sheltered Workshops (SWs), or the MSF-appointed ADAP Agency in lieu of a medical report. This applies only when the child is enrolled in a SPED school, DAC, or SW that is onboard the ADAP programme. In all other cases, the mental capacity assessment must be conducted by a medical capacity assessment must be conducted by a medical doctor or psychiatrist.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Your child is:
  - between 18 and 21 years old as well as in the graduating cohort in a Special Education (SPED) school; or
  - above 18 years old and enrolled in an MSF-funded Day Activity Centre (DAC) or Sheltered Workshop (SW).
- You agree to use the standard list of powers/orders available under the Integrated Family Application Management System (iFAMS) when filing a simplified Deputyship application.
- All family members and any other caregivers agree for you to make the application (i.e. it is an uncontested case).
sections.How to apply?:
Caregivers can approach the relevant staff in the SPED school, Day Activity Centre or Sheltered Workshop to indicate interest to apply for Deputyship. The school or centre will work with an MSF-appointed ADAP Agency to guide the parent/caregiver in their Deputyship application.

For Caregivers whose child with disability is not enrolled in a service, please contact ADAP Agency directly via phone or email for enquiries on deputyship application.

# Dementia Day Care

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-DDC*

Mind stimulating activities, exercises and personal care at day care centres for seniors with dementia.

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Day Care, Referral required, Subsidies

## About this support
Services at day care centres help seniors with mild to advanced dementia continue living in the community and delay the need for institutionalisation. They include:

- Group and individual activities to slow down deterioration of physical and mental functions (based on their abilities)
- Individualised care plans for seniors with suitable maintenance exercises
- Assistance with daily personal care
- Caregiver support activities (e.g. support groups, talks and care demonstrations, etc)
- Offered on weekdays, but some centres also provide weekend support

## Who is this for?
Senior diagnosed with mild to advanced dementia, and/or require supervision during the day while their caregivers are at work.

## How to apply?
You can apply:

- Through the hospital, polyclinic or GP who is familiar with your loved one’s condition and needs
- At any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)

If you are interested to view the list of service providers, visit the [AIC’s website](https://aic.sg/Care-Services/Day-Care).

For further assistance, you can contact AIC via the hotline[1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060) or [submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg).

- Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines in Singapore.
- Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.

## What to expect?
Subsidies are available depending on the [means-test](https://aic.sg/care-services/home-medical#faq) result.

- Only applicable to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents

embedding_text:

# Inpatient Hospice Palliative Care Service (IHPCS)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-IHPCS*

Supports end-of-life patients who cannot be cared for at home and require inpatient care.

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Palliative care, Referral required

## About this support
Provides medical and emotional support for end-of-life patients who cannot be cared for at home and their caregivers, including services provided by specialised care teams such as:

- Specialist palliative care focusing on the management of symptoms such as pain, breathlessness, nausea and vomiting
- Emotional, spiritual and grief support and counselling
- Palliative rehabilitation, including physiotherapy and occupational therapy
- Music and art therapy

## Who is this for?
- Patient with a prognosis of less than 3 months who needs:
  - Specialised care especially in the last phase of life, when care at home, in a nursing home or outpatient setting is not possible.

- Patient with a prognosis of less than 12 months who requires:
  - Time-limited care up to 28 calendar days for severe symptoms that cannot be managed in outpatient settings

## How to apply?
You can apply:

- Through the hospital, polyclinic or GP who is familiar with your loved one’s condition and needs
- At any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)

If you are interested to view the list of service providers, visit the [AIC’s website](https://aic.sg/Care-Services/Inpatient-Hospice-Palliative-Care-Services) .

For further assistance, you can contact AIC via the hotline[1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060) or [submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg).

- Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines in Singapore.
- Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.

## What to expect?
- Subsidies are available depending on the [means-test](https://aic.sg/care-services/home-medical#faq) result.
  - Only applicable to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents
- MediShield Life and MediSave can be used to cover costs.
- If patients need further financial assistance, their respective service providers will be able to provide more information.

# Day Hospice Care

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-PDC*

A safe and supportive environment during the day for patients with life-limiting illnesses and their caregivers.

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Caregiver support, Referral required

## About this support
Provides specialised care and holistic support at centres during the day for patients and their caregivers, aimed at improving the patients’ quality of life. Services include, but are not limited to:

- Palliative care with medical and nursing support

- Patients who have been diagnosed by a doctor to have a life-limiting illness and a prognosis of less than 1 year

# Nursing Home

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-NH*

A long-term residential care facility for seniors who have limited or no caregiver support and require assistance with daily nursing and living needs.

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Caregiver support, Referral required

## About this support
Provides round-the-clock nursing and care services, including:

- Help with daily living activities such as going to the toilet, showering, eating, etc
- Nursing support such as management of nasogastric tube, urine catheter, wound dressing, etc
- Physical and social activities such as maintenance exercises, outings, etc

For selected nursing homes with dementia and/or psychiatric facilities, services include:

- Programmes and activities for cognitive stimulation to slow down the deterioration of the senior’s physical and mental functions

## Who is this for?
- Senior who has a physical or mental disability because of illness
- Unable to be cared for at home by family or paid domestic worker, and has tried all other care options such as using day care, home medical, home nursing services, etc

## How to apply?
You can apply:

- Through the hospital, polyclinic or medical social worker who is familiar with your loved one’s condition and needs
- At any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)

If you are interested to view the list of providers, visit the [AIC’s website](https://www.aic.sg/Care-Services/Nursing-Home).

For further assistance, you can contact AIC via the hotline[1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060) or [submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg).

- Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines in Singapore.
- Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.

## What to expect?
- Subsidies are available depending on the [means-test](https://aic.sg/Care-Services/nursing-home#faq) result.
  - Only applicable to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents
  - Additional fees such as deposits and other charges may apply.

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-CRC*

**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-MDCC*

**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS

# Service and Conservancy Charges (S&CC) Rebate

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/SCCR*

Quarterly rebates to offset S&CC fees for HDB households. Eligible households will receive 1.5 to 3.5 months of the GST Voucher (GSTV) – S&CC Rebate.

## Highlights
- 1.5 to 3.5 months of S&CC Rebate in each Financial Year
- Rebates will be given out in January, April, July and October
- No application needed

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Budget 2024, HDB households, Rebates

## About this support
- Offsets between 1.5 and 3.5 months of S&CC
- Eligible households will receive their S&CC rebates in January, April, July, and October

## Who is this for?
A HDB household will be eligible for the S&CC rebate if all the criteria below are fulfilled:

- There must be at least one Singapore Citizen flat owner or occupier in the flat
- The flat owner(s) and essential occupier(s) of the flat do not own or have any interest in a private property
- The flat owner(s) have not rented out the whole flat

## How to apply?
- No application required
- S&CC rebates will be credited directly to your household's S&CC account managed by your respective Town Council

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.govbenefits.gov.sg/)

## Email / Form
HDB residents can check or enquire about their household's eligibility for GSTV – S&CC Rebate using these e-Services for [purchased flats](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/AG10AWScRebate/AG10SRebatesMain) and [rental flats](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/AG10AWScRebate/AG10SRentalRebatesMain).

Domains: Caregiving support

# Caregiver Training and Support Programme

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-CTCP*

Provides training and support to caregivers of persons with mental health conditions so that they can better cope with their caregiving duties.

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, PR
**Keywords:** Caregiver support, Free

## About this support
CTSP consists of the Caregivers-to-Caregivers (C2C) Programme and Engagement-to-Empowerment (E2E) Programme. C2C aims to provide caregivers with the knowledge and skills regarding caregiving so that they can better cope with their caregiving duties.

C2C provides various types of training courses that range from 8 to 12 sessions and in 3 different languages, to cover general or specific mental health conditions. Through the C2C training courses, caregiver leaders are also identified and trained to volunteer as caregiver leaders to support other caregivers in subsequent C2C classes and /or outreach and advocacy work.

E2E consists of the following components:

- Caregiver-for-Caregiver (C4C) Support Programme: 12 support group sessions over a year, with the aim of increasing support networks for caregivers. The first six sessions will be held in-person and will aim to provide support and equip caregivers with coping skills. Subsequent sessions may be a mix of online or in-person sessions, including self-run activities by caregivers with support from Mindfull Community Limited staff, to gather fellow caregivers for social activities or a sharing session.
- Train-the-Trainer (TTT): Caregivers who indicated interest to contribute and identified by staff as having potential are coached and trained as Volunteer Trainers and/or to support advocacy and outreach work through “Train-the-Trainer” modules so they can volunteer to support CAL’s programmes and activities.

## Who is this for?
- Caregivers of Persons with Mental Health Issues (PMHIs).
- This can range from spouses, partners, parents, siblings, grandchildren, friends, neighbours, etc of someone who is experiencing a mental health condition.

## How to apply?
Register online through the [form](https://forms.office.com/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=mH6MQ8-ncE-ro_WXOpzXWwTicfzzzZ1Jqtl-rNfRemJUMEpJWUo4NFFQVjZMWDE4NEs3N1hPWTBHNiQlQCN0PWcu&route=shorturl).

## What to expect?
After registration, interested participants will receive a call and email from Mindfull Community Limited to confirm their registration.[form](https://forms.office.com/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=mH6MQ8-ncE-ro_WXOpzXWwTicfzzzZ1Jqtl-rNfRemJUMEpJWUo4NFFQVjZMWDE4NEs3N1hPWTBHNiQlQCN0PWcu&route=shorturl)

Domains: Caregiving support, Counselling and crisis support, Education and learning, Family, parenting and relationships, Mental health

# SAMH Youthreach

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-SY*

Provides psychosocial support and recovery programmes for youths aged 13 to 21 with emotional, psychological and psychiatric issues in the community.

**Who it targets:** Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, PR
**Keywords:** Counselling, Free, Referral required

## About this support
The programme staff work with youths and their families to minimise risk, promote safety and improve functioning.

Services include:

- Counselling Case Management
- Family Psychoeducation Programme
- Expressive Therapies
- Psycho-social Activities

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents aged 13 to 21 with emotional, psychological and/or psychiatric issues.
- No recent history of violent behaviour, alcohol or substance abuse, or sexual acting out behaviour.
- Willing to participate in the centre's activities.
- Family is willing to participate in case management and family education programmes.

## How to apply?
Referral by a psychiatrist, school counsellor, or social worker using the SAMH referral form is required.

## What to expect?
- An intake interview with child/youth and caregiver will be arranged to assess suitability.
- Upon successful registration, the child/youth and caregiver will be engaged for services including case management, psychoeducation and psychosocial development programmes.

description: A legal document that allows you (the 'Donor') to appoint one or more trusted persons (the 'Donee') to  make decisions on your behalf in the event you lose mental capacity.
embedding_text:
Domains: Caregiving, Caregiving support, Legacy planning, Retirement and legacy planning

# Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-LPA*

A legal document that allows you (the 'Donor') to appoint one or more trusted persons (the 'Donee') to  make decisions on your behalf in the event you lose mental capacity.

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Advance Care Planning, Fees payable

## About this support
An LPA allows you to appoint trusted individuals to make decisions on (i) personal welfare and (ii) property and affairs, on your behalf in the event you lose mental capacity.

## Who is this for?
Donors must:

- Be 21 years old and above
- Have the mental capacity to make your own decisions
- Not be an undischarged bankrupt if you wish to make an LPA for property and affairs matters

Donees must:

- Be 21 years old and above
- Be your spouse or partner, family member or relative, friend, or a licensed trust company for property and affair matters only
- Have the mental capacity to make their own decisions

## How to apply?
You can:

- [Apply online](https://opg-eservice.msf.gov.sg/) or
- You may also [book an appointment](https://www.booking.gov.sg/public/services/G4x7rneZ/list) or visit a [ServiceSG Centre](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/find-a-service/life-planning-service/) today for in-person guidance and assistance
  for your application. Please note that a [LPA certificate issuer](https://book.health.gov.sg/lpa) is required to ensure that the donor has the mental capacity to make a LPA.

## What to expect?
Here are the steps on how to make an LPA:

- Step 1: Decide on the type of LPA form
  - LPA Form 1 grants general powers to Donee(s) who will make decisions on your behalf when you lose mental capacity
  - LPA Form 2 is for applicants who want to appoint more than 2 Donees and/or more than 1 replacement Donee, and grant specific or customised powers that are not in the scope of LPA Form 1. You will need to engage a lawyer for LPA Form 2.
- Step 2: [Find an LPA certificate issuer ](https://book.health.gov.sg/lpa)who is:
  - A medical professional accredited by the OPG
  - A registered psychiatrist
  - A practising lawyer (excluding lawyers registered under section 36E of the Legal Profession Act 1966)
- You and the LPA certificate issuer must digitally sign the LPA using the Singpass app. Your Donees can sign electronically by accepting their appointment.
- For your LPA to be legally valid, the certificate issuer must submit the LPA application to Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) via OPG Online (OPGO), as authorised by you.

# Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/SNSS*

Enables parents to set aside CPF savings for the long-term care of children with special needs.

## Highlights
- Parents may nominate child to receive payouts from their CPF savings after they pass on
- Minimum monthly payout is $250, parents may decide on a higher amount
- Submit the application and supporting documents to SNTC via email or mail

**Who it targets:** Families, Persons with disabilities
**Keywords:** CPF payouts, Parents, Special needs

## About this support
- Parents may nominate child with special needs to receive payouts from their CPF savings after death with minimum monthly payout of $250.
- If the nominating parent’s CPF savings upon his/her demise is insufficient to support a year’s worth of payout (e.g. a minimum monthly payout is S$250 x 12 months = S$3,000), the CPF savings will be disbursed as a lump sum to the nominee with special needs.

## Who is this for?
The nominating applicant should be:

- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- The parent or an appointed legal guardian of the child with special needs

The child with special needs should:

- Have a permanent disability based on any one of the following:
  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment
  - A visual impairment: Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye
  - A hearing impairment: Moderate hearing loss or worse in the better ear
  - Intellectual disability
  - Autism

Proof of disability must be provided using the [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification) completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional.

**Or**

- is attending or had attended a Special Education School

The 6 ADLs are:

- Eating
- Bathing
- Dressing
- Transferring
- Toileting
- Walking or moving around

## How to apply?
Before proceeding, all applicants are encouraged to check if your child’s disability status has already been verified.

Find out more here: https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification

You can apply by submitting the completed [application form](https://www.sgenable.sg/snss) and supporting documents:

- via mail to Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS), Future Care Planning Resource Centre by SG Enable, 22 Lengkok Bahru, Vista, Enabling Village #03-03  Singapore 159824
- via email to [futurecareplanning@sgenable.sg](mailto:futurecareplanning@sgenable.sg).

You'll need to provide copies of:

- Nominating applicant's and child's NRIC
- Child's Birth Certificate

If your child's disability status has not been verified:

- Supporting document from the SPED school issued on the school’s official letterhead stating that the Person with Special Needs (PSN) is currently attending or has previously attended the SPED school or
- [Disability Verification Form (DVF) ](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)completed by a Registered Healthcare Professional*

After mailing the application and upon approval by MSF, parents will receive an eligibility letter, which they should bring to the CPF Board to make the SNSS nomination.

*Please note that a submitted Disability Verification Form (DVF) does not mean that your child’s disability status has been verified.

## Where to go
[22 Lengkok Bahru 159824](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159824)

Future Care Planning Resource Centre by SG Enable,

Enabling Village #03-03

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.sntc.org.sg/services/special-needs-savings-scheme-(snss))

## Email / Form
[futurecareplanning@sgenable.sg](mailto:futurecareplanning@sgenable.sg)

## Phone number
Special Needs Savings Scheme Hotline:

[6278 9598](tel:62789598)

(Operating hours: 9am-6pm on weekdays, closed on weekends and public holidays)

# CAREwell

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/izIXWd7S*

CAREwell is a program that supports caregivers in their caregiving role, emotional and mental wellness, decision- making regarding services, and care management.

## Highlights
- Each family is guided by a transdisciplinary CAREwell Key Worker.
- CAREwell Key Workers meet with caregiver for needs analysis and establish family support plan.

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities
**Keywords:** Caregiver support

## About this support
CAREwell offers tailored support to caregivers through a combination of approaches:

1. Trauma-informed emotional support and mental health advisory for caregivers
2. Professional support on service navigation, care coordination, and service integration for meeting dependent and family’s social and health needs.

Each family is paired with a Keyworker, a trained professional in social work, healthcare, special needs, or related fields. The Keyworker will work with the caregiver to assess needs and identify challenges, establish a family support plan, and implement strategies to support both the caregiver and their dependent.

## Who is this for?
CAREwell program is a highly subsidised program made affordable to all caregivers of persons with special needs.

Interested caregivers are encouraged to get in touch with us to find out the eligible subsidies available to them.

## How to apply?
Interested caregivers or external agency can click on the request link for CAREwell. For caregivers, you will receive an email with a link to ‘CSG Caregiver Needs Form’. Fill in the form and our team will contact you shortly.

Applicants to CAREwell are screened for suitability before being enrolled into the programme.

## Where to go
[20 Lengkok Bahru 159053](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)
#03-06/07 Block Vista

## Agency website
https://caring.sg/carewell

## Email / Form
[https://www.caring.sg/contact-us](https://www.caring.sg/contact-us/)

# CAREconnect

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/bncVrBSn*

CAREconnect offers inclusive social events for family bonding and connection to fellow caregivers and volunteers, through mobilising support groups, organising inclusive, social, and/or respite events, and webinars.

## Highlights
- CAREconnect goes beyond just offering services. It’s a community movement because it aims to build a network of support for caregivers within their local neighborhoods.
- CAREconnect conducts inclusive events for caregivers. 92% of caregivers agreed that the events helped them to feel more included in their neighbourhood.
- The monthly webinars focus on a variety of topics and resources that would help caregivers make informed decisions and provide some answers to questions and difficulties they may have. 82% of caregivers at CAREconnect Webinars agreed that the sessions were helpful in learning to care for their child better.

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities
**Keywords:** Caregiver support

## About this support
CAREconnect offers a variety of events to cater to different needs and preferences:

- Informative Webinars: CAREconnect offers online webinars that provide valuable caregiving resources and information, accessible from the comfort of home.
- Engaging Physical Events: CAREconnect organizes face-to-face events, in collaboration with volunteers and grassroots organizations, offering caregivers the opportunity to connect, share experiences, and receive emotional support.

By offering both online and in-person events, along with strong community ties through volunteers and grassroots organizations, CAREconnect builds an inclusive and accessible support system for caregivers.

Beyond just offering services, CAREconnect is a community movement focused on creating a support network for caregivers within their local neighborhoods. Partnership with grassroots enhances CAREconnect’s ability to reach a broader audience and address the unique challenges caregivers face.

## Who is this for?
Caregivers of persons with special needs.

## How to apply?
Click CaringSG event link to view available events. Registration information can be found at each individual event page.

[20 Lengkok Bahru 159053](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)

Domains: Caregiving, Caregiving support, Disability support, Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits, Healthcare and well-being

# Home Caregiving Grant (HCG)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/HCG*

Provides financial support to help with caregiving expenses for households caring for persons with moderate to severe disabilities.

## Highlights
- Payouts of $200, $400 or $600 per month
- Processing time takes up to 4 weeks
- Apply through AIC’s eService portal (eFASS)

**Who it targets:** Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors
**Keywords:** Caregiving expenses, Cash assistance, PWDs

## About this support
Monthly cash payout of $200, $400 or $600

## Who is this for?
Care recipient must meet the following criteria:

- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident with a parent, child or spouse who is a Singapore Citizen
- Lives in Singapore
- Always requires some assistance on a permanent basis with at least 3 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living (ADLs)
- Monthly per capita household income of less than or equal to $4,800 or less  (or property annual value of $21,000 or below for households with no income)
- Those with multiple properties will receive the lowest HCG payout of $200 per month
- [Not in a residential long-term care institution](https://www.aic.sg/financial-assistance/home-caregiving-grant#q5a)

The 6 ADLs are:

- Eating
- Bathing
- Dressing
- Transferring
- Toileting
- Walking or moving around

## How to apply?
You can apply:

- Online at the [AIC eService Portal](https://efinance.aic.sg/)
- At any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us)

You'll need to provide:

- [Completed Functional Assessment Report](https://edge.sitecorecloud.io/agencyforinb6cc-agencyforin73f5-production08ac-d178/media/agency-for-integrated-care/Files/Financial-Assistance/Functional-Assessment-Report.pdf) from your General Practitioner, a registered Nurse or a registered Physio/Occupational Therapist
- NRIC details
- Bank details

## Where to go
[Contact Us | AIC](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.aic.sg/financial-assistance/home-caregiving-grant)

## Email / Form
[Contact Us | AIC](https://www.aic.sg/contact-us)

## Phone number
AIC Hotline: [1800 650 6060](tel:1800-650-6060)

# Enhancement for Active Seniors (EASE)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/EASE*

Subsidy for Singapore Citizen households with at least one senior who meets age criterion and needs help to install senior-friendly fittings.

## Highlights
- Up to 95% subsidy of improvement costs
- Respond within 14 working days upon receipt of application
- Apply via EASE e-Service or Mobile@HDB

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors
**Keywords:** Seniors, Subsidies

## About this support
- Depending on your flat type, the subsidy can cover up to 95% of the total improvement cost.
- ['Calculate Calculate Cost of HIP/ EASE Improvement Items' e-Service](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/DJ02AWFNCALV7/Main)
  - Choose ‘EASE (Direct Application)’ under the selection type, indicate your flat type and the EASE improvements you wish to have.
- If you are a senior living in a rental flat, your preferred EASE improvement items will be fully funded by the Government.

## Who is this for?
Singapore Citizen household with a senior who is aged:

- 65 and above; or
- Between 60 and 64, and requires assistance for one or more of the Activities of Daily Living (ADLs):
  - Eating
  - Bathing
  - Dressing
  - Transferring
  - Toileting
  - Walking or moving around

## How to apply?
You can apply:

- [Apply for Enhancement for Active Seniors (EASE) Online via EASE](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/BN37AWEASE/BN37PMain.jsp)
- Mobile@HDB

You are required to submit a [Functional Assessment Report](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/-/media/managing-my-home/upgrading-and-redevelopment/enhancement-for-active-seniors-ease/FAR-Sep-2025.pdf) if you are a Singapore Citizen flat owner with at least one member in the household aged between 60 and 64 who requires assistance for one or more of the Activities of Daily Living (ADL)

- The Functional Assessment Report for the elderly aged between 60 and 64 must be endorsed by a qualified assessor such as a Singapore Medical Council fully registered doctor, and must be submitted together with your application form

## Where to go
[Book an appointment via e-Appointment service](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/BF13AWAppointmentWeb/branch/)

[View more details](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/upgrading-and-redevelopment/enhancement-for-active-seniors-ease)
