title: Live On!
description: Year-long, family-centric psychological intervention for youths with high suicide risk as they transit from hospitalisation into the community.
embedding_text:
Domains: Counselling and crisis support, Family, parenting and relationships, Mental health

# Live On!

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-LOBTCS*

Year-long, family-centric psychological intervention for youths with high suicide risk as they transit from hospitalisation into the community.

**Who it targets:** Families, Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, PR
**Keywords:** Free, Referral required, Suicide Intervention

## About this support
- LiveOn! is a 1-year high frequency and intensive suicide intervention programme that targets youths aged 12 to 18 years old with suicidality risk, and includes their family members in the intervention.
- Objectives of the programme includes:
  - Providing immediate support to youths with suicidal thoughts or attempts in the community
  - Providing continuous community support for youths and the families once they are discharged from primary care institutions
  - De-escalating youths' emotions and strengthening family support through individual and family counselling

## Who is this for?
- 12 to 18 years old youths who have been discharged from IMH due to suicidality.

## How to apply?
- This programme is only eligible for youths who have been discharged by IMH, KKH, NUH, and other public hospitals due to suicidality, and have been assessed by a clinician to be eligible for referral.
- Call the TOUCHline (1800 377 2252, 9am to 6pm from Monday to Friday) or email [mentalhealth@touch.org.sg](mailto:mentalhealth@touch.org.sg) if you do not have a hospital referral but still require support.
- If you are suicidal and require immediate support, call Samaritans of Singapore (SOS) at 1767.

## What to expect?
This programme consists of individual counselling for the youths, as well as family sessions.

**Individual sessions (for the youth)**

- In the Acute phase, the youth will meet with the social worker / counsellor / psychologist weekly for 6 to 12 sessions to de-escalate emotions.
- In the Continuation phase, the youth will meet with the social worker / counsellor / psychologist twice a month, for another 5 to 12 sessions.
- In the Maintenance phase after the above is completed, the youth will remain in contact with the caseworker through calls and text messages for 3 to 6 months for continuous support and monitoring . If youths relapse, an assessment will be conducted and the case will be re-opened.

**Family sessions (for the caregivers of the youth)**

- Meet with the social worker / counsellor twice a month from the start of the programme for 4 to 6 sessions to learn skills on how to support the youth better, which includes safety planning and crisis management School counsellors will also be contacted, with client and parental consent.

# Safe Place

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/a0ctwtOS*

Programme aims to empower women and their families with unsupported pregnancies to make informed and life-giving choices.

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Free

## About this support
The programme provides the following services:

- Case management and counselling
- Pre- and postnatal skills equipping
- Baby essentials
- Temporary accommodation
- Referrals to other support partners

## Who is this for?
Safe Place serves pregnant women up to 32 weeks gestation who consent to receiving support services. For clients under 17 years, parental consent is required, although exceptions are considered based on individual circumstances.

## How to apply?
If you are a pregnant woman who needs help, know of one who needs help or need information about unsupported pregnancy, please contact Safe Place at 6817 4202 or text via WhatsApp at 8891 4214 to speak to the caseworkers.

For community partners, please submit a referral form and attach a social report (if available) via email ([safeplace@lakeside.org.sg](mailto:safeplace@lakeside.org.sg)).

A social worker will be in touch within 3 working days.

## What to expect?
Service users who require help with their pregnancy may contact Safe Place via email/call/WhatsApp.

Case plans and duration of case are customised to meet the unique needs and circumstances of the service users.

title: Sober Living Framework (SLF)
description: Provides crisis intervention, therapy support, and long-term aftercare for persons and families impacted by substance and/or behavioural addictions.
embedding_text:
Domains: Counselling and crisis support, Family, parenting and relationships, Mental health

# Sober Living Framework (SLF)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-SLFS*

Provides crisis intervention, therapy support, and long-term aftercare for persons and families impacted by substance and/or behavioural addictions.

**Who it targets:** Families, Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Addiction, Fees payable

## About this support
The SLF comprises intervention tracks for addicted persons or Significant Other Persons (SOP; includes kin and family members, partner, close friends, guardian) at 5 different stages of needs:

- Track 1: Outreach, Education and Awareness – to raise awareness of addictions and advocate for early intervention
- Track 2: Relapse Prevention and Extended Care – individual and group counselling, family support, self-help support group
- Track 3: Sober Living – for persons in the early remission phase with less than 6 months sobriety from addictive behaviour
- Track 4: Maintenance – for persons with at least 6 months sobriety
- Track 5: For Family/SOP – individual and group counselling, support group

Note: Not all participants will enter and complete each track in a linear order.

## Who is this for?
All services are open to Singapore Citizens and persons residing in Singapore who are:

- Assessed to have a present or past addiction issue (including drugs, alcohol, compulsive gambling, shoplifting, sex, porn use and gaming), with the expressed desire to seek help or,
- Currently impacted by the addiction of a loved one.

For addiction treatment:

- Services are provided to all persons aged 14 and above

For family counselling:

- Support is provided to individuals aged 10 and above

For outreach programmes:

- Conducted for individuals aged 14 and above

Those who are under the age of 16 must be accompanied by a parent, guardian or authorised adult.

## How to apply?
You may contact WE CARE for more information. Alternatively, WE CARE also accepts referrals through other agencies (e.g. State Courts, MSF, Prisons, family service centres, hospitals, other social service agencies).

## What to expect?
The intake and assessment process involves an interview where the person’s motivation is assessed and their readiness, reasons and desire for change are explored.

- For persons who are assessed to be ambivalent about stopping their addictive behaviour, brief therapy will be conducted, with the primary goal of engaging with the person such that they will return for help in the future when ready for change.
- For persons who are assessed to be highly motivated for change, they will be recommended to seek medical detoxification (if necessary), or directly assigned to the relevant track.

embedding_text:
Domains: Counselling and crisis support, Family, parenting and relationships

# Maintenance Support Central (MSC)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-MSCM*

Provides support and assistance for clients who have difficulty in receiving spousal and/or child maintenance.

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Free

## About this support
MSC empowers individuals by providing knowledge of their marital and maintenance rights while offering comprehensive support in collaboration with community partners.

1.      Maintenance Applications

- Assists in the filing of Fresh Maintenance Applications (FMO) via the Integrated Family Application Management System (iFAMS)
- Assists in the Enforcement of Maintenance Orders (EMO) through video-link filing (iFAMS)
- Appointments must be made in advance

2.      Legal Clinics

- Offers Civil Family Law legal clinic on the first and third Monday evenings of each month
- Offers Syariah Family Law legal clinic on the third Monday of each month
- Legal clinics are open to individuals residing in Singapore, with an income cap criteria

3.      Court Process Guidance

- Offers legal guidance which includes explanation of standard legal procedures and legal terms related to family law

4.      Counselling Services

- Provides face-to-face and phone counselling for individuals who require emotional support for marital issues, post-divorce/separations, parenthood struggles, and/or similar concerns
- Counselling services are chargeable, based on clients’ financial capabilities

5.      Educational Talks

- Legal talks on family law matters designed to benefit the public, social service professionals, and community partners. These sessions aim to raise awareness, enhance understanding, and equip participants with practical knowledge to navigate legal challenges effectively.
- Talks are conducted by guest speakers who are experts in Family and Syariah law

MSC also assists in responding to enquiries by sharing information or referring them to other community partners.

## Who is this for?
- Services are rendered to individuals residing in Singapore who face financial abuse, marital issues, or have a Singapore court order and require legal support to navigate family law matters.
- This includes individuals who are dealing with unpaid maintenance, divorce proceedings, and financial difficulties arising from marital conflicts.

## How to apply?
- You may apply to file Fresh or Enforcement of Maintenance application online (https://ifams.gov.sg/sop/#iFAMS). Alternatively, you may also contact the MSC programme's hotline at 6837 0611 to make an appointment.
- You can register for the online legal clinic (https://forms.office.com/r/4JucwmuQfc). If you qualify, programme staff will get back to you by 3 working days on the details.
- You may register for counselling service online (https://forms.office.com/r/mvdxTJcBFF) or call the hotline at 6571 0185 / 6837 0611 (WhatsApp)

## What to expect?
Service users who require the programme’s services will need to complete a registration form. Staff will confirm the appointments with the service user within 3 to 5 working days of form submission. For clients who register for legal clinic or counselling service, the processing time is 3 working days. All other services can be arranged at the time of contact.

embedding_text:
Domains: Counselling and crisis support, Healthcare and well-being, Mental health

# Addiction Support Programme for Inclusion, Recovery, and Empowerment (ASPIRE)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/54sFPLUr*

For individuals aged 10 and above who have a present or past addiction issue (including gaming, compulsive gambling, shoplifting, drugs, alcohol, sex and porn use) or are currently impacted by the addiction of a loved one.

**Who it targets:** Families, Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, OTHERS, PR
**Keywords:** Addiction, Counselling

## About this support
Addiction Support Programme for Inclusion, Recovery and Empowerment (ASPIRE) provides screening, intake, assessment, and intervention, for persons and families impacted by addictions, particularly behavioural addictions. It provides professional community therapeutic services that contributes to the community integration of persons and families affected by addictions.

## Who is this for?
Singapore citizens and persons residing in Singapore who are:

1. assessed to have a present or past addiction issue (including gaming, compulsive gambling, shoplifting, drugs, alcohol, sex and porn use), with the expressed desire to seek help OR
2. currently impacted by the addiction of a loved one.

## How to apply?
You may call, walk-in, or email our various agencies for requests on counselling. You may also be referred from other organisations and services. Information about the Addiction Support Service is available via the agencies’ website and brochures.

## What to expect?
Individuals who seek help can expect in-person and virtual counselling. These can take place via individual sessions, family sessions or group sessions. If referred, individuals are screened for service eligibility within 3 weeks after case is allocated/assigned.

Domains: Counselling and crisis support, Education and learning, Family, parenting and relationships, Work and employment

# Babes Pregnancy Crisis Support

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-BPCS*

For individuals aged 21 and below needing support with their pregnancy, so that they are aware of their options and are able to make an informed decision regarding their pregnancy.

**Who it targets:** Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, PR
**Keywords:** Free, Teenage Pregnancy and Sexuality

## About this support
Babes supports pregnant teens through:

- Casework and counselling
- 24-hour helpline
- Practical support (befriender, baby essentials, employment & back to school assistance etc)
- Information & resources
- Outreach and youth engagement events

## Who is this for?
- Pregnant teenager who needs help; Anyone who needs information about teenage pregnancy
- Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents

## How to apply?
If you are a pregnant teen who needs help, know of one who needs help or need information about teenage pregnancy, please contact Babes' 24-hour helpline at 6206 6641 or text via WhatsApp at 8111 3535 to speak to the caseworkers.

## What to expect?
- Teenagers who require help with their pregnancy and/or anyone who needs information about teenage pregnancy may contact Babes via the 24-hour helpline (call/text).
- When an enquiry is attended to, the Helpliner will also assess if the teenager is eligible to be a case under Babes. Should the assessment be one that Babes can assist, Babes will arrange for a meeting with the teenager and/or her family/partner within 3-5 working days to assess the needs and provide the necessary support and guidance.

# Protection Specialist Centre (PSC)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-FVSCF*

Provides services for individuals and families experiencing family violence, intimate partner violence or sexual violence.

**Who it targets:** Families, Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Abuse, neglect & violence, Free

## About this support
Protection Specialist Centres (PSC) provide a holistic range of socio-emotional, supportive and practical services to survivors, including their families and other vulnerable members in the family in order to address the danger and likelihood of future harm posed to the survivors and meet the survivors’ needs.

Services provided include:

- Casework
- Counselling
- Application of personal protection orders

## Who is this for?
- Survivors of family violence, intimate partner violence or sexual violence
- Persons who abuse
- Vulnerable family members who are witnesses of abuse or neglect/self-neglect.

## How to apply?
You may refer to the Service Providers section and call or email any of the centres for assistance.

**Care Corner Project StART** 
[6476 1482](tel:64761482)
[projectstart@carecorner.org.sg](mailto:projectstart@carecorner.org.sg)

Domains: Counselling and crisis support, Mental health

# SOS Suicide Crisis Intervention Programme

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-SSCIP*

Provides confidential emotional support to individuals facing a crisis, thinking about suicide or affected by suicide through helpline, face to face in-person, and other support services.

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Free, Suicide Intervention

## About this support
SOS Suicide Crisis Intervention Programme comprises:

- 24-hour Hotline
- CareText
- Intervention outcalls
- Specialist counselling for individuals in crisis and persons grieving a suicide loss
- Support groups for individuals with prior suicide attempts and active suicidality
- The Programme serves self-referrals, as well as referrals from partner agencies (i.e. police, hospitals, social service agencies) and concerned third parties.

## Who is this for?
Persons at risk of suicide

## How to apply?
Reach out to SOS via the 24/7 Hotline: 1767; or CareText: WhatsApp 9151 1767.

## What to expect?
Clients can access SOS Hotline calling 1767, a 24-hour Hotline run by trained volunteers and staff. Depending on suicide risk, clients may be encouraged to seek immediate support from the hospitals (e.g. IMH), and/or receive community services or further counselling support at SOS. For callers with immediate suicide risk, SOS will activate their mobile crisis response team ("Active Rescue") to coordinate and deliver emergency intervention, led by a Crisis Support Supervisor on duty.

embedding_text:
Domains: Counselling and crisis support, Mental health

# Lighthouse Project

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/IloiKSsT*

Provides psychotherapy, psychological assessment and case management for youths aged 12–25 with complex moderate to high mental health needs.

**Who it targets:** Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Free, Referral required

## About this support
The Lighthouse Project aims to be a beacon of light that attracts and correctly directs youths (aged 12-25 years old) with complex moderate to high mental health needs to accessible and appropriate help by doing the following:

- Provides psychotherapy (e.g. cognitive behavioural therapy) for youths with complex moderate to high mental health needs.
- Conducts psychological assessments (e.g. UCLA PTSD scale) to evaluate and monitor clients.
- Provides case management including referral to hospitals, case conferencing, and handholding into hospital-based treatment.
- Right-sites youths requiring higher-tiered care into primary, secondary, or tertiary care using the therapeutic relationship built with Limitless practitioners.
- Improves community standards of care through clinical supervision and training of partner organisations by Limitless' psychologists.

## Who is this for?
Youths aged 12-25 with moderate to high mental health needs.

## How to apply?
Clients need to be referred by service providers or restructured hospitals. Self-referrals are also accepted and assessed for eligibility.

Contact Limitless at *SCAPE, 2 Orchard Link, #04-06 grovve, Singapore 237978. Operating hours: Monday to Friday, 9am to 6pm.

## What to expect?
Clients would need to be referred to the programme. Lighthouse project staff would then make contact with the youth for assessment and basic emotional support. Youths may then be referred further. The duration and frequency of sessions would depend on clinician assessment.

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-LOTSSL*

Persons grieving a suicide loss

- When you reach out to SOS via call, text or email, SOS staff or trained volunteers will provide emotional support and if needed, encourage you to come for grief counselling and attend support groups subsequently for longer term support.

# Community Law Centre in North West (Community Law Centre @ Realm of Tranquility)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/QpRxBoCe*

This programme seeks to deliver integrated legal care in the North West District of Singapore by working collaboratively with community partners to holistically help and empower socially excluded individuals.

**Who it targets:** Low-income, Seniors
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Free

## About this support
Pro Bono SG’s Community Law Centre @ Realm of Tranquility will:

1. Facilitate or provide legal guidance and representation to socially and virtually excluded persons;
2. Work closely with community partners in the North West district to provide integrated legal care to socially and virtually excluded persons in the community;
3. Provide training and support to community partner staff and, where relevant, their volunteers to identify potential unmet legal needs among socially and virtually excluded beneficiaries, including referring those persons for follow-up assistance at the Community Law Centre;
4. Provide training and support to volunteer lawyers serving at Pro Bono SG's network of community legal clinics and pro bono representation schemes;
5. Conduct law awareness talks for socially and virtually excluded persons/their caregivers to equip them with functional legal knowledge of their rights and protections; and
6. Build up a corpus of best practices and knowledge database as a centre of excellence in integrated, holistic socio-legal healing

## Who is this for?
The key target groups that the programme intends to serve include:

1. Socially excluded persons* residing or working in the North West District (based on CDC postal locator) who face legal and other complex issues, and who will benefit from integrated legal care; and
2. Community partners such as Family Service Centres, Community Development Councils, Social Service Offices and Social Service Agencies in the North West District.

*Socially excluded persons are persons who may face significant barriers in accessing legal services due to socio-economic, mobility, psychological, psychiatric, language and technological factors. Such persons may include transnational families and the sandwich class who do not qualify for Government legal aid schemes.

## How to apply?

# SOS Care Text

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/ECsnBwjK*

24/7 confidential text support for suicide prevention and crisis intervention, accessible to all but targeting at youths from the ages 10 to 29 years old with suicide risk.

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Free

## About this support
Samaritans of Singapore (SOS) Care Text is dedicated to providing confidential emotional support to individuals facing a crisis, thinking about suicide or affected by suicide. This crisis intervention and suicide prevention work is done through text messaging.

This programme contributes to the identification of individuals who are suicidal or in crisis, initiation of early intervention and preventive measures, and connecting these individuals to appropriate resources where necessary

This programme is targeted at youths from the ages of 10 to 29 years old with suicide risk, but not limited to this group and anyone can access this service. Programme aims to reduce suicide risks for persons in distress through texting which is a preference for the youths. The SOS Care Text is available round-the-clock to anyone who requires emotional support and or is affected by suicide and complements the current SOS crisis hotline service. The text service is anonymous.

## Who is this for?
Targeted at youths aged 10 to 29 years old with suicide risk, but services are open to all users.

## How to apply?
CareText can be accessed via WhatsApp at 9151 1767.

## What to expect?
Clients can access CareText by texting in to WhatsApp 9151 1767. The 24-hour text messaging platform run by trained volunteers and professional staff. Depending on users' needs, they may be encouraged to seek immediate support from the hospitals (e.g. IMH), and/or receive community services or further counselling support at SOS. For texters with immediate suicide risk, SOS will activate their mobile crisis response team ("Active Rescue") to coordinate and deliver emergency intervention, led by a Crisis Support Supervisor on duty.

sections.About this support:

Domains: Counselling and crisis support, Family, parenting and relationships, Mental health

# Youth Integrated Team (YIT)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/YIT*

Provides community-based mental health assessment, therapeutic intervention, case management for youths with mild mental health conditions while monitoring and checking in with the youth before, during and after intervention has been provided.

**Who it targets:** Families, Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, PR
**Keywords:** Caregiver support, Referral required

## About this support
You can approach over 100 community mental health teams in the community islandwide such as YIT, providing the following support:

- Provide mental health assessments and support youths in understanding and identifying their care needs.
- Provide coordinated person-centric care intervention and support for youths and their caregivers through providing assessments, therapeutic intervention and case management.
- Engage community and healthcare partners to build a supportive environment for youths with mental health conditions through active collaboration and co-management of cases.
- Facilitate the formation of supportive relationships with families and peers in the recovery journey of youths.

These community mental health teams are developed under the Community Mental Health Masterplan driven by the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC), together with the Ministry of Health (MOH). The teams are fully funded by the government and there is no out-of-pocket cost.

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- Youths at higher risk for mental health conditions, their families and their support systems.
- Aged 12 to 25 years old

## How to apply?
- Call or email the providers to make an appointment. Visit [AIC’s website](https://aic.sg/Care-Services/Community-Mental-Health-Services) to search for service providers by** **postal code, address or your device’s current location.
- If you are already seeing a General Practitioner (GP) or Polyclinic doctor, you may approach them for support.

## What to expect?
Applicants may need to fulfil the services’ in-take criteria and providers’ service boundaries, if any.

Domains: Counselling and crisis support, Family, parenting and relationships, Mental health

# Strengthening Families Programme (FAM)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-SFPFFF*

Provides divorce support and family counselling to all families.

**Who it targets:** Families, Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Counselling, Families, Marital and Divorce Support

## About this support
- Provides specialised services and programmes for families facing early signs of stress, as well as divorcing and divorced families.
- These support services include marriage and divorce support programmes, and a family counselling service.
- For Minor couples who are marrying, they are required to attend a complimentary mandatory Marriage Preparation Programme (MPrep - required by law) provided by the agency.
- Young couples are also encouraged to attend the MPrep before they marry.

## Who is this for?
- Divorcing and divorced families
- Families facing marital, parenting or intrapersonal issues
- Individuals/couples below 21 years old need to seek parental or guardian (who is above 21 years old) consent.
- Strengthening Families Programme (Fei Yue - Choa Chu Kang) and Strengthening Families Programme (Care Corner - Tampines) also provide marriage support for civil minor couples (either one or both parties under 18 years old), civil young couples (groom aged between 21 and 24, bride 21 & above), and transnational couples

## How to apply?
Apply through phone calls, emails, walk-in, or referrals by other agencies.

## What to expect?
- Individuals/couples can contact the agency to request for more information on services.
- Agency worker will conduct an enquiry and intake assessment for suitability and appropriate services required.

description: Provide temporary accommodation and social work intervention to homeless families who have exhausted all other means of accommodation.
embedding_text:
Domains: Counselling and crisis support, Family, parenting and relationships, Housing and shelters

# Transitional Shelter (TS)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-TST*

Provide temporary accommodation and social work intervention to homeless families who have exhausted all other means of accommodation.

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, PR
**Keywords:** Fees payable, Referral required, Shelters

## About this support
- Transitional Shelter (TS) provides temporary accommodation to homeless families who have exhausted all other means of accommodation.
- It provides onsite social work intervention to address the complex needs of the admitted families/individuals to achieve long-term and stable housing.

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizen/ Permanent Resident
- Exhausted all other means of accommodation and facing financial difficulties
- Require social work intervention and willing to work with caseworkers to achieve long-term housing
- Able to live independently in the community, in a communal shelter setting (i.e. does not require close supervision or nursing care)

## How to apply?
- You may contact your nearest Family Service Centre (FSC) for assistance if you are homeless.
- The TS will only accept applications from FSCs and other community agencies with social work competencies that can assess whether the family/individual meets the admission criteria.
- The referring agency will need to send in the application form, social report and supporting documents to TS for assessment.

To find the FSC in your neighbourhood, call Comcare hotline at [1800 222 0000](tel:18002220000) or visit 
https://www.msf.gov.sg/our-services/directories.

## What to expect?
- Upon receiving referral, the TS will conduct an intake assessment to ensure that the applicant is eligible for the shelter.
- Clients must work with the TS on case goals and intervention plans to achieve long-term stable housing eventually.

embedding_text:
Domains: Counselling and crisis support, Family, parenting and relationships

# Child Protection Specialist Centre (CPSC)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-CPSCC*

Serves as specialists on child protection matters to provide community-based support to children who face abuse or neglect at home.

**Who it targets:** Families, Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Abuse, neglect & violence, Free, Referral required

## About this support
Child Protection Specialist Centres (CPSCs) provide child-centric, family-focused and community-based support to children who face abuse or neglect at home.

Support provided includes:

- Safety planning
- Casework intervention
- Counselling to address the risks posed to the children and young persons
- Practical and other relevant services to the children and young persons and their families

## Who is this for?
Children and young persons who face abuse or neglect at home.

## How to apply?
- Referral is required.
- Contact CPSC via phone call or email to enquire on the referral process.

## What to expect?
- After receiving the referral, the social worker from CPSC will contact the referring person to find out more about the presenting abuse or neglect concerns.
- The CPSC will then inform on whether the referral is assessed to be suitable for CPSC to provide the intervention.
- If assessed to not be suitable, CPSC will advise on the other possible services or contact points.

embedding_text:
Domains: Counselling and crisis support, Family, parenting and relationships, Mental health

# Family Service Centre (FSC)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-FSCF*

FSCs provide support for vulnerable individuals and families with social and emotional issues, and work towards stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, PR
**Keywords:** Resources and Support

## About this support
FSCs are community-based social services that provide support for vulnerable individuals and families with social and emotional issues. Social Work Practitioners at the FSCs provide case management support and also partner with other agencies to coordinate holistic support for clients to help them achieve stability, self-reliance, and social mobility.

FSC services include:

- Information and Referral: Providing information about social services, and linking individuals and families to appropriate social services and community resources based on the assessed needs
- Casework: Providing holistic case management and individual/family counselling
- Group Work: Bringing individuals and families with common needs together for purposeful group interactions to address their concerns and bring about positive change
- Community Work: Tapping on community resources to help individuals and families support and empower one another.

## Who is this for?
FSCs are open to families and individuals:

- Regardless of age, race, language or religion;
- At different life stages (such as couples, families with young children, adolescents, or elderly members); and
- Of various family structures

## How to apply?
Call, walk in or email the FSCs for help on family, socio-emotional, interpersonal or other social issues. 
To find the FSC in your neighbourhood, you can call ComCare hotline at [1800 222 0000](tel:18002220000) or visit 
https://www.msf.gov.sg/our-services/directories.

## What to expect?
- Upon contact with a FSC, a FSC worker will assess the needs of the individual/family and determine the type of support needed.
- If FSC services are required, the FSC will then work with the individual/family on their issues with the appropriate social work interventions.
- If the FSC’s services are not required and other supportive services by other partners can help to meet these needs, the FSC worker will refer the individual/family to appropriate social services or community resources.

# Our Lives Our Voices (OLOV)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/f4VjU9VH*

OLOV aims to empower clients to become self-advocates and foster an inclusive society where PWIDs can independently participate in the community in a meaningful manner. Through personalised training and peer support, it builds confidence and independence.

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities
**Citizenship:** PR, SG
**Keywords:** Education

## About this support
The programme provides structured, personalised training supported by a customised web application, peer-led facilitation, and community engagement. It equips PWIDs with essential communication and interpersonal skills, empowering them to discover their strengths, express their views, take on meaningful community roles, and pursue greater autonomy, purpose, and active participation in society.

## Who is this for?
1. PWIDs aged 18 years and above with an IQ below 70
2. PWIDs who demonstrate ability to participate in group training sessions, express basic intentions and preferences.
3. PWIDs registered under MINDS programmes

## How to apply?
Interested applicants can apply through the following:

1. Email to [olov@minds.org.sg](mailto:olov@minds.org.sg)

2.  Submit the form via https://tinyurl.com/olovinterest

3. Call 65478503

## What to expect?
1. Basic screening will be conducted to ensure that PWIDs meet the criteria
2. PWIDs will also be assessed over 2 trial sessions to determine suitability and interest.
3. Enrollment is throughout the year.

# ElderShield

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/ELDERSHIELD*

Provides basic financial support to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents with severe disability, especially during old age and need long-term care.

## Highlights
- Receive up to $400 per month for up to 5 or 6 years
- Apply through AIC eServices for Financing Schemes (eFASS)
- Processing time will take between 6 to 8 weeks

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors
**Keywords:** Cash assistance, Health Insurance, Long-term

## About this support
- Monthly cash payouts of $300 or $400 for up to 5 or 6 years upon severe disability, depending on the ElderShield plan
- Can be used for long-term care needs, such as hiring a helper, paying for care services, or daily expenses

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents who are existing ElderShield policyholders
- Assessed by an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor to be unable to perform at least 3 out of the following 6 Activities of Daily Living (ADLs):
  - Washing
  - Dressing
  - Feeding
  - Toileting
  - Walking or moving around
  - Transferring

## How to apply?
As of 1 January 2020, applications for enrolment into ElderShield as a new policyholder have closed.

Existing policyholders can apply for claims:

- Online at the [AIC eServices for Financing Schemes (eFASS)](https://efinance.aic.sg/)
- Via assistance from the nursing home your loved one is staying in
- At any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)

You will need to contact an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor for a Severe Disability Assessment (SDA) as part of the claim application. Visit the [AIC’s website](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Severe-Disability-Assessment) for a list of assessors.

## Where to go
[Visit the AIC Link branch nearest to you](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)

Note: By appointment only

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/ElderShield)

# CareShield Life

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/CARESHIELD*

Provides basic financial protection for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents with severe disability, especially during old age and need long-term care.

## Highlights
- Monthly payout for 2026 is $689 and increases annually
- Apply through AIC's eServices for Financing Schemes (eFASS)

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors
**Keywords:** Cash assistance, Health Insurance, Long-term

## About this support
- Monthly cash payouts if you remain severely disabled and meet the eligibility criteria for claims
- Monthly cash payout for 2026 is $689 and increases annually until age 67 or whenever a successful claim is made, whichever is earlier

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents who are CareShield Life policyholders
- Assessed by an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor require full assistance with at least 3 out of the following 6 Activities of Daily Living (ADLs):
  - Washing
  - Dressing
  - Feeding
  - Toileting
  - Walking or moving around
  - Transferring

## How to apply?
You can apply:

- Online at the [AIC eServices for Financing Schemes (eFASS)](https://efinance.aic.sg/)
- Via assistance from the nursing home your loved one is staying in
- At any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)

You will need to contact an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor for a Severe Disability Assessment (SDA) as part of the application. Visit the [AIC’s website](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Severe-Disability-Assessment) for a list of assessors.

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us)

## Email / Form

# ElderFund

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/ELDERFUND*

Discretionary government assistance scheme to support care needs of lower-income Singapore Citizens with severe disability.

## Highlights
- Up to $250 cash per month
- Processing time will take between 6 to 8 weeks
- Apply through AIC eServices for Financing Schemes (eFASS)

**Who it targets:** Low-income, Persons with disabilities
**Keywords:** Cash assistance, Lower-income, PWDs

## About this support
- Supports lower-income, severely disabled Singapore Citizens
- Provides up to $250 cash payout per month for as long as they remain eligible
- Payout can be used for long-term care needs such as hiring a helper and daily expenses

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizen aged 30 and above
- Lives in Singapore
- Has a monthly household income per capita of $1,500 or less
- Has a MediSave balance of less than $10,000
- Assessed by an MOH-accredited assessor to require full assistance with at least 3 out of the following 6 Activities of Daily Living (ADLs):
  - Washing
  - Dressing
  - Feeding
  - Toileting
  - Walking or moving around
  - Transferring
- Not a CareShield Life or ElderShield policyholder
- Not a CareShield Life or ElderShield supplement plan policyholder
- No longer an active recipient of ElderShield claims (including supplement claims)
- Not eligible for IDAPE, or no longer an active recipient of IDAPE

## How to apply?
You can apply:

- Online at the [AIC eServices for Financing Schemes (eFASS)](https://efinance.aic.sg/)
- Via assistance from the nursing home your loved one is staying in
- At any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)

You will need to contact an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor for a Severe Disability Assessment (SDA) as part of the application. Visit the [AIC’s website](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Severe-Disability-Assessment) for a list of assessors.

Applications from Singaporeans who do not meet the guiding financial criteria but have difficulty meeting their long-term care needs will be considered on a case-by-case basis.

## Where to go
[Visit the AIC Link branch nearest to you](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/ElderFund)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg)

## Phone number
AIC hotline: [1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060)

Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.

Domains: Disability support, Education and learning, Family, parenting and relationships

# Early Intervention Programme for Infants & Children (EIPIC)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-EIPFICE*

EIPIC is a centre-based programme that provides therapy and educational intervention for children aged 0-6 years who require medium to high levels of early intervention (EI) support.

**Who it targets:** Families, Persons with disabilities
**Citizenship:** SG, PR
**Keywords:** Intervention and Therapy, Referral required

## About this support
EIPIC is a centre-based programme that provides therapy and educational intervention for children aged 0 to 6 years who require medium to high levels of early intervention (EI) support.

The continuum of EI services include:

- EIPIC Under-2s
  - Targeted at children under 2 years old
  - Trains parents/caregivers so that they can effectively carry out intervention strategies in the child’s daily routines at home
- EIPIC@Centre
  - Provides both therapy and educational intervention services, typically in small groups
- DS-Plus
  - Provided in preschools targeted at children aged 2 to 6 years requiring low levels of EI support, and are attending preschools.

## Who is this for?
Children who are:

- From birth to 6 years old
- Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents;
- Assessed by a paediatrician to be at risk of a developmental, intellectual, sensory or physical disability, or a combination of disabilities; and
- Not concurrently enrolled in any other ECDA-funded EI programmes (i.e. DS-LS, DS-Plus programmes).

## How to apply?
- You may approach a doctor at any polyclinic to obtain referral for assessment at the Department of Child Development (DCD) at KK Women’s and Children’s Hospital (KKH) or Child Development Unit (CDU) at National University Hospital (NUH).
- Alternatively, you may approach a private paediatrician for assessment and recommendation for EIPIC.
- If your child is assessed to be suitable for EIPIC, the hospital or the private paediatrician will recommend EIPIC and submit the application to SG Enable upon your consent.

More information can be found on the [Enabling Guide](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/therapy-intervention/early-intervention-programme-for-infants-children).

## What to expect?
- Upon receiving the referral, SG Enable will contact you within 10 working days to provide necessary information to help you make an informed decision on your choice of EI Centre.
- Your selected EI Centre will contact you within 2 weeks of referral to arrange an interview and assessment of your child.
- Enrolment into a suitable programme at the preferred centre is subject to the availability of vacancies at the centre and approval of the respective centre management.

Domains: Disability support, Education and learning, Family, parenting and relationships

# Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children - P (EIPIC-P)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-EIPFIACPEP*

EIPIC-P is a programme that provides therapy and educational intervention for children aged 0 to below 7 years who require medium to high levels of early intervention (EI) support.

**Who it targets:** Families, Persons with disabilities
**Citizenship:** SG, PR
**Keywords:** Intervention and Therapy, Referral required

## About this support
EIPIC-P offers alternative Early Intervention (EI) services for children who have been referred for the Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children (EIPIC). Instead of enrolling at government-funded EIPIC centres, children could enrol at ECDA-appointed private centres at subsidised rates.

## Who is this for?
Children who are:

- From birth to 6 years old.
- Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.
- Assessed by a paediatrician to be at risk of a developmental, intellectual, sensory or physical disability, or a combination of disabilities; and
- Not concurrently enrolled in any other ECDA-funded EI programmes (i.e. EIPIC, DS-LS, DS-Plus programmes).

## How to apply?
- You may approach a doctor at any polyclinic to obtain a referral for assessment at the Department of Child Development (DCD) at KK Women’s and Children’s Hospital (KKH) or Child Development Unit (CDU) at National University Hospital (NUH).
- Alternatively, you may approach a private paediatrician for an assessment.
- If your child is assessed to be suitable for EIPIC, the hospital or the private paediatrician will recommend EIPIC and submit the application to SG Enable upon your consent.
- More information can be found on the [Enabling Guide](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/therapy-intervention/early-intervention-programme-for-infants-and-children-p).

## What to expect?
To be eligible for EIPIC-P, the child should be referred by a paediatrician to the Early Intervention (EI) Programme , with the referral made through SG Enable.

- Upon receiving the referral, SG Enable will contact you within 10 working days to provide necessary information to help you make an informed decision on your choice of an EI Centre (government-funded EIPIC centre or EIPIC-P centre).
- Your selected EI Centre will contact you within 2 weeks of referral to arrange an interview and assessment of your child.
- Enrolment into a suitable programme at the preferred centre is subject to the availability of vacancies at the centre, and approval of the respective centre management.

title: Sheltered Workshops
description: Sheltered Workshops offer employment and/or vocational training to adults with disabilities who do not possess the competencies or skills for open employment.
embedding_text:
Domains: Disability support, Work and employment

# Sheltered Workshops

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-SW*

Sheltered Workshops offer employment and/or vocational training to adults with disabilities who do not possess the competencies or skills for open employment.

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities
**Citizenship:** SG, PR
**Keywords:** Employment Support and Vocational Training, Referral required

## About this support
Sheltered workshops offer the following:

- Employment and/or vocational training to adults with disabilities who do not possess the competencies or skills for open employment.
- Allow participants to practice in jobs or tasks where the processes are either simple or broken down into simpler steps.
- Participants will gain valuable experience at the workshop, thereby improving their prospects for open employment.

## Who is this for?
Applicants should be:

- 18 years old and above*^#
- Singapore citizens of Permanent Residents^^
- Have a permanent disability based on any one of the following:
  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment
  - A visual impairment: Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye
  - A hearing impairment: Moderate hearing loss or worse in the better ear
  - Intellectual disability
  - Autism

Proof of disability must be provided using the [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)** completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional.

- Applicants should not be suffering from any untreated infectious disease.

*Students of Government and community-funded SPED schools should be encouraged to remain in school until graduation. Parents of SPED graduands may approach their School to discuss the transition plans of the children prior to graduating from School.

^Applicants who are below age 21 will need consent of parents or legal guardians for their application.

#Applicants who are aged 21 and above with no mental capacity, will need the consent of the appointed deputy(s)/donee(s) on behalf of the applicant.

^^For Permanent Residents, at least one immediate family member must be a Singapore Citizen. Immediate family members refer to spouses, parents, children or the applicant, including stepparents and stepchildren.

**From 8 September 2025, the [Disability Verification Form (DVF)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification) is the standardised proof of disability required to verify an individual’s disability status when applying for selected MSF disability schemes and services and other selected Government schemes. Applicants can check if their disability status is already verified via their Touchpoints, SupportGoWhere, or call SG Enable at [1800-8585-885](tel:1800-8585-885)

## How to apply?
- Please approach a social service professional from a Touchpoint (e.g. Social Service Agency (SSA), hospitals etc.) for assistance in submitting a Sheltered Workshop application. If you are currently not receiving support from any social service or medical touchpoints, you may [approach SG Enable for assistance](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/child-adult-care/information-and-referral-services).
- Before meeting your Touchpoints, all applicants are encouraged to check if your disability status has already been verified by logging into [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/pwdr/apply) with your Singpass. If you do not have a verified disability status, the Touchpoint will guide you to the relevant registered healthcare professionals to assist with DVF.

**Submission of applications to SG Enable by Social Service Professional (Online or Hardcopy)**

**Step 1:**

All applicants should check if they have a verified disability status by logging into [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/pwdr/apply) with their Singpass. If the applicant already has a verified disability status, a DVF is not required.

**Step 2:**

If the applicant does not have a verified disability status or has a new disability condition which has not been verified previously, registered Touchpoint Assessor/Admin must submit a copy of the DVF completed by a relevant registered Healthcare Professional together with the AD application.

**Step 3:**

Registered touchpoints’ Assessor/Admin may submit clients’ AD application and completed DVF online via CorpPass (recommended) or via hardcopy.

1. **Online submission (Recommended)**
  Log into e-Services using your CorpPass
2. **Hardcopy submission**
  Download the [AD application form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/ad-application-form.pdf?sfvrsn=71d5f444_3), print and send together with the required documents. If required, you may download sections of the AD application form and DVF below for use:
  - [Client Assessment Form (Revised)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/final-caf-r-form.pdf?sfvrsn=c2d096c3_1)
  - [Medical Information Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/final-interim-medical-information.pdf?sfvrsn=c4f804d4_1)
  - [Declaration Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/declaration-form.pdf?sfvrsn=a7fa3568_2)
  - [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)

## What to expect?
- Upon receiving the referral, SG Enable will contact you to provide information to help you make an informed decision on your choice of service.
- Acceptance into the programme at the preferred centre is subject to the availability of vacancies and approval of the centre management.

# Special Education (SPED) School (Autism Spectrum Disorder with intellectual impairment)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-SESSAWII*

Special Education (SPED) schools provide education for children and youth with disabilities who are of school-going age.

**Who it targets:** Families, Persons with disabilities
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Education, Fees payable

## About this support
Government and community-funded Special Education (SPED) schools cater to children and youths with moderate-to-severe special educational needs and require more intensive and specialised support in their schooling journey.

Different SPED schools cater to students with different special educational needs.

Visit [MOE Special Education (SPED) schools](https://www.moe.gov.sg/special-educational-needs) to learn about the support for students with special educational needs and their educational pathways.

## Who is this for?
These SPED schools offer the customised curriculum for students who have Autism Spectrum Disorder with intellectual impairment.

All schools serve students aged 7 to 18, except:

- APSN Chaoyang School (7 to 12 years old)
- APSN Katong School (7 to 16 years old)
- APSN Tanglin School (13 to 16 years old)
- Grace Orchard School (7 to 18 years old)
- Metta School (7 to 21 years old)
- APSN Delta Senior School (17 to 21 years old)

The six schools mentioned above specifically cater to students who have Autism Spectrum Disorder with mild intellectual disability.

Metta School and APSN Delta Senior School offer Vocational Certification Programmes for students aged 17 to 21.

## How to apply?
Please visit [MOE Special Education (SPED) schools](https://www.moe.gov.sg/special-educational-needs) for details on the application process for SPED schools.

## What to expect?
Please visit [MOE Special Education (SPED) schools](https://www.moe.gov.sg/special-educational-needs/sped-schools) and each SPED school’s website for more information on each school.

Domains: Disability support

# Shared Stay-in Senior Caregiving Services (Stay-in SCS)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/7gjb1DT2*

Shared caregiving services for seniors living together in a shared residence.

**Who it targets:** Seniors, Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Care in centre, Seniors

## About this support
Trained caregiving staff provides seniors living together with basic support, such as:

- Basic care
- Help with Activities of Daily Living (ADLs)
- Meal preparation
- Domestic tasks
- Social activities

## Who is this for?
- Senior who is able to live mostly independently but need help with some ADLs
- Is able to make decisions about their care, or has a next-of-kin who can do so on their behalf

## How to apply?
You can contact the service provider directly to find out more about their service offerings. Visit the [AIC’s website](https://www.aic.sg/Care-Services/Shared-Stay-in-Senior-Caregiving-Services) to search for service providers by** **postal code, address or your device’s current location.

For further assistance, you can contact AIC via the hotline[1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060) or [submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg).

- Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines in Singapore.
- Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.

## What to expect?
- Stay-in SCS does not provide medical or nursing care.
- Subsidies are currently not available, as it is a private service.

# Enabling Business Hub

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/LPsRp3sD*

Developed by SG Enable, Enabling Business Hubs (EBHs) bring training and employment opportunities closer to homes for persons with disabilities through customised job support and inclusive workplace practices.

## Highlights
- Employment for PwDs
- Training and employment opportunities for PwDs

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities
**Keywords:** Employment Support and Vocational Training, Jobseekers, PWDs

## About this support
With an on-site Employment Support Team, persons with disabilities can look forward to a comprehensive suite of employment-related services such as vocational assessment, training, job-matching and post-placement job support. These services aim to better match persons with disabilities to jobs in the region based on their skills and interests and support them in employment.

EBH@Jurong

Located beside Lakeside MRT, at 111A Yuan Ching Road, Singapore 619606, EBH@Jurong aims to bring training and employment opportunities closer to the homes of persons with disabilities living in the West, including those with higher work support needs.

Key Features of EBH@Jurong

1. Provide targeted training and support** **to prepare persons with disabilities for employment in the logistics sector.
2. Provide on-site employment support, including longer and more intensive employment support for persons with disabilities with higher work support needs and require a longer runway of support to work independently in the community.

## Who is this for?
Applicants should be:

- Aged 16 and above
- Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents
- Verified to have a permanent disability of any of the following:
  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least one of the six Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment
  - Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye
  - Moderate hearing loss or worse in the better ear
  - Intellectual disability
  - Autism
- Preferably living in the West or keen to work in the Logistics industry

## How to apply?
**Prior to application, applicants are encouraged to check if your disability status has already been verified by logging into **[**SupportGoWhere**](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/status/pwdr)**. **

**Preparation of documents**

The following supporting documents are required before making an application:

- [Disability Verification Form (DVF)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/disability-verification-form.pdf) (To be completed and endorsed by registered healthcare professional if disability status is unverified)
- Copy of NRIC Front and Back
- [One Referral Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/one-referral-form-with-omnibus_2025.pdf?sfvrsn=ab89bee_1) (For email/physical submissions only)

**How to apply**

Persons with disabilities seeking employment assistance may:

1. Apply online via [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/ebh/apply),[ ](#_msocom_5)or
2. Download the One Referral Form (ORF) and email the supporting documents to EBH@Jurong at [EBH_Jurong@bizlink.org.sg](mailto:EBH_Jurong@bizlink.org.sg) or;
3. Contact [EBH_Jurong@bizlink.org.sg](mailto:EBH_Jurong@bizlink.org.sg) to schedule an appointment with the EBH@Jurong employment services team.

Persons with disabilities keen on other employment programmes, please email us at [employment@sgenable.sg](mailto:employment@sgenable.sg).

Domains: Disability support

# Gift Of A Lifetime Plus (GOAL+)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/bjQYWnuX*

Gift Of A Lifetime Plus (GOAL+) aims to provide eligible caregivers of person with disability (PWDs) with an initial capital of $5,000 to set up trust accounts with Special Needs Trust Company Pte Ltd (SNTC). Under GOAL+, the Government sponsors matching donations of up to $10,000 for low- and middle-income families who contribute to the trust account within a five-year window period.

## Highlights
- GOAL+ is a sponsorship scheme that aims to help caregivers save and provide for their dependant with disability. SG Enable Case Managers will invite eligible caregivers to apply for GOAL+ during the trust set-up process.  

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities
**Keywords:** Caregiving expenses, PWDs, Special needs

## About this support
How does GOAL+ work?

1. GOAL+ runs from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031. Eligible caregivers whose PWDs do not have a Special Needs Trust (SNT) account can receive $5,000 from Community Chest to set up one.
2. Eligible caregivers of PWDs with verified disability can qualify for matching top-ups of up to $10,000 from the Government.
3. GOAL+ allows for a five-year top-up window for eligible SNT accounts, so that caregivers can plan contributions via cash top-up to the trust account in a more sustainable manner. Applicants are strongly encouraged to top up the trust account as soon as practicable. Any contribution made beyond the five years will not be entitled to matching top-ups from the Government.

## Who is this for?
To qualify for GOAL+, PWD must meet the following criteria:

- A Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- The family has a per capita household income (PCHI) of ≤ $3,600 (P64), or annual value (AV) of property ≤ $21,000 for households with a PCHI of $0.
- Has a verified disability

## How to apply?
Before applying for GOAL+, all applicants are encouraged to:

1. Check if the PWD’s disability status has already been verified by logging into [SupportGoWhere](http://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/pwdr/apply) with your Singpass. If PWD is above 21 years old and does not have Singpass, you may check his/her disability status by calling the Operator (Bizlink) at 64366635 or email to [msfdisability@bizlink.org.sg](mailto:msfdisability@bizlink.org.sg).
2. If PWD does not have a verified disability status, he/she must get a [Disability Verification Form (DVF)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification) completed by a relevant registered Healthcare Professional*.

*Please note that a submitted DVF does not mean that PWD’s disability status has been verified.

Please contact SG Enable for an appointment with a Case Manager to:

(i)     Find out how the Special Needs Trust works

(ii)    Assess eligibility for GOAL+ sponsorship

[22 Lengkok Bahru 159824](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159824)

Vista, Enabling Village #03-03

[6278 9598](tel:62789598)
(Operating hours: 9am-6pm on weekdays, closed on weekends and public holidays)

Applicants are strongly encouraged to top up the trust account as soon as practicable. Any contribution made beyond the five years will not be entitled to matching top-ups from the Government.
sections.Who is this for?:
To qualify for GOAL+, PWD must meet the following criteria:

- A Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- The family has a per capita household income (PCHI) of ≤ $3,600 (P64), or annual value (AV) of property ≤ $21,000 for households with a PCHI of $0.
- Has a verified disability
sections.How to apply?:
Before applying for GOAL+, all applicants are encouraged to:

1. Check if the PWD’s disability status has already been verified by logging into [SupportGoWhere](http://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/pwdr/apply) with your Singpass. If PWD is above 21 years old and does not have Singpass, you may check his/her disability status by calling the Operator (Bizlink) at 64366635 or email to [msfdisability@bizlink.org.sg](mailto:msfdisability@bizlink.org.sg).
2. If PWD does not have a verified disability status, he/she must get a [Disability Verification Form (DVF)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification) completed by a relevant registered Healthcare Professional*.

*Please note that a submitted DVF does not mean that PWD’s disability status has been verified.

Please contact SG Enable for an appointment with a Case Manager to:

(i)     Find out how the Special Needs Trust works

(ii)    Assess eligibility for GOAL+ sponsorship

Domains: Disability support, Financial support and benefits

# Special Needs Trust

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/cllsZZkD*

Special Needs Trust Company (SNTC) is a not-for-profit trust company and a registered charity. As a fully owned subsidiary of SG Enable, SNTC provides affordable trust services to safeguard monies set aside by caregivers to fund the long-term care needs of their beneficiaries who are persons with disability. 

The Special Needs Trust (SNT) is a legal arrangement for SNTC to hold monies for persons with disability (PWD).

## Highlights
- Sponsorship schemes eg GOAL+ are available to enable lower-income families set up the Special Needs Trust with $5,000. 

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities
**Keywords:** PWDs, Special needs

## About this support
After the Special Needs Trust (SNT) is set up, SNTC works with caregivers to put in place proper plans and arrangements that will enhance the financial well-being of PWDs (Beneficiary).

The SNT pathway is as per the following:

1. Caregiver opens an SNT account with an initial deposit of 5,000
2. Beneficiary receives gifts under the caregiver’s will, CPF cash and insurance nominations

Disburse funds to the beneficiary upon the caregiver’s passing or incapacity according to latter’s wishes set out in the Letter of Intent.

1. The trust fund is managed by the Public Trustee and principal value is guaranteed by the Government. SNTC fees are 90-100% subsidised by the Ministry of Social and Family Development.
2. Reviews are conducted periodically to check on the beneficiary's well-being.
3. Case Managers will advise caregiver on the future care needs of the beneficiary through a personalised care plan.

## Who is this for?
Caregivers (Settlor) setting up the SNT should be:

- 21 years and above
- Has mental capacity
- Not an undischarged bankrupt

Persons with Disability (Beneficiary) must be:

- A Singaporean or Permanent Resident
- Residing in Singapore
- Has a verified disability

## How to apply?
To start the Special Needs Trust journey, please contact SG Enable for an appointment with a Case Manager at [futurecareplanning@sgenable.sg](mailto:futurecareplanning@sgenable.sg).

Domains: Caregiving, Disability support

# CAREbuddy

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/7mQT5PCe*

CAREbuddy is a supportive service for caregivers, provided by trained volunteers (CAREbuddy) who are also caregivers to dependents with disabilities.

CAREbuddy programme is 6-months long during which the CAREbuddy provides emotional support, shares resources, and helps caregivers progress in their caregiving journey.

## Highlights
- Caregivers will be matched with a CAREbuddy of a similar profile, according to availability.
- The CAREbuddy supports the Caregiver to work through personal and family goals, in ways that bring about positive changes.
- 97% of caregivers felt connected to their CAREbuddy and enjoyed good rapport / communication.

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities
**Keywords:** Caregiver support, PWDs

## About this support
CAREbuddy program consists of a network of trained volunteers who are caregivers to persons with dependents with disabilities themselves.  These trained volunteers befriend caregivers on a one-to-one basis, lend a listening ear, and journey with caregivers over a six-month period with at least 4 touchpoints to bring about positive changes in their caregiving journey.

Caregivers will be paired with a CAREbuddy who shares a similar profile, based on availability.

The dates and timing of the meet ups will be arranged according to both the CAREbuddy’s and Caregiver’s convenience.

CAREbuddy volunteers understand the challenges and experiences of caring for dependents with special needs or disabilities, as they are caregiver themselves.

Kindly note that CAREbuddy programme does not provide respite and emergency support. CAREbuddy volunteer is not a mental health or special needs professional and will not be able to support the caregiver in areas where professional knowledge and skills are required.  CAREbuddy volunteers do not provide 24 hours hotline, SOS service, child-minding or child-buddy service.

## Who is this for?
CAREbuddy program is a highly subsidised program made affordable to all caregivers of persons with special needs.

Interested caregivers can contact CaringSG to find out the eligible subsidies available to them.

## How to apply?
Interested caregivers or external agency can click on the link to request for CAREbuddy.

embedding_text:
Domains: Disability support

# Enabled Living Programme (ELP)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/s1Mns2Os*

A community living programme that empowers adults with disabilities to live independently in the community for as long as possible

## Highlights
- Basic support (such as basic home maintenance, community engagement, and referral to other agencies for additional support as needed) to enable independent living and social engagement in the community

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities
**Keywords:** PWDs, Rental flats

## About this support
The Enabled Living Programme (ELP) is a community living initiative that empowers adults with disabilities with low to moderate support needs to live independently for as long as possible.

Sited in public rental flats, ELP helps adults with disabilities age in place by providing an ecosystem of care and social support that includes on-site services – such as daily living and social skills coaching and community engagement.

By fostering community integration, ELP supports adults with disabilities to build meaningful connections, enhancing their overall well-being, autonomy, and dignity.

The ELP sites and appointed service providers are listed on the [Enabling Guide](https://www.enablingguide.sg/elp-and-hsp).

## Who is this for?
Applicants should:

1. Be a Singapore Citizen​
2. Be aged 35 to 64
3. Have a permanent disability based on one or more the following [(refer to the disability profile(s) that each ELP site serves)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/child-adult-care/elp-and-hsp#abouttheelpsites):
  - Physical disability – Requires assistance with at least one of the six Activities of Daily Living (ADLs)* due to physical impairment
  - Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye
  - Moderate hearing loss or worse in the better ear
  - Intellectual disability
  - Autism

Proof of disability must be provided using the [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)**  completed by a relevant registered Healthcare Professional.

1. Not be enrolled in any government-funded adult disability hostel, adult disability residential home or day activity centres
2. Not have any caregivers who are available or capable of caring for them
3. Not have significant physical health, mental health or behavioural needs that are beyond what ELP can reasonably support
4. Fulfils Housing and Development Board (HDB)’s public rental flat criteria under the Joint Singles Scheme

Applicants who do not meet the eligibility criteria may still be considered, subject to a case-by-case assessment.

Notes:

* The six ADLs are washing, dressing, feeding, toileting, mobility and transferring.

** From 8 September 2025, the Disability Verification Form (DVF) is the standardised proof of disability required to verify an individual’s disability status when applying for selected MSF disability schemes and services and other selected Government disability schemes. Applicants can check if their disability status is already verified via their Touchpoints, SupportGoWhere, or call SG Enable at 1800-8585-885.

## How to apply?
Interested and eligible individuals can indicate their interest by submitting the online [Interest Form](https://form.gov.sg/68ef4f88c0ad227e08a66dcb) to SG Enable.

The relevant Service Provider will reach out to the applicants for assessment within 10 working days. Please note that submitting this form does not guarantee enrolment into the Enabled Living Programme.

Domains: Disability support, Work and employment

# Job Placement and Job Support

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/ejdrPN9A*

Provides persons with disabilities employment assistance through job matching and job coaching for up to 12 months.

## Highlights
- Vocational assessment to assess work readiness
- Explore job opportunities with inclusive employers
- Receive job support for up to 12 months: On-site job coaching to facilitate workplace integration

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities
**Keywords:** Employment Support and Vocational Training, Jobseekers, PWDs

## About this support
SG Enable works with partner agencies funded by the government to provide Job Placement and Job Support (JPJS) services such as APSN, Autism Resource Centre (Singapore), Movement for the Intellectually Disabled of Singapore (MINDS) and SPD. Persons with disabilities who approach SG Enable for employment assistance will be referred to a suitable partner agency, subject to the respective agency’s eligibility criteria.

SG Enable and its appointed partners provide specialised job placement and job support services that include the following:

- Assessing the jobseeker’s strengths, job interests and skills, and identifying training opportunities
- Helping the jobseeker identify job opportunities and link up with prospective inclusive employers
- Assessing the nature of the job and its tasks for suitability
- Assessing the built environment for accessibility
- Working with the employer to job redesign and recommend workplace modification, making use of assistive devices, if needed
- On-site job coaching to help the new employee integrate into the workplace

## Who is this for?
Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents who are verified to have a permanent disability of any of the following:

- Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least one of the size Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment
- Moderate Visual Impairment or worse in the better eye
- Moderate Hearing Loss or worse in the better ear
- Intellectual Disability
- Autism

^You can check if your disability status is verified on [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/status/pwdr) or contact us at [employment@sgenable.sg](mailto:employment@sgenable.sg).

## How to apply?
**Preparation of documents**

The following support documents are required before making an application:

- [Disability Verification Form (DVF)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/disability-verification-form.pdf) (To be completed and endorsed by registered healthcare professional)
- Copy of NRIC Front and Back
- One Referral Form (for email/physical submissions only)

**How to apply**

Persons with disabilities seeking employment assistance may apply

1)      Online via SupportGoWhere, or

2)      Download the [One Referral Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/one-referral-form-with-omnibus_2025.pdf?sfvrsn=ab89bee_1) and email us at [employment@sgenable.sg](mailto:employment@sgenable.sg), or

3)      Approach SG Enable’s Information and Career Centre, located within the Enabling Village, for assistance.

Jobseekers with disabilities can also apply for vacancies with our inclusive employers in our [Disability Employment Portal](https://eservice1.enable.gov.sg/MSFPortal/EDS/Employment/Pages/Common/Index/Index.aspx).

## Where to go
[20 Lengkok Bahru 159053](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)

Enabling Village #01-01

[View more details](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/training-employment/job-placement-and-job-support)

## Email / Form
[contactus@sgenable.sg](mailto:contactus@sgenable.sg)

embedding_text:
Domains: Disability support, Mental health, Work and employment

# Hospital-to-Work Transition Programme

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/zQnhRFwq*

Provides case management, rehabilitation and employment support for persons with acquired disability from accidents or medical conditions who are looking to return to work.

## Highlights
- Provides employment assistance for persons with acquired disabilities
- Personalised rehabilitation and training facilitation
- 1-1 case management services

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities
**Keywords:** Employment Support and Vocational Training, Jobseekers, PWDs

## About this support
Jobseekers in the programme can get personalised career re-assessment, rehabilitation and job-matching services. Persons with disabilities who are already in employment can also benefit from job support services. A case manager will support you throughout your transition to work, providing the following services:

Rehabilitation

- For clients requiring rehabilitation support, SG Enable collaborates with partner agencies such as SPD and ABLE to provide integrated rehabilitation and employment support services.

Case management

- Assessing the jobseeker’s strengths, job interests and skills, and identifying job options.
- Facilitate psychosocial and community support through referrals, if needed.
- Recommending relevant training courses, building resume and strengthening interview skills.
- Assessing the nature of the job and its tasks for suitability.
- Assessing the built environment for accessibility.

- Vocational re-assessment, training coordination, job matching and placement, and on-site job coaching to help the new employee integrate into the workplace.

- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- Above 16 years of age
- Medically certified as fit for employment
- Persons with a permanent acquired disability*^ based on any one of the following:
  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least one of the six Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment
  - Moderate Visual Impairment or worse in the better eye
  - Moderate Hearing Loss or worse in the better ear

*If your condition does not fall under the categories listed above, you may still approach SG Enable for a discussion.

^You can check if your disability status is verified on [SupportGoWhere ](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/status/pwdr)by logging with your Singpass or contacting us at [H2W_SWW@sgenable.sg](mailto:H2W_SWW@sgenable.sg).
