- [Fitness for Employment and Rehabilitation Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/h2w-fitness-for-employment-and-rehabilitation-form.pdf) (To be completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional)
- [Hospital-to-Work Application Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/h2w-application-form.pdf) (For email/physical submissions only)
- [OneMSF Omnibus Consent Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/onemsf-omnibus-consent-form_version-1-0.docx)
- Copy of NRIC Front and Back

** For persons with disabilities**:

- Apply online via [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/h2w/apply), or
- Email [H2W_SWW@sgenable.sg](mailto:H2W_SWW@sgenable.sg) with the above completed supporting documents
- Approach SG Enable’s Information and Career Centre, located within the Enabling Village, for assistance.

** **

**For Healthcare Professionals (HCP) **making referrals:

- Apply online via [Partner Portal](https://partner.casecentral.gov.sg/), or
- Email [H2W_SWW@sgenable.sg](mailto:H2W_SWW@sgenable.sg) with the above supporting documents filled and endorsed.

[20 Lengkok Bahru 159053](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)

# CareShield Life / ElderShield Supplements 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/2K6v76Ac*

Provides additional benefits, like higher payouts, for CareShield Life or ElderShield policyholders.

## Highlights
- Supplement premiums can be paid using cash or MediSave for flexibility in payment
- Can acquire multiple supplement policies to suit your needs
- Grants extra coverage in addition to your existing CareShield Life or ElderShield plan

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors
**Keywords:** Health Insurance, Long-term care

## About this support
- Complements your CareShield Life or ElderShield plan with enhanced coverage, providing extra benefits such as increased monthly payouts
- Flexibility to buy multiple supplement policies for enhanced coverage
- Premiums for Supplements can be paid thru cash or by using your or your family member’s MediSave, limited to $600 per calendar year per insured person
- If you have existing Supplements under ElderShield and choose to join CareShield Life, you may continue to maintain your previous policy and can claim from both

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- Existing CareShield Life or ElderShield policyholder

## How to apply?
- Application for plans is done through the individual insurers
- To review and compare Supplement plans, you may:
  - visit insurer websites or contact them directly for plan details.
  - read more about Supplements and see the [comparison charts available online for CareShield Life and ElderShield supplements](https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/schemes-and-subsidies/careshield-life/careshield-life-and-eldershield-supplements)

[View more details](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/healthcare-financing/getting-supplementary-coverage/careshield-life-eldershield-supplements)

Domains: Disability support, Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits, Healthcare and well-being

# CareShield Life Premium Subsidies 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/PKQxhC2q*

To ensure that CareShield Life premiums are affordable, the Government has committed to providing several premium support measures, such as Premium Subsidies, Participation Incentives and Additional Participation Incentives for Merdeka and Pioneer Generation.

## Highlights
- Means-tested CareShield Life Premium Subsidies of up to 30% 

**Who it targets:** Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors
**Keywords:** Health Insurance, Subsidies

## About this support
- Means-tested Premium Subsidies of up to 30% for eligible lower- to middle-income households
- Transitional support will also be provided to all policyholders to help manage the premium increases from 2026 to 2029, following the CareShield Life 2025 Review
- Participation Incentives for Singapore Citizens born in 1979 or earlier who joined and were covered under CareShield Life between 1 January 2024 and 31 December 2024: Up to $1,875 ($187.50/year)
- Additional Participation Incentives for Pioneer and Merdeka Generation citizens who joined and were covered under CareShield Life between 1 January 2024 and 31 December 2024: $1,125 ($112.50/year)
- Participation incentives and Additional Participation Incentives will be spread equally over 10 years and used to offset premiums payable for each year

## Who is this for?
**Eligibility for means-tested Premium Subsidies:**

- Subsidies of up to 30% for eligible Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents
- Permanent Residents will receive half the subsidy rate applicable for Singapore Citizens
- Household monthly income per person of $3,600 or below
- Living in residences with an Annual Value (AV) of $31,000 and below
- Not owning more than 1 property

As of 1 Jan 2025,

Household Income Tier
Household Monthly Income Per Person
Subsidy
Lower-Income
$0 - $1,500
30%
Lower-Middle-Income
> $1,501 - $2,600
25%
Upper-Middle-Income
> $2,601 - $3,600
20%

Note: The above subsidy rates apply to those living in residences with an AV of $21,000 or less. Residences with an AV between $21,001 and $31,000 receive 10% less subsidies. Those who live in residences with an AV above $31,000 or own multiple properties will not receive these subsidies.

**Eligibility for Participation Incentives:**

- For Singapore Citizens born in 1979 or earlier who joined and were covered under CareShield Life by 31 December 2024
- Depending on birth year
- Total Participation Incentives will be spread equally over 10 years and used to offset premiums payable for each year

**Eligibility for Additional Participation Incentives:**

- For Merdeka and Pioneer Generation seniors who joined and were covered under CareShield Life by 31 December 2024
- Provided on top of Participation Incentives
- Total Participation Incentives provided will be spread equally over 10 years and used to offset premiums payable for each year

**Eligibility for Transitional Support (CareShield Life 2025 Review)**

All policyholders who see an increase in their gross premiums. Transitional support is directly provided to policyholders. Policyholders do not need to apply for this support.

Please click [here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/healthcare-financing/careshield-life/careshield-premiums-and-subsidies) for more information on Premium Subsidies, Participation Incentives and Additional Participation Incentives.

## How to apply?
The subsidies that you are eligible for will be automatically applied to your CareShield Life premiums.

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us)

Note: By appointment only

## Agency website
Please click [here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/healthcare-financing/careshield-life/careshield-premiums-and-subsidies) for more information on Premium Subsidies, Participation Incentives and Additional Participation Incentives.

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/contact-us)

## Phone number
Healthcare Hotline: [1800-222-3399](tel:1800-222-3399)

To avoid waiting on the line, you may book an appointment [here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/appt/oas/form).

# Special Education (SPED) School (Multiple Disabilities)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-SESSMD*

Special Education (SPED) schools provide education for children and youth with disabilities who are of school-going age.

**Who it targets:** Families, Persons with disabilities
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Education, Fees payable

## About this support
Government and community-funded Special Education (SPED) schools cater to children and youths with moderate-to-severe special educational needs and require more intensive and specialised support in their schooling journey.

Different SPED schools cater to students with different special educational needs.

Visit [MOE Special Education (SPED) schools](https://www.moe.gov.sg/special-educational-needs) to learn about the support for students with special educational needs and their educational pathways.

## Who is this for?
These SPED schools offer the customised curriculum for students aged 7 to 18 with Multiple Disabilities.

These schools include:

- Cerebral Palsy Alliance Singapore School (East)
- Cerebral Palsy Alliance Singapore School (West)
- Rainbow Centre Margaret Drive School

Note: From 2026, AWWA School @ Napiri will not be enrolling students with Multiple Disabilities.

## How to apply?
Please visit [MOE Special Education (SPED) schools](https://www.moe.gov.sg/special-educational-needs) for details on the application process for SPED schools.

## What to expect?
Please visit [MOE Special Education (SPED) schools](https://www.moe.gov.sg/special-educational-needs/sped-schools) and each SPED school’s website for more information on each school.

# Persons with Disabilities Concession Card (PWDCC)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/PWD-CONCESSION*

Provides persons with disabilities with concessionary rates for travel on public transport.

## Highlights
- Discount of up to 55% off adult public transport fares and option to buy monthly pass at $55 per month
- Persons with Disabilities Concession Card will be mailed out within 14 working days after SimplyGo receives your application
- Apply online via SG Enable website

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities
**Keywords:** Public transport, PWDs

## About this support
- Discount of up to 55% off for adult public transport fares
- Option to purchase Monthly Public Transport Concession Pass at $55 per month for unlimited travel on train and basic bus services
- No additional fares for distance beyond 7.2km

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizen and Permanent Resident
- Aged 7 to below 60 years old
- Have a permanent disability based on any one of the following:
  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment
  - A visual impairment: Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye
  - A hearing impairment: Moderate hearing loss or worse in the better ear
  - Intellectual disability
  - Autism

Proof of disability must be provided using the [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification) completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional.

## How to apply?
Proof of disability must be provided using the [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification) completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional.

For more information on the application process, please visit [Enabling Guide](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/transport/persons-with-disabilities-concession-card).

## Where to go
[Enabling Village](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)
[20 Lengkok Bahru](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)
[#01-01, Singapore 159053](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)

# Tax Reliefs

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/sygrV7iy*

Provides tax reliefs to taxpayers who support family members in need, inclusive of dependants with disabilities.

## Highlights
- Provides up to $14,000 of tax relief for taxpayers who support family members in need, inclusive of dependants with disabilities or impairment 

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Dependents, PWDs, Tax relief

## About this support
- [**Grandparent Caregiver Relief (GCR) **](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/cVyhpH3s/grandparent-caregiver-relief-gcr)

Provides tax relief of up to $3,000 to working mothers who engage their parents, grandparents or in-laws as caregivers for their children.

- [**Parent Relief/ Parent Relief (Disability)**](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/TAX_RELIEF_CAREGIVERS_DISABLED/parent-reliefparent-relief-disability)

Provides tax relief of up to $14,000 per dependant for individuals supporting their parents, grandparents or in-laws, with additional relief for dependants with disabilities.

- [**Sibling Relief (Disability)**](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/U3ip0GiR/sibling-relief-disability)

Provides tax relief of up to $5,500 per dependant to individuals supporting their siblings or siblings-in-law with disabilities.

- ** **[**Spouse/Spouse Relief (Disability) **](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/nO5dmWvA/spouse-reliefspouse-relief-disability)

Provides tax relief of up to $5,500 to individuals who support their spouse, including those with disabilities.

## Who is this for?
- Working mothers (married, divorced, or widowed) with a Singaporean child under 12/unmarried child with disabilities and caregiver/s that resides in Singapore

- Taxpayers supporting dependant/s aged 55 and above, including those with disabilities, living in their household.
- Taxpayers supporting sibling/s with a disability/mental impairment in the same household.

- Taxpayers supporting a spouse with an annual income under $4,000, including those with disabilities.

## How to apply?
Please click on the link to the respective schemes above to find out how to apply.

[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.iras.gov.sg/contact-us/locate-us)

# Disabled Persons Scheme (DPS)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/DPS_MSF*

Eligible drivers are exempted from paying the premium for the Certificate of Entitlement (COE) and the Additional Registration Fee (ARF) when they purchase a vehicle.

## Highlights
- Exemption from Certificate of Entitlement (COE) and Additional Registration Fee (ARF) for eligible persons with disabilities who are gainfully employed and need a vehicle to earn a living
- For Singaporean Citizens with permanent physical disabilities who are medically certified as permanently disabled and incapable of taking public transport (i.e. bus and/or MRT), but fit to drive

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities
**Keywords:** Employment Support and Vocational Training, PWDs, Transport

## About this support
- Eligible drivers are exempted from paying the ​premium for the Certificate of Entitlement (COE) and the Additional Registration Fee (ARF) when they purchase a vehicle

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizen
- Persons with permanent physical disabilities who are medically certified by doctors from the Tan Tock Seng Hospital, Clinic for Advanced Rehabilitation Therapeutics (CART) as permanently disabled and incapable of taking public transport (i.e. bus and/or MRT), but fit to drive
- Gainfully employed and need a vehicle to earn a living
- Possesses a valid Class 3 Driving Licence
- In the 30th income percentile or below where household income does not exceed $6,500 for a 4-member household
- Vehicle must meet all of the following specifications:
  - Engine capacity must not be more than 1,600cc
  - Maximum power output of not more than 97kW (130bhp)
  - Open Market Value (OMV) of not more than S$20,000

## How to apply?
For more information on the application process, please visit [Enabling Guide](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/transport/disabled-persons-scheme).

## Where to go
[Enabling Village](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)

[#01-01, Singapore 159053](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)

# Parent Relief/Parent Relief (Disability)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/TAX_RELIEF_CAREGIVERS_DISABLED*

Provides tax relief of up to $14,000 per dependant, to recognise individuals supporting their parents, grandparents, parents-in-law or grandparents-in-law in Singapore.

## Highlights
- Up to $14,000 per dependant
- Claim Parent Relief/Parent Relief (Disability) for up to 2 dependants
- May be shared with other claimants provided no one else is claiming any other relief (except Grandparent Caregiver Relief) on the same dependant

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors
**Keywords:** Caregiver support, Tax relief

## About this support
**For taxpayer who stays with dependant**

- $9,000 parent relief per dependant
- $14,000 Parent Relief (Disability) per dependant

**For taxpayer who does not stay with dependant**

- $5,500 parent relief per dependant
- $10,000 Parent Relief (Disability) per dependant

## Who is this for?
The dependant:

- was 55 years of age or above
- is living in your household in Singapore
  - If the dependant lived in a separate household in Singapore, you must have incurred $2,000 or more in supporting them
- has disability or mental impairment (for the claim of Parent Relief (Disability))

## How to apply?
**For e-Filing**

- Log in with your Singpass or [Singpass Foreign user Account (SFA)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/digital-services/others/singpass-foreign-user-account-(sfa)-for-foreign-individuals) at [myTax Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/login/selection)
- Go to “Individuals” > “File Income Tax Return”
- Select “File” to File Income Tax Return
- Go to “4. Deductions, Tax Reliefs and Rebates”
- Select “Add New” > “Parent”
- Click “Update” and enter your claim

**For paper filing**

- Complete the item on "Parent/Parent Relief (Disability)" on Form B1 & B
- Complete the particulars of your dependant(s) in Appendix 2

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs/parent-relief-parent-relief-(disability))

# Spouse Relief/Spouse Relief (Disability)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/nO5dmWvA*

Provides tax relief of up to $5,500 to both male and female taxpayers who have supported their spouses.

## Highlights
- Spouse Relief of $2,000, up to $5,500 for spouse with disability or mental impairment

**Who it targets:** Families, Persons with disabilities
**Keywords:** Dependents, PWDs, Tax relief

## About this support
- Spouse Relief of $2,000 for taxpayers who have supported their spouses
- Spouse Relief (Disability) of $5,500 for taxpayers who have supported their spouses with disabilities

## Who is this for?
**For Spouse Relief:**

You must fulfil all these conditions in the previous year:

- Your spouse has been living with / supported by you
- Your spouse did not have an annual income of more than $8,000
- You have made maintenance payments under a Court Order or Deed of Separation (if you are legally separated from your spouse)

**For Spouse Relief (Disability):**

- Dependant must be certified by a doctor to require the need for assistance with any of the 6 Activities of Daily Living:
  - Washing or Bathing
  - Dressing
  - Feeding
  - Toileting
  - Transferring
  - Mobility
- Dependant must be certified by a doctor to be impaired in any of these 3 areas:
  - Self-Care and Activities of Daily Living
  - Compliance to Psychiatric Treatment
  - Education or Work
- No other claimants may claim the Parent Relief / Parent Relief (Disability) or Sibiling Relief (Disability) on the same dependant (your spouse)

## How to apply?
**For e-Filing**

Is this the first time you are claiming the relief?

Yes
No
- Log in with Singpass or [Singpass Foreign user Account(SFA)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/digital-services/others/singpass-foreign-user-account-(sfa)-for-foreign-individuals) at [myTax Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/login/selection)
- Go to “Individuals” > “File Income Tax Return”
- Select “File” > File Income Tax Return
- Go to “4. Deductions, Tax Reliefs and Rebates”
- Select “Add New” > “Spouse”
- Fill in the relevant information and select “Update”
- If you were previously approved for relief last year, the amount will be pre-filled and granted to you automatically
- Follow the steps on the left and select “Not Claiming” if you wish to withdraw your claim

**For Paper Filing**

Is this the first time you are claiming the relief?

Yes
No
- Complete the item on “Spouse/Spouse Relief (Disability)” section on Form B1 & B
- Complete the particulars of your spouse in Appendix 2
- Complete the item on “Spouse/Spouse Relief (Disability)” section on Form B1 & B

**For first-time Handicapped Spouse Relief claims:**

Email 1 of the following documents via [myTax Mail](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/login/selection)

- Completed Application for Claim of Disability Related Tax Reliefs
- Letter / supporting documents from the disability association in respect of your spouse, indicating details of their disabilities

# Grandparent Caregiver Relief (GCR) 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/cVyhpH3s*

Provides tax relief of up to $3,000 to working mothers who engage their parents, grandparents, parents-in-law or grandparents-in-law as caregivers for their children.

## Highlights
- Claim $3,000 for Grandparent Caregiver Relief (GCR) 

**Who it targets:** Families, Persons with disabilities
**Keywords:** Caregiver support, Tax relief

## About this support
- Eligible working mother can claim relief of $3,000
- Caregiver may be the subject of other relief claims e.g. Parent Relief, Spouse Relief

## Who is this for?
To be eligible for GCR, you must meet all the following conditions:

- Working mother who is married, divorced or widowed
- Caregiver resides and lives in Singapore^
- Caregiver is a parent / grandparent / parent-in-law / grandparent-in-law (in-laws include that of ex-spouses')
- As of last year, caregiver has been looking after a Singapore Citizen child aged 12 and below / an unmarried child with disabilities
- Caregiver's annual income did not exceed $8,000 from any trade, business, profession, vocation and / or employment in the previous year
- No one else has claimed GCR on the same caregiver. Relief is limited to 1 claim for 1 parent / grandparent i.e. a single claim of $3,000

^ Dependant has been staying in Singapore on a permanent basis. Foreign dependants must have stayed in Singapore for at least 8 months in the previous year.

## How to apply?
**For e-Filing:**

- If claiming the relief for the first time:
  - Log in with Singpass or [Singpass Foreign user Account (SFA)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/digital-services/others/singpass-foreign-user-account-(sfa)-for-foreign-individuals) at [myTax Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/login/selection)
  - Navigate to “Individuals” > “File Income Tax Return”
  - Select “File” to File Income Tax Return
  - Go to “4. Deductions, Tax Reliefs and Rebates”
  - Select “Add New” > “Grandparent Caregiver”
  - Fill in the relevant information and select “Update”
- If you have previously claimed GCR, the amount will be pre-filled and granted to you automatically. You may refer to the above steps if you would like to make changes to your relief

**For paper filing:**

- For Form B1 & B, fill in the “Grandparent Caregiver Relief” section.
- Include your dependant's details in Appendix 2 as well, if it’s your first time claiming GCR

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.iras.gov.sg/contact-us/locate-us)

[View more details](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs/grandparent-caregiver-relief)

- Caregiver resides and lives in Singapore^
- Caregiver is a parent / grandparent / parent-in-law / grandparent-in-law (in-laws include that of ex-spouses')
- As of last year, caregiver has been looking after a Singapore Citizen child aged 12 and below / an unmarried child with disabilities
- Caregiver's annual income did not exceed $8,000 from any trade, business, profession, vocation and / or employment in the previous year
- No one else has claimed GCR on the same caregiver. Relief is limited to 1 claim for 1 parent / grandparent i.e. a single claim of $3,000

# Sibling Relief (Disability)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/U3ip0GiR*

Provides tax relief to individuals supporting their siblings and siblings-in-law with disability.

## Highlights
- Claim up to $5,500 per dependant

**Who it targets:** Families, Persons with disabilities
**Keywords:** Dependents, PWDs, Tax relief

## About this support
Relief of $5,500 granted to individual for each sibling or sibling-in-law supported.

## Who is this for?
- To claim Sibling Relief (Disability), all of the following conditions must be met:
  - Dependant must have disability^ or mental impairment^^
  - Dependant lived / has been living with you (on a permanent basis) in the same household in Singapore
  - If they live in a separate household, you must have incurred $2,000 or more in supporting them
- No other type of relief has been claimed on the same dependant by someone else e.g. another family member
- If multiple claimants are supporting the same sibling or sibling-in-law and claim the Handicapped Brother / Sister Relief for them, it will be shared among the claimants

^ Certified by a doctor to require assistance in any of the 6 Activities of Daily Living (Washing or Bathing, Dressing, Feeding, Toileting, Transferring, Mobility).

^^ Certified by a doctor to be impaired in any of these 3 areas: Self Care and Activities of Daily Living, Compliance to Psychiatric Treatment, Education or Work.

## How to apply?
If you were previously approved for relief last year, the amount will be pre-filled and granted to you automatically. If you need to make changes to your relief, please refer to the below instructions for first-time applicants.

**For e-Filing**

If this is your first time claiming this relief:

- Log in with your Singpass or [Singpass Foreign user Account (SFA)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/digital-services/others/singpass-foreign-user-account-(sfa)-for-foreign-individuals) at [myTax Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/login/selection)
- Navigate to “Individuals” > “File Income Tax Return”
- Select“File" to File Income Tax Return
- Go to ““4. Deductions, Tax Reliefs and Rebates”
- Select "Add New" > “Sibling”
- Fill in the relevant information and select “Update”
- Email IRAS through [myTax Mail](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/login/selection) under myTaxPortal via Singpass login:
- Completed [Application for Claim of Disability Related Tax Reliefs](https://www.iras.gov.sg/media/docs/default-source/uploadedfiles/application-for-claim-of-disability-related-tax-reliefs.doc?sfvrsn=442cf660_28)
- Letter / supporting documents from the disability association / Special Education school in respect of your sibling, indicating details of their disabilities

**For paper filing**

- Complete the item on “Sibling Relief (Disability)” in Form B1 & B
- If this is your first time claiming the relief:
  - Fill in the details of your sibling/sibling-in-law in Appendix 2
  - Email IRAS through [myTax Mail](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/login/selection) under myTaxPortal via Singpass login:
  - Completed [Application for Claim of Disability Related Tax Reliefs](https://www.iras.gov.sg/media/docs/default-source/uploadedfiles/application-for-claim-of-disability-related-tax-reliefs.doc?sfvrsn=442cf660_28)
  - Letter / supporting documents from the disability association / Special Education school in respect of your sibling, indicating details of their disabilities

If you were eligible for the relief but no longer qualify, please withdraw the claim from your Income Tax Return if the relief has been auto-included.

[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.iras.gov.sg/contact-us/locate-us)

[Submit an enquiry](https://www.iras.gov.sg/contact-us/individual-income-tax)

highlights: Provides tax relief of up to $12,000
embedding_text:
Domains: Disability support, Financial support and benefits

# Earned Income Relief 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/oS6OeT45*

Provides tax relief for individuals who are gainfully employed or carrying on a trade, business, profession or vocation.

## Highlights
- Provides tax relief of up to $12,000 

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Employment Support and Vocational Training, Lower-income, PWDs

## About this support
- Receive tax relief of up to $8,000, depending on your age
- Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) are granted increased relief of up to $12,000

## Who is this for?
- You are employed / self-employed and have received taxable earned income from your employment, pension or trade / business / profession / vocation in the previous year
- To be considered eligible for higher relief, PWDs must have a permanent disability or mental impairment affecting work ability defined as follows:
  - Physical disability - requires assistance in any of the following 6 Activities of Daily Living (ADLs):
    - Washing or Bathing
    - Dressing
    - Feeding
    - Toileting
    - Transferring
    - Mobility
  - Mental disability - impaired in any of the following 3 activities:
    - Self Care and ADLs
    - Compliance to Psychiatric Treatment
    - Education or Work

## How to apply?
- The relief is granted automatically if you have taxable earned income
- If you are claiming Earned Income Relief (Disability) for the first time, please email the following via [myTax Mail](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/login/selection):
  - Completed Tax Relief Form - [Application for Claim of Disability - Related Tax Reliefs](https://www.iras.gov.sg/media/docs/default-source/uploadedfiles/application-for-claim-of-disability-related-tax-reliefs.doc?sfvrsn=442cf660_28)
  - Letter / supporting documents from the disability association, indicating details of the disabilities
  - Next, you must complete your Income Tax Return as follows:
  - If e-Filing, enter disability or mental impairment details under Section "4. Deductions, Reliefs and Parenthood Tax Rebate" > "Earned Income Relief"
    - If using paper filing, include handicap details in Appendix 2 of the Income Tax Form
- Once claimed, the relief will be granted automatically in subsequent years if you are eligible

[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.iras.gov.sg/contact-us/locate-us)

[View more details](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs/earned-income-relief)

# Qualifying Child Relief (QCR)/Child Relief (Disability)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/XPg2wTUs*

Provides tax relief to parents to recognise their efforts in supporting their children.

## Highlights
- Claim up to $7,500 per dependant
- Can be applied alongside the Working Mother’s Child Relief (WMCR) scheme for additional support 
- Parents may share the QCR / Child Relief (Disability)

**Who it targets:** Families, Persons with disabilities
**Keywords:** Dependents, Special education, Tax relief

## About this support
- QCR of $4,000 per qualifying child
- Child Relief (Disability) of $7,500 per child with disabilities
- Eligible working mothers can also apply for Working Mother's Child Relief (WMCR) in conjunction with the QCR / Child Relief (Disability) for additional support
- Parents may share the QCR / Child Relief (Disability) based on an agreed apportionment

## Who is this for?
**To be eligible for QCR, you must meet all the following conditions:**

During the previous year,

- Your child is unmarried and is either:
  - Born to you and your spouse / ex-spouse
  - A stepchild
  - Legally adopted
- Your child was either:
  - Below 16 years old
  - Above 16 years old and studying full-time at any university, college or other educational institution
- Your child did not have an annual income exceeding $8,000.

**To be eligible for Child Relief (Disability):**

- Your child must be unmarried / have been unmarried in the previous year and is either:
  - Born to you and your spouse / ex-spouse
  - A stepchild
  - Legally adopted
- Your child meets any of the following criteria:
  - Your child is certified by a doctor to require assistance in any of the 6 Activities of Daily Living:
    - Washing or Bathing
    - Dressing
    - Feeding
    - Toileting
    - Transferring
    - Mobility
  - Your child is certified by a doctor to be impaired in any of these 3 areas:
    - Self-Care and Activities of Daily Living
    - Compliance to Psychiatric Treatment
    - Education or Work
  - Your child is attending (or is recommended by a doctor to attend) a Special Education (SPED) school
  - Your child is not attending a SPED school but has significant special educational needs, resulting in severe functional impairments

** **

**Conditions related to claiming WMCR together with QCR / Child Relief (Disability):**

- The total claimable relief for QCR, Child Relief (Disability) and WMCR combined is capped at $50,000 per child
- When claiming both QCR / Child Relief (Disability) and WMCR, the QCR and Child Relief (Disability) claims will take precedence. WMCR claims will only be applied after.

## How to apply?
**Please refer to the following processes to apply for QCR:**

**For e-Filing**

- If claiming QCR for the first time, log in to [myTax Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/login/selection) using your Singpass or [Singpass Foreign user Account (SFA)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/digital-services/others/singpass-foreign-user-account-(sfa)-for-foreign-individuals)
- Navigate to "Individuals" > "File Income Tax Return"
- Select "File" to File Income Tax Return
- Go to "4. Deductions, Tax Reliefs and Rebates"
- Select “Add New” > “Child".
- Fill in the relevant information and select “Update”.
- If you were previously approved for relief last year, the amount will be pre-filled and granted to you automatically this year
- If you would like to make changes, please follow the above e-Filing process for first-time applicants

**For paper filing**

- Complete the "Child Relief" section in Form B1 & B
- Include your child's details in Appendix 2 if it's your first time claiming

**Please refer to the following processes to apply for Child Relief (Disability):**

For first-time Child Relief (Disability) claims, email 1 of the following documents via [myTax Mail](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/login/selection)

- Completed Tax Relief Form - [Application for Claim of Disability Related Tax Reliefs](https://www.iras.gov.sg/media/docs/default-source/uploadedfiles/application-for-claim-of-disability-related-tax-reliefs.doc?sfvrsn=442cf660_28)
- Letter / supporting documents from the disability association / SPED school in respect of your child, providing details of their disabilities, to IRAS

If your child is attending / has been recommended to attend a SPED school or has significant special education needs, please refer to the [“First-time Child Relief (Disability) claims” section on the Qualifying Child Relief (QCR)/Child Relief (Disability) page)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs/qualifying-child-relief-(qcr)-handicapped-child-relief-(hcr)) for more details.

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.iras.gov.sg/contact-us/locate-us)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs/qualifying-child-relief-(qcr)-child-relief-(disability))

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://www.iras.gov.sg/contact-us/individual-income-tax)

## Phone number
IRAS hotline: [1800-356-8300](tel:1800-356-8300)

Domains: Disability support, Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits, Healthcare and well-being

# Additional Premium Support for MediShield Life and CareShield Life  

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/1GKrS2tn*

Provides financial support for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents who are unable to afford their MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums (where applicable) even after Government subsidies and MediSave use and have limited family support.

## Highlights
- Financial aid for those who cannot afford premiums after subsidies and with insufficient MediSave, and have limited family support 
- Covers MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums (where applicable) for the next 2 policy years, as well as any outstanding premiums
- Open to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents living overseas 

**Who it targets:** Low-income
**Keywords:** Health Insurance, Lower-income, Subsidies

## About this support
Covers MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums (where applicable) for the next 2 policy years upon approval.

## Who is this for?
- Eligibility for APS is based on:
  - The financial means of the applicant and his/her immediate family members
- You will not be eligible for APS if you have sufficient MediSave to pay for your MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums or have purchased an Integrated Shield Plan and/or ElderShield/CareShield Life Supplements
- If you are granted APS and purchase an Integrated Shield Plan and/or ElderShield/CareShield Life Supplement afterwards, you will stop receiving APS

## How to apply?
- You will be invited to apply for APS if you have insufficient MediSave and have limited family support to help you pay for your MediShield Life premiums
- The invitation will include an application form with details on the application process, which must be submitted along with the relevant supporting documents
- There is no need for you to apply for APS ahead of time
- Applications may take up to 20 working days to be assessed, and applicants will receive a notification on the application outcome

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us)

Note: By appointment only

## Agency website
[View more details ](https://ask.gov.sg/moh?topic=MediShield Life&subtopic=Additional Premium Support#conte)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](mailto:aps@medishieldlife.sg)

## Phone number
Healthcare Hotline: [1800-222-3399](tel:1800-222-3399) 
For overseas callers: [+65 6222 3399](tel:62223399)

To avoid waiting on the line, you may [book an appointment](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/appt/oas/form).

# CPF Education Loan Scheme

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/3OUzHyMJ*

A loan scheme that allows CPF member to use their Ordinary Account (OA) savings to pay for their own, children’s, spouse’s, siblings' or relatives' government subsidised tuition fees for full-time diploma/degree courses at Approved Educational Institutions (AEIs).

## Highlights
- Allows for the use of OA savings to pay for the government subsidised tuition fees for full-time diploma/degree courses at Approved Educational Institutions (AEIs)
- Applications will only be processed after the application period for the approved educational institution has closed
- Processing of application generally takes 3 working days upon receipt of the student's enrolment confirmation from the approved educational institution

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** CPF, Education expenses, Students

## About this support
- Allows the use of OA savings to pay for own, children’s, spouse’s, siblings' or relatives' government subsidised tuition fees for [full-time diploma/degree courses at Approved Educational Institutions (AEIs)](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/what-courses-are-covered-by-the-cpf-education-loan-scheme)
- The student (i.e., borrower) would need to start repaying the principal amount withdrawn plus the accrued interest in cash, to the lender’s CPF OA, one year after graduating from or leaving the course of study, whichever occurs earlier

Note:

- OA savings can be used up to the Available Withdrawal Limit under the CPF Education Loan Scheme
- The Available Withdrawal Limit is either 40% of your accumulated OA savings, or your remaining OA balance, whichever is lower
- The amount that can be used is also subject to the tuition fees payable
- If you are 55 or older, you must set aside the Full Retirement Sum (FRS) in your Retirement Account before using the remaining OA savings, up to the Available Withdrawal Limit.
- You may wish to check how much tuition fees can be paid using [OA savings.](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/how-much-of-tuition-fees-can-be-paid-using-cpf-ordinary-account-oa-savings)

## Who is this for?
- CPF members/lenders with OA savings are eligible to pay for their own, children’s, spouse’s, or relative’s government subsidised tuition fees using OA savings, up to the Available Withdrawal Limit
- The Available Withdrawal Limit is up to 40% of accumulated OA savings, or the remaining OA balance, whichever is lower
- The CPF member can check the Available Withdrawal Limit through the CPF website using Singpass
- Only full-time diploma / degree courses at Approved Educational Institutions (AEIs) are covered under this loan scheme
- For the list of approved courses, you may refer to [approved courses under this scheme](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/what-courses-are-covered-by-the-cpf-education-loan-scheme)
- Here are the alternative education financing options:
  - [MOE Higher Education Student Loan](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/what-is-the-moe-higher-education-student-loan-hesl)
  - [Other financing options offered by the institutions](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/what-are-the-financing-options-from-moe-and-the-educational-institutions)
  - [Post-Secondary Education Account funds](https://www.moe.gov.sg/financial-matters/psea)

## How to apply?
- Apply online through [“Forms and e-applications"](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications) at [CPF website](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/apply-for-cpf-education-loan) with your Singpass
- You must read the accompanying Terms & Conditions, and Procedures & Guidelines before you complete the online form
- Before you submit your application online under the CPF Education Loan Scheme:
  - Check the application period for the approved educational institution you are applying to use CPF savings to pay your tuition fees
  - Ensure you are accepted by the institution and confirm that it is an approved educational institution under the CPF Education Loan Scheme
  - Establish whether you are a new (e.g. fresh intake for AY2024/2025) or existing student (e.g. 2nd year student) under the institution
- You are required to submit 1 (one) application form for each CPF lender, for the entire course of study, unless you enrol into a different AEI
- Please note the application period for use of CPF savings under CPF Education Loan Scheme differs for each AEI
- You may [refer to their schedules here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/apply-for-cpf-education-loan/application-schedule)

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us)

Note: By appointment only

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/sub-categories?category=P_M_OS)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/feedback)

## Phone number
CPFB Hotline: [1800-227-1188](tel:1800-227-1188)

# Youth COP

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-YC*

Aims to foster positive development and strengthen protective factors, empowering youths as crime-prevention leaders to help their communities thrive, stay safe, and build resilience.

**Who it targets:** Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Referral required, Youths at risk

## About this support
Youth COP is a 3-year developmental programme that empowers students to become confident, responsible crime-prevention leaders who help keep their peers and communities safe. In partnership with Neighbourhood Police Centres and selected schools, the programme develops youths into active contributors who serve, protect, and care for their community through meaningful engagement and public education efforts.

Through strong collaboration with families, schools, police, and the wider community, Youth COP equips students with leadership skills, crime-prevention knowledge, and opportunities to make a positive impact. As Crime Prevention Ambassadors, participants build a strong sense of identity and self-worth, gain the competencies to navigate life’s challenges, make informed decisions, and foster safer, more caring school and community environments.

## Who is this for?
The programme supports secondary school students in selected schools, with leadership potential by providing guidance, developmental opportunities, and the knowledge and skills to understand laws and their implications. Youth COP nurtures these young people into positive contributors within their schools and communities, grounded in the belief that all youths grow and thrive when supported with strong relationships, meaningful experiences, and opportunities to realise their potential.

## How to apply?
- Students can nominate themselves through the booths in school.
- Students can also be nominated for the programme through school personnel (e.g. teachers).

## What to expect?
- Programme staff will conduct a selection interview with the nominated student (by self or other school referral)  Students will be assessed for their risks, needs and suitability for this programme, within 2 to 3 weeks of referral or sign-up.
- In the event that student is not suitable for the programme, they will be given a letter to explain reasons for rejection and will be directed to other services based on the social worker's recommendations.

description: Offers literacy and behavioural intervention to support children aged 5 to 12 years old with learning difficulties.
embedding_text:
Domains: Education and learning

# Epworth Literacy and Behaviour Intervention

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/L6htu6Eh*

Offers literacy and behavioural intervention to support children aged 5 to 12 years old with learning difficulties.

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income
**Citizenship:** SG, OTHERS, PR
**Keywords:** Education, Fees payable

## About this support
Offers literacy and behavioural intervention to support children with literacy and behavioural challenges.

Services include:

- Literacy and/or language intervention - provides children between 5 to 12 years old with skills and strategies to overcome their learning challenges and develop literacy skills.
- Behavioural intervention - supports children between 5 to 12 years old in the aspects of essential executive functioning for learning, task readiness, on-seat behaviour, and basic social competency skills.
- Parenting workshops are also offered for parents to increase their knowledge in effective parenting and understanding the needs of their children.

## Who is this for?
Children aged between 5 - 12 years old (in pre-schools and mainstream schools) with learning difficulties assessed to be behind their same-aged peers in their literacy and/or language skills.

## How to apply?
You may contact the service provider directly for enquiries and to sign up for the programme.

## What to expect?
Epworth will screen to assess if the child is eligible and suitable for the programme.

# Large Families Scheme

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/Q1UpgN0i*

Provides more support for Singaporean families who have three or more children.

## Highlights
- Increased Child Development Account (CDA) First Step Grant to $10,000
- Large Family MediSave Grant of $5,000
- Large Family LifeSG Credits of $1,000 annually, during the years that the third and subsequent child turns 1 to 6 years old

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Budget 2025, Families, Parents

## About this support
The SG Child Support Package announced at the 2026 National Day Rally will replace the Baby Bonus Scheme and Large Families Scheme. The increased CDA First Step Grant for large families will cease from April 2027. As Child Credits will be given to all eligible children under the Package, Large Family LifeSG Credits will also cease, with no disbursements in 2027. More details on additional support for large families will be provided at a later date.

Learn more about the [SG Child Support Package](https://go.gov.sg/sgchildsupportpackage).

Families will receive additional support of up to $16,000 for each third and subsequent Singapore Citizen child, on top of existing Baby Bonus Scheme benefits.

**Child Development Account (CDA) First Step Grant**

- $10,000 CDA First Step Grant (increase from $5,000)
- For each third and subsequent Singapore Citizen child born on or after 18 February 2025
- Deposited into the eligible child's CDA within two weeks of CDA opening
- Can be used to defray approved preschool and healthcare expenses of the child and/or his/her siblings

**Large Family MediSave Grant**

- $5,000 Large Family MediSave Grant
- For each third and subsequent Singapore Citizen child born on or after 18 February 2025
- Deposited into the mother's MediSave account, following child's Baby Bonus enrolment
- Can be used to offset the mother’s pregnancy and delivery costs, or approved dependant's healthcare expenses

**Large Family LifeSG Credits**

- $1,000 annually in Large Family LifeSG Credits
- For each third and subsequent Singapore Citizen child, including those turning 1 to 6 years old in 2025
- Credits are disbursed to the CDA trustee of the child and accessible via LifeSG mobile app
- Can be used at any merchant that accepts payments using PayNow UEN QR or NETS QR, to defray household expenses
- Credits are valid for 12 months from disbursement, with the expiry date displayed in the LifeSG mobile app

## Who is this for?
Families with a third or subsequent Singapore Citizen child born on or after 18 February 2025 will receive:

- the increased CDA First Step Grant of $10,000,
- a $5,000 Large Family MediSave Grant, and
- $1,000 annually in Large Family LifeSG Credits during the years that the child turns 1 to 6 years old*.

*The Large Family LifeSG Credits also applies to existing large families with at least one child aged six or below.

## How to apply?
No application is required.

## Agency website
[View more details](http://go.gov.sg/LFS)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://www.msf.gov.sg/AskMSF)

## Phone number
Baby Bonus and Large Families Scheme hotline: [1800 111 2222](tel:18001112222)

# Child Development Account 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/CDAA*

Special savings account for the child, which can be used for approved areas of child-raising expenditure, including healthcare and preschool fees.

## Highlights
- CDA First Step Grant enhanced by $2,000 for eligible Singaporean children 
- Up to $15,000 in Government co-matching  for eligible Singaporean children
- Enhancements will apply to eligible Singaporean children born on or after 14 February 2023

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Budget 2023, Families

## About this support
The SG Child Support Package announced at the 2026 National Day Rally will replace the current Baby Bonus Scheme and Large Families Scheme. Those currently on the Baby Bonus Scheme will be automatically transitioned to the Package. In the meantime, existing payouts will continue as usual. 

Learn more about the [SG Child Support Package](https://go.gov.sg/sgchildsupportpackage).

The Child Development Account (CDA) is a special savings account for the child, which can be used for defray child-raising costs. The First Step Grant is automatically deposited after the CDA is opened, and subsequent savings will be co-matched by the Government, up to a cap.

Eligible Singaporean children born on or after 14 Feb 2023 will qualify for the following enhanced CDA benefits announced at Budget 2023.

**Child Development Account First Step Grant:**

- $5,000 automatically credited into the CDA upon account opening.

**Government co-matching of CDA savings:**

- Eligible Singaporean children are entitled to Government co-matching up to a cap of $4,000 for the first child, $7,000 for the second child, $9,000 for the third and fourth child, and $15,000 for the fifth child and beyond.

## Who is this for?
- Child is a Singapore Citizen
- Children born on or after 14 Feb 2023
- Parents are lawfully married
- Children of unwed parents may be eligible for CDA benefits if they are born on or after 1 September 2016.

## How to apply?
All parents can apply for Baby Bonus Scheme at LifeSG:

- [Bundled service](https://www.life.gov.sg/services/birth-registration) together with child’s birth registration
- [Direct application](https://www.life.gov.sg/services/baby-bonus) for child who has already registered for birth

**Keywords:** Education, Mentoring

The programme core services includes

- 1-1 mentoring

- Family bonding activities

Singapore citizens/ Singapore PRs aged 6 – 13 years old from vulnerable backgrounds (e.g. ComLink+ families, parental incarceration, referral from school counsellors).

Children aged 7 to 12 years (in mainstream schools) with learning difficulties.

The centre will conduct an intake assessment and consultation session with the child to better understand their needs and discuss follow up support and suitability for the programme.

# The Builders Project

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-TBP*

Aims to increase social capital and social discipline, and accomplish positive outcomes in Primary 4-6 school children who have been assessed to have higher needs.

**Who it targets:** Families
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Referral required, Social-emotional Support

## About this support
The Builders Project is an early intervention programme targeting Primary 4-5 school children that aims to promote positive school climate and culture that are conducive for achieving social capital and social discipline. The programme works with the parents and teachers of the identified students which leads to better school outcomes such as lower chronic school absenteeism, premature withdrawal from school and other adolescent risk behaviours.

## Who is this for?
P4 to P6 children who:

- Are in mainstream primary schools
- Have been assessed to have higher need

## How to apply?
- Schools will refer students to the programme.

## What to expect?
- The one year programme is available in selected partner schools.
- Lutheran Community Care Services (LCCS) will administer a pre-screening tool to students referred by teachers and social workers.
- Based on the results, LCCS and teachers will jointly decide on the identified students who are suitable for further support.

# Halogen SPARK!

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-HS*

A structured evidence-based entrepreneurship curriculum that targets Secondary 3 students who are from the G1/G2 Subject Based Banding (SBB) Stream that improves better school-focused outcomes, including their attendance and academic performance.

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Referral required

## About this support
Halogen SPARK! is an upstream intervention programme that targets Secondary students who are from the G1/G2 SBB stream. It targets pre/low/mid-risk students from the Financial Assistance Scheme (FAS) and/or come from challenging and disadvantaged backgrounds.

The programme is a structured evidence-based programme developed by NFTE (Network for Teaching Entrepreneurship), where the key objectives are to increase service users' social-emotional and academic competencies through the incorporation of English and Math in the programme curriculum. It supports the development of numeracy and literacy skills through the entrepreneurship modules, and aims to instill self-confidence and self-efficacy in youths.

## Who is this for?
Secondary 3 students who are from the G1/G2 Subject Based Banding (SBB) stream

## How to apply?
- Schools will refer the students to the programme at the start of the calendar year.
- Halogen SPARK! and teachers will jointly decide on the identified students on their service eligibility.

## What to expect?
- The one year programme is available in selected partner schools.
- Halogen SPARK! will conduct a pre-programme survey for all enrolled students for the purpose of further adjustments to the programmes depending on the student demographics.

# The Scaffold Programme

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-TSP*

Supports Secondary 1 and 2 students, who have been identified to have higher needs, including socio-emotional and behavioural difficulties, at risk of delinquency, and observed to have low school connectedness.

**Who it targets:** Families, Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Referral required

## About this support
The Scaffold Programme (TSP) is an upstream, early intervention programme that supports lower secondary school students in mainstream schools, who are predisposed to latent risk factors or premature withdrawal from school.

TSP aims to provide quality school social work intervention for students and their ecosystems that lead to improved school outcomes, reduced referrals to downstream programmes, improvement in parent-child relationships and school-student attachment.

## Who is this for?
Secondary 1 and 2 students who have been identified to have higher needs including:

- Socio-emotional and behavioural difficulties
- At risk of delinquency
- Observed to have low school connectedness

## How to apply?
The programme adopts a class-based design – i.e. school teachers will identify and refer suitable classes to join the programme at the start of the calendar year.

## What to expect?
- The one year programme is available in selected partner schools
- Agency will have a discussion with relevant school personnel on the needs of the classes
- The agency will then customise the service component to address the unique needs of the class

# Youth GO! Programme

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/YOUTH-GO*

An engagement and intervention programme for youths who may benefit from additional support (aged 12-21) that helps them stay focused in their studies/work, remain crime-free, develop problem-solving skills and be resilient.

**Who it targets:** Families
**Citizenship:** SG, PR
**Keywords:** Referral required, Youths at risk

## About this support
- Youth GO! is an engagement and intervention programme that supports youths who may benefit from additional support.
- Its objectives are to help youths who may benefit from additional support be meaningfully engaged in their studies or work, stay crime-free, develop problem-solving skills and be resilient individuals.

## Who is this for?
Youths who:

- are Singapore Citizens/Permanent Residents (PR)
- are between 12 - 21 years old
- Diplay the following:
  - Pro-criminal attitude/behaviour;
  - Physically/verbally aggressive behaviour; and/or
  - Subject to negative peer influence

Youths who had completed the Guidance Programme (GP), Streetwise Programme (SWP), Youth Enhanced Supervision (YES) and/probation but require further support, and youths who are out-of-school and not engaged in meaningful work, can be eligible for the YGP, subject to meeting the above criteria.

## How to apply?
- Referrals can be made by contacting the respective Youth GO! service provider according to the region of the youth's residential address or the hotspot area.
- Please refer to [Youth GO! Programme webpage](https://www.msf.gov.sg/what-we-do/help-those-in-need/article/programmes/Youth-GO-Programme) for information on the regions served by the different service providers, and their contact information.

## What to expect?
- For hotspot referrals, Youth GO! workers will work towards befriending the youth to assess if they fit the criteria of the target clientele.
- Where referrals are successful, Youth GO! workers will continue to engage the youth and conduct casework and intervention through positive engagement activities and case counselling sessions.

# Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/2TFgSkxq*

Provides educational financial support for eligible Singapore Citizens' post-secondary education.

## Highlights
- Funds can be used for approved programmes, repay government loans, and financial schemes
- No application needed

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Education, Education expenses, Students

## About this support
- PSEA Funds can be used to pay:
  - one's own or siblings’ approved education programmes at approved institutions
  - government education loans and financial schemes
- PSEA balances earn interest at the same rate as the CPF Ordinary Account (CPF-OA), currently 2.5% per annum
- Unused PSEA funds will be transferred to the CPF-OA when the account holder turns 31, subject to CPF-OA usage rules

## Who is this for?
- You must be a Singapore Citizen with a balance in either:
  - the Child Development Account (CDA) when it is closed
  - the Edusave Account when turning 17 years old or is no longer studying in a Ministry of Education (MOE)-funded school, whichever is later
- The PSEA will also be opened for Singapore Citizens who are:
  - eligible for PSEA top-ups by the Government
  - recipient of the first payment of the National Service Housing, Medical and Education (NS HOME) Awards
  - recipient of the annual education bursary under the Home Ownership Plus Education (HOPE) Scheme

## How to apply?
No application required.

## Where to go
[MOE Customer Service Centre, 1 North Buona Vista Drive MOE Building, Podium Block Singapore 138675](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=138675)

Note: By appointment only.

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.moe.gov.sg/financial-matters/psea)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](mailto:MOE_PSEA@moe.gov.sg)

## Phone number
MOE Hotline:[6872 2220](tel:68722220)

# MUIS Zakat Financial Assistance

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/MUIS-FAS*

Provides monthly financial assistance and support in other forms to eligible low-income Muslim households.

## Highlights
- Monthly financial assistance for eligible individuals 
- Support for emergency needs and burial expenses 
- Study grants and food vouchers available 
- Assessment based on Per Capita Income of $500 or lower for eligibility 

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income
**Keywords:** Lower-income, Resources and Support

## About this support
Potential benefits include:

- Monthly financial support: Dependent on Per Capita Income (PCI) criteria
- Settlement of debt: One-time settlement of arrears for basic necessities (utility and conservancy charges)
- Emergency assistance: Renders emergency assistance in times of crisis such as natural disasters, fire, or accidents
- Burial expenses: Covers burial expenses incurred upon death of a Zakat beneficiary and their immediate family members
- Study grants: Subsidies for national examinations mosque-based part-time Islamic education, and low-income students with special needs
- Fidyah food vouchers: To purchase food supplies at approved Fidyah retailers islandwide

## Who is this for?
- Available to Muslim Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents
- Per Capita Income (PCI) must be $500 or lower to qualify
- Applicants will undergo an assessment interview with a Social Development Officer (SDO) at the nearest Social Development (SD) mosque
- Required documents: NRIC, birth certificate, income and bank documents, and other relevant supporting documents
- Outcome notified by mail within up to 6 weeks

## How to apply?
- Call a Social Development (SD) mosque closest to your home for an appointment.
- Schedule an assessment interview with an SDO.
- During the interview, please prepare to bring your personal identification documents, such as NRIC and birth certificate, income and bank documents (payslips, CPF statements, bank books etc.), and other relevant supporting documents (bills, medical memos, referral letters etc.) to help verify your application

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest SD mosque](https://www.zakat.sg/how-to-apply-zakat/)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.zakat.sg/zakat-assistance/)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](mailto: info@muis.gov.sg)

## Phone number
MUIS Hotline: [6359 1199](tel:63591199)

Domains: Active Ageing, Education and learning, Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits, Financial/Retirement Planning, Work and employment

# SkillsFuture Credit

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/SKILLSFUTURE_CREDITS*

For Singapore Citizens aged 25 and above to pay for or offset the out-of-pocket course fees of approved courses.

## Highlights
- SkillsFuture Credits can be used on top of existing SWDA course fee subsidies
- Submit your claim via MySkillsFuture within 60 days before course starts
- No application required

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Courses, Trainings

## About this support
- Singapore Citizens aged 25 and above will receive an opening credit of S$500. Opening credits will not expire.
- A one-off SkillsFuture Credit top-up of $500 was provided to every Singapore Citizen aged 25 and above as at 31 December 2020. These credits will expire on 31 December 2025.
- Can be used on top of existing government course subsidies to pay for a wide range of approved skills-related courses, such as:
  - Courses subsidised or approved by SkillsFuture Singapore including online courses
  - Selected courses offered by Ministry of Education (MOE)-funded institutions
  - Courses supported by lead agencies
  - SkillsFuture@PA courses offered by the People’s Association and selected courses under National Silver Academy

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizen
- Aged 25 and above

## How to apply?
- No application required
- How to use your SkillsFuture Credit:
  - Step 1: Inform your Training Provider that you intend to use your SkillsFuture Credit in part or in full for the qualifying course fees at the point of course registration

# SkillsFuture Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/SFMCES*

Provides up to 90% subsidy on course fees for Singapore Citizens aged 40 and above.

## Highlights
- Up to 90% subsidy on course fees for Singapore Citizens aged 40 and above 
- At least 90% subsidy on programme costs for MOE-subsidised courses at institutions like Autonomous Universities, Polytechnics, and ITE 

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Mid-career, Trainings

## About this support
- Up to 90% subsidy on course fees for courses offered by Skills & Workforce Development Agency (SWDA)-appointed Continuing Education and Training (CET) Centres
- At least 90% subsidy on programme costs for Ministry of Education (MOE)-subsidised full-time and part-time courses at institutions like Autonomous Universities, Polytechnics, and the Institute of Technical Education
- For certifiable-skills training courses, up to 70% subsidy on course fees

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizen
- Aged 40 and above
- Qualifies for the Ministry of Education (MOE)/Skills & Workforce Development Agency (SWDA) base course fee subsidy

## How to apply?
- Enrol in a course that is supported by Skills & Workforce Development Agency (SWDA) or offered by one of the following institutions:
  - Autonomous Universities (AU):
    - National University of Singapore (NUS)
    - Nanyang Technological University (NTU)
    - Singapore Management University (SMU)
    - Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD)
    - Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT)
    - Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS)
  - Polytechnics
  - Institute of Technical Education (ITE)
  - LASALLE College of the Arts and Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts (NAFA)
  - National Institute of Early Childhood Development (NIEC)
- Ensure the course is eligible for MOE/SSG base course fee subsidy
  - The enhanced subsidy will be applied automatically at the point of enrolment if you are eligible

# Singapore Workforce Skills Qualifications

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/SGWSQ*

A national credential system that trains, develops, assesses and certifies skills and competencies for the workforce.

## Highlights
- WSQ is a national credential system for skills and competencies certification
- No academic prerequisites required for entry, recognises prior work experience and credentials

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Jobseekers, Mid-career, Trainings

## About this support
- Acquire job role-specific skills and competencies through competency-based training
- Gain portable credentials to improve employability and mobility
- Access to bite-sized modules leading to Statements of Attainment and full WSQ qualifications
- Quality assured qualifications awarded by Skills & Workforce Development Agency (SWDA) or in partnership with established awarding bodies

## Who is this for?
- Open to all individuals, regardless of academic background
- Recognises prior learning and work experience

## How to apply?
To enrol in Workforce Skills Qualifications (WSQ) courses:

- Visit the [MySkillsFuture portal](https://www.myskillsfuture.gov.sg/content/portal/en/index.html) to browse available WSQ courses
- Register for the course through the training provider
- Complete the course to receive a Statement of Attainment or WSQ qualification

Domains: Education and learning, Financial support and benefits, Work and employment

# Workfare Skills Support (Level-Up)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/L0DUZZzA*

Enhanced tier of Workfare Skills Support (WSS), supporting lower-wage Singaporean workers who go for long-form training.

## Highlights
- Provides training allowance  of at least $300 per month
- Covers a wide catalogue of long-form courses (including Nitec, Higher Nitec, Diplomas, Post-Diplomas, and Undergraduate courses)
- Covers multiple bouts of long-form training
- Apply online via the Training Allowance System using Singpass

**Who it targets:** Low-income
**Keywords:** Budget 2025, Lower-wage workers, Trainings

## About this support
**Training Allowance (TA)**

- Full-time training: 50% of average income over the latest available 12-month period, with minimum allowance of $300 per month
- Part-time training: $300 per month

**Coverage for multiple rounds of long-form training**

Every individual can receive:

- Up to 24 months of monthly TA between ages 30 to 39
- Up to another 24 months of monthly TA from age 40. This is a shared cap between WSS (Level-Up) and the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme
- For each age period, the cap is shared between both full-time and part-time training

**Courses supported include:**

- SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme courses
- Nitec, Higher Nitec, Diplomas, Post-Diplomas, and Undergraduate courses by Institutes of Higher Learning
- From 2026 Q4, long-form Workforce Skills Qualifications (WSQ) full qualifications

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizen;
- At least 30 years old or older as of 31 December of the preceding year, or at least 13 years old for persons with disabilities;
- Earn an average gross monthly income of not more than $3,000 for the past 12 months;
- Have declared your net trade income and made MediSave contributions in full if you are self-employed;
- Live in a property with an annual value of $21,000 and below as at 31 December of the preceding year;
- Own not more than one property; and
- If you are married:
  - you and your spouse together not own more than one property; and
  - the assessable income of your spouse does not exceed $70,000 of the preceding Year of Assessment

The above is similar to the [**Workfare Income Supplement**](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/growing-your-savings/government-support/workfare-income-supplement) (WIS) criteria.

## How to apply?
You can apply online via the [Training Allowance System (TAS)](https://go.gov.sg/wss-level-up-tas)** **using your Singpass.

[View more details](https://go.gov.sg/wss-level-up)

Domains: Education and learning, Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits

# MOE Higher Education Student Loan (HESL) Scheme

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/jduPoSEk*

Loan scheme to help students who are taking MOE-subsidised diploma, undergraduate or postgraduate programmes in publicly-funded post-secondary education institutions to finance their tuition fees and borrow a living allowance loan for other education-related expenses. It also helps undergraduates to finance cost of institution-approved overseas student programme.

## Highlights
- Base provision and means-tested balance fee coverage components under the HESL scheme can cover up to 100% of subsidised tuition fees for eligible Singapore Citizen (SC) students
- Eligible students who meet the income eligibility criteria can also apply for a living allowance loan component under the HESL scheme to cover their education expenses 
- Loan is interest-free during the course of study; interest and repayment commence upon a student’s graduation or leaving the institution

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Education expenses, Students

## About this support
For Diploma students
There are two loan components under HESL:
(i)     Base provision to cover up to 90% of subsidised tuition fees payable, depending on the student’s citizenship;
(ii)   Means-tested provisions
·  Loan to cover remaining 10% of subsidised tuition fees (for SC only)
·  Living allowance loan of up to $3,200 per academic year
For Undergraduate and Postgraduate students
There are two loan components under HESL:
(i)     Base provision to cover up to 90% of subsidised tuition fees payable, depending on the student’s citizenship;
(ii)   Means-tested provisions
· Loan to cover remaining 10% of subsidised tuition fees (for SC undergraduates only)
· Living allowance loan of up to $4,100 per academic year (for full-time undergraduate students only)
· Loan to cover up to $12,000 for the cost of one institution-approved overseas student programme (for full-time SC undergraduates only)

## Who is this for?
The HESL will be available to the following students, and the loan components available will depend on the student’s citizenship and level of study:

- SC, Singapore Permanent Resident (PR) and international student (IS) studying full-time MOE-subsidised diploma courses in any of the local polytechnics.
- SC and PR studying full-time MOE-subsidised diploma courses in Institute of Technical Education (ITE).
- SC and PR studying full-time MOE-subsidised diploma and undergraduate programmes in LASALLE College of the Arts (LASALLE), Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts (NAFA) and University of the Arts Singapore (UAS).
- SC, PR and IS studying full-time MOE-subsidised undergraduate, full-time MOE-subsidised postgraduate by coursework, and full-time/part-time MOE-subsidised postgraduate by research programmes in autonomous universities.
- SC studying part-time MOE-subsidised undergraduate programmes in autonomous universities.

Depending on the level of study and type of institution, the means-tested loan provisions are for:

- SC and PR with gross monthly household per capita income (PCI)^ of $3,500 or less.
- IS with gross monthly household PCI of $1,875 or less.

^Monthly PCI is computed based on total monthly gross household income (GHI) divided by number of family members living in the same household.

## How to apply?
- The following students can apply for HESL via the new [StudentLoanSG (SLSG)](https://go.gov.sg/slsg) portal from July 2026.
  - Newly matriculated students in Academic Year (AY) 2026 intake; and
  - Existing students (before AY2026 intake) who do not have Tuition Fee Loan (TFL) and Study Loan (SL) for their current course of study.
- Refer to the respective institution website for details on application window period and application procedures.
- Existing students who have already taken up TFL and/or SL will continue to receive their current loan provision.  No action is required from them.  However, if they wish to apply for new or additional loan provision under the HESL scheme, they should first approach their institution for advice and assessment of needs.

## Where to go
[Customer Service Centre](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=138675)
[1 North Buona Vista Drive](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=138675)
[MOE Building, Podium Block](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=138675)
[Singapore 138675](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=138675)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.moe.gov.sg/financial-matters/government-loan-schemes)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://www.moe.gov.sg/feedback)

Domains: Education and learning, Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits

# Student Care Fee Assistance (SCFA)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/SCFA*

Provides fee assistance for children from lower-income working families enrolled in Student Care Centres (SCCs) registered with MSF.

## Highlights
- Subsidies of up to $290 per month for children enrolled in SCCs , and co-payments from $11 per month for children enrolled in Special SCCs (SSCCs)
- One-time Start-Up Grant (SUG) of up to $400 per child
- Child must attend an SCC registered with MSF

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income
**Keywords:** Budget 2026, Students, Subsidies

## About this support
- For children attending SCCs aged 7 to 14 years old (Primary 1 to Secondary 2) in the calendar year in which subsidies commence, the subsidy is up to $290 per month, depending on your monthly household income.
- For children attending SSCCs aged 7 to 18 years old in the calendar year in which subsidies commence, the out-of-pocket amount from $11 per month, depending on your monthly household income. Please visit the [Enabling Guide by SG Enable](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/child-adult-care/special-student-care-centres) for more information on the subsidies.
