## Who is this for?
- Child is a Singapore Citizen or a Permanent Resident (at least one immediate family member in the same household must be a Singapore Citizen)
- Both you and your spouse are each working at least 56 hours a month
- Child must attend a Student Care Centre registered with MSF
- For children attending SCCs aged 7 to 14 years old (Primary 1 to Secondary 2) in the calendar year in which subsidies commence, the monthly gross household income must be $4,500 or less for families with 4 or fewer members, or monthly household income per capita must be $1,125 or less for families with 5 or more members. From January 2027: The monthly gross household income must be $6,500 or less, or monthly household income per capita must be $1,625 or less.
  For children attending SSCCs aged 7 to 18 years old in the calendar year in which subsidies commence, the monthly gross household income must be $9,200 or less for families with 4 or fewer members, or monthly household income per capita must be $2,300 or less for families with 5 more members. Please visit [Enabling Guide by SG Enable](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/child-adult-care/special-student-care-centres) for more information on the subsidies.

**How Income is Calculated**

- For salaried employees:
Based on average gross monthly income over 12 months from CPF records or the latest IRAS assessment (within the last 2 years).
Includes: basic salary, bonuses, commissions, overtime pay, allowances, cash rewards, and employee CPF contributions.
- For self-employed individuals:
Based on average trade income over 12 months from the latest IRAS assessment (within the last 2 years), or income declared to CPF Board.

**Note:** Family members refer to the child’s grandparents or siblings below 21 years old who live at the same address, are not working or have no income, and are Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents.

Your gross monthly income will be determined via HOMES as part of the means-test.

For further information, please refer to [MSF | Student Care Fee Assistance](https://www.msf.gov.sg/what-we-do/student-care/for-parents/student-care-fee-assistance).

## How to apply?
All SCFA applications must be submitted online via [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/scfa)  at least six months before the intended start date. For example, if you wish to apply for SCFA effective from January 2027, you may submit the application from July 2026 onwards. SCFA approval will commence from the month in which the application is received, or from the month following the expiry of any existing SCFA, whichever is later.

[Click here to learn more about the SCFA application process.](https://www.msf.gov.sg/docs/default-source/student-care/scfa-infographic---application-process.pdf)

- If you're unemployed or looking for work, you will need to provide supporting documents (for example, proof of job search, medical letter, or medical certificate).
- With the SCFA, if you still face difficulties with the monthly co-payment of your child's student care fees, you may submit an appeal through the SCC, along with supporting documents detailing the change in circumstances and an explanation of the reasons for the appeal. Appeals will be considered on a case-by-case basis, and if approved, will commence from the month when the appeal was submitted

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.msf.gov.sg/what-we-do/student-care/for-parents/student-care-fee-assistance)

## Email / Form
[MSF_Comcare_SCFA@msf.gov.sg](mailto:MSF_Comcare_SCFA@msf.gov.sg)

## Phone number
ComCare hotline: [1800 222 0000](tel:18001112222)

Operating hours: Monday to Sunday, 7am to 12 midnight

Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines in Singapore.

# SkillsFuture Advice

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/SKILLSFUTURE-ADVICE*

A webinar that helps you learn about SkillsFuture programmes, MySkillsFuture portal and funding support.

## Highlights
- 1-hour webinar

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Jobseekers, Webinars, Workers

## About this support
Free 1-hour webinars that will guide you in developing your resilience and upskilling plans through practical information and online resources:

- Understand your resilience and find learning programmes/initiatives that suit your needs
- Learn practical tips on developing your resilience mindset, building a circle of social support and improving your employability by planning for the future
- Learn about SkillsFuture programmes, including SkillsFuture Credit, funding support to offset your course fees, as well as, government support schemes (SGUnited jobs and COVID-19 support grant) to help you ride through the tough times
- Get an introduction to the MySkillsFuture portal that will help you in your career and learning development
- Discover courses to help you transit into available job roles and a glimpse into the hiring sectors

## Who is this for?
All Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents

## How to apply?
- You can [sign up online](https://form.gov.sg/#!/60dde90a22fd030012f32901).
- You may also access [online resources](https://www.myskillsfuture.gov.sg/content/portal/en/career-resources/career-resources.html?type=education-career-personal-development) to guide you in your skill development.

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/SFDWP*

## Highlights
- Develop a deep understanding of critical digital competencies for the evolving economy
- Safely navigate technology-rich environments with cybersecurity awareness
- Master various digital tools, including nationally recognized platforms, for strategic data utilization

- Navigate technology-rich environments with awareness of cybersecurity risks, ensuring secure work practices

# SkillsFuture Mid-Career Training Allowance

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/SF-MID-CAREER-TA*

Supports both full-time and part-time long-form training for Singapore Citizens aged 40 and above to upskill and reskill. Individuals can decide which type of training best suits their needs.

## Highlights
- Training Allowance (TA) of up to $3,000 per month for full-time training, and a flat rate of $300 per month for part-time training
- Up to 24 months of TA for each individual throughout their lifetime

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Budget 2026, Mid-career

## About this support
- Training Allowance (TA) for full-time, long-form training
  - 50% of an individual's average earned monthly income in the latest 12 months before course start date, with a minimum allowance of $300 and a maximum allowance of $3,000 per month
  - Eligible for individuals who enrol in selected full-time, long-form training programmes
  - Eligible for individuals with income in the latest 12 months before course start date
- TA for part-time, long-form training
  - Flat rate of $300 per month
  - Eligible for employed individuals who enrol in selected part-time, long-form training programmes

## Who is this for?
Singapore Citizen aged 40 and above pursuing selected full-time and part-time long-form training programmes

[Visit MySkillsFuture Website](https://www.myskillsfuture.gov.sg/)

# MyCareersFuture 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/tmyOMyke*

The one-stop portal for job search and application needs. It uses Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) to help jobseekers discover career opportunities, make career transitions, or search for jobs based on skills matches.  It also provides valuable career-related resources, including career insights and career guidance to facilitate their career planning and career development processes.

## Highlights
- Our latest Job-to-Skills job matching algorithm connects you with opportunities tailored to your skills and experience.
- Utilise CareersFinder to discover personalised upskilling and career recommendations based on your unique profile.
- Filter jobs eligible for Government support such as Career Conversion Programmes, Graduate Industry Traineeships (GRIT) Programme and Mid-Career Pathways Programmes
- Elevate your skills with our curated articles, webinars, and courses designed for your professional growth.

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Employment Support and Vocational Training, Jobseekers

## About this support
- **Advanced Matching Algorithm: **Our latest Job-to-Skills job matching algorithm connects you with opportunities tailored to your skills and experience.
- **CareersFinder by MyCareersFuture: **[CareersFinder](https://careersfinder.mycareersfuture.gov.sg/) harnesses Government data and artificial intelligence to help individuals discover personalised upskilling and career recommendations based on their unique profile to achieve their career goals.
- **Government Support Eligibility: **Filter jobs eligible for Government support such as:
  - Career Conversion Programmes (CCP) if you are open to reskill and change career/occupations
  - GRaduate Industry and Traineeship Programme (GRIT) if you are a fresh graduate looking for a traineeship opportunity, and
  - Mid-Career Pathways Programmes (MCPP) if you are a mature individual looking for a mid-career attachments.
- **CareersCompass by MyCareersFuture:** Access curated articles, career guides and expert insights to help you navigate career planning, skills development and job search strategies.
- **CareersHorizon by MyCareersFuture: **A one-stop digital platform for career-related event registrations and management. It enables Singaporeans to access a comprehensive suite of career resources, including online articles, virtual career events, seminars, and workshops. The platform also offers micro-learning content, such as podcasts, covering topics relevant to all career stages. Additionally, it supports Singaporeans in searching and registering for career events, and it also facilitates networking opportunities between employers and individuals.

## Who is this for?
Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents who are looking to plan their careers, make career transitions, or search for jobs.

Embark on your journey to professional success with [MyCareersFuture](https://www.mycareersfuture.gov.sg/).

# The GRIT Academy

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/VG22AnYD*

Mentoring programme for youths-at-risk in Jurong.

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Free

## About this support
The GRIT Academy (TGA) aims to provide individual mentoring support for youths-at-risk aged between 11 to 17 years old residing or studying in schools in Jurong; and serve as the primary relationship holder to follow through with the youths as they transit to other youth programmes.

## Who is this for?
The target clientele is youths-at-risk aged between 11 to 17 years old residing or studying in schools in Jurong (i.e. Jurong West, Jurong East and Taman Jurong).

Applicants must fulfil at least one of the following criteria to be eligible for the programme:

1. Youths who lack meaningful engagements such as those not attending Co-Curricular Activities, as well as youths who often loiter at public areas such as playgrounds and void decks.
2. Youths with underprivileged background such as youths from low-income families, students receiving the MOE Financial Assistance Scheme and youths staying in rental flats.
3. Youths exhibiting at-risk behaviour such as poor affiliation to schools, minor behavioural issues, socio-emotional issues and/or peer issues.

## How to apply?
Complete the form on https://lakeside.org.sg/our-services/the-grit-project/ and email it to [thegritproject@lakeside.org.sg](mailto:thegritproject@lakeside.org.sg).

## What to expect?
Screening for potential service users will take approximately 2 weeks from the referral/youth sign-up. Adjustment to the screening time frame will be considered based on the assessed urgency.

# Infant and Childcare Subsidies

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/INFANT-CHILD-CARE*

Provides tiered subsidies to help cover infant care and childcare fees for Singapore Citizen children from different income backgrounds.

## Highlights
- Working applicants: Basic Subsidy of $600 for infant care and $300 for childcare
- Non-working applicants: Basic Subsidy of $150 for infant care and childcare
- Additional Subsidy for working applicants

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Child care, Infant care, Subsidies

## About this support
**Working applicants (mother or single father who works at least 56 hours per month)**

- Basic Subsidy of $600 for infant care and $300 for childcare
- Additional Subsidy of up to $710 for infant care and up to $467 for childcare

**Non-working applicants**

- Basic Subsidy of $150 for infant care and childcare
- Eligible applicants who are not working or who are non-parent caregivers can apply for Special Approval to receive the higher Basic Subsidy and Additional Subsidy that working applicants receive

## Who is this for?
Types of subsidies
Eligibility criteria
For all subsidies
- Child must be a Singapore Citizen
- Enrolled in an infant care or childcare centre licensed by ECDA
Additional Subsidy
- Working applicants (mother or single father who works at least 56 hours per month)
- Monthly household income of up to $12,000, or monthly household income per capita of up to $3,000 for larger families with 5 or more family members in the same household
  - From 1 January 2027, monthly household income thresholds will be raised to $15,000, or $3,400 per capita
Special Approval
- Main subsidy applicants who are not working due to the following reasons:
  - Looking for a job
  - Studying, training, or on course for at least 56 hours a month
  - Pregnancy
  - Medically unfit for work due to hospitalisation, long-term illness and/or permanent disability
  - Taking care of a special needs child
  - Taking care of a sick family member who requires a full-time caregiver
  - Caring full-time for a younger child aged 24 months and below who is not enrolled in a preschool
  - Incarcerated
  - Non-parent caregivers who are caring for the child such as grandparents, legal guardian, foster parents, and head of a children’s home
- Families who are tenants of a rental flat under the HDB’s Public Rental Scheme or are beneficiaries of ComCare Short-To-Medium-Term Assistance (SMTA) or Long-Term-Assistance (LTA) will automatically qualify for maximum preschool subsidies upon application for Special Approval

## How to apply?
Refer to Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) [website](https://www.ecda.gov.sg/parents/preschool-subsidies/how-to-apply-or-make-changes-to-subsidies) to apply or make changes to subsidies

## Where to go

- Subsidy amount depends on monthly household income, and will be directly disbursed to the child's kindergarten
- Eligible applicants will receive a yearly KiFAS SUG capped at $240 per year to help cover initial costs such as registration fee, deposit, school uniform, insurance, and educational material fees, in addition to the basic subsidies

## Who is this for?
- Child must be a Singapore Citizen
- Enrolled in an Anchor Operator or Ministry of Education Kindergarten
- Monthly household income of up to $12,000, or monthly household income per capita of up to $3,000 for larger families with 5 or more family members in the same household
  - From 1 January 2027, monthly household income thresholds will be raised to $15,000, or $3,400 per capita
- Yearly SUG:
  - Applicants with monthly household income of up to $1,900, or monthly household income per capita of up to $650 for larger families with 5 or more family members in the same household, can further apply for SUG
  - Each application is assessed on a case-by-case basis

## How to apply?
Refer to Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) [website](https://www.ecda.gov.sg/parents/preschool-subsidies/how-to-apply-or-make-changes-to-subsidies/subsidy-application-for-new-preschool-enrolment) on steps on how to apply for subsidies

# Edusave Account

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/EDUSAVE-ACC*

Provides $230 to $290 annually for approved fees and programmes for every Singapore Citizen child, aged 7 to 16 or studying in a primary or secondary school. Ad-hoc top-ups may be made by the Government to the child’s Edusave account periodically.

## Highlights
- Receive annual contributions of $230 to $290 for all eligible Singapore Citizen children 
- No application needed 

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Education, Students

## About this support
- Annual contributions to Edusave accounts for primary school students: $230
- Annual contributions to Edusave accounts for secondary school students: $290
- Funds can be used for approved school enrichment programs, miscellaneous fees, approved educational activities and personal learning devices / assistive devices.
- Edusave account balances earn interest at a rate pegged to the CPF Ordinary Account (CPF-OA), currently at 2.5%

## Who is this for?
- You must be a Singapore Citizen child, either aged 7 to 16 years old or enrolled in a Ministry of Education (MOE)-funded primary / secondary school
- Junior college and Millennia Institute students do not receive annual contributions but can use remaining Edusave funds

## How to apply?
No application required.

## Where to go
[MOE Customer Service Centre 1 North Buona Vista Drive MOE Building, Podium Block Singapore 138675](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=138675)

# Voluntary Housing Refund 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/Z9jTRTTL*

Allows you to return any CPF savings used for your home purchase to your CPF account while still owning your property. Doing so reduces the refund amount you would have to make and increases the cash proceeds you would get when you eventually sell or transfer your property. This also boosts your retirement savings as you can benefit from CPF interest rates.

## Highlights
- Grow your retirement savings with CPF interest rates
- Greater cash proceeds and lower required CPF refund upon property sale or transfer

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** CPF top-ups

## About this support
- Receive more cash proceeds and refund less to your CPF account when selling or transferring your property
- Take advantage of CPF’s interest rates and retire with more
- Re-use CPF savings for the various CPF approved schemes if needed

## Who is this for?
- You have used your Ordinary Account (OA) savings to purchase your property
- Please note the following conditions when making the voluntary housing refund:
  - You can refund up to the CPF principal amount withdrawn towards the property plus its accrued interest to your CPF account
  - If you are an undischarged bankrupt, you have to obtain the Official Assignee’s approval to make this housing refund
  - While housing grants will generally be refunded to your OA if you have an HDB flat, the grant(s) may be partially credited to your Special Account / Retirement Account and MediSave Account if you have received more than $30,000 in grant(s)
  - If you are 55 and above, the refunded amount [will be used to meet your Full Retirement Sum (FRS)](http://www.cpf.gov.sg/VHRAge55), which supports your retirement needs through monthly payouts
  - Any refunds beyond your cohort’s FRS will remain in your OA
- You can read more on [housing refunds and their processes](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/infohub/educational-resources/sales-proceeds-after-selling-your-home)

## How to apply?
Check the amount of voluntary refund you can make under the “What happens if” section in your [Home ownership dashboard](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/homeownershipdashboard).

You can make the voluntary housing refund through the following methods:

- Log in to [my cpf digital services](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/make-a-voluntary-housing-refund) using your Singpass:
  - Choose your property and enter a refund amount

Or

- Use the CPF Mobile app:
  - Download the CPF Mobile app
  - Log in with your Singpass
  - Tap on 'Services'
  - Choose 'Voluntary Housing Refund'

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us)

Note: By appointment only

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/growing-your-savings/saving-more-with-cpf/make-a-voluntary-housing-refund)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://cpf.gov.sg/contact-us)

## Phone number
CPF hotline: [1800-227-1188](tel:1800-227-1188)

To avoid waiting on the line, you may book an appointment [here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/appt/oas/form).

embedding_text:
Domains: Caregiving, Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits, Housing and shelters

# Home Protection Scheme (HPS)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/HPS*

Mortgage-reducing insurance that protects you and your loved ones from losing your Housing and Development Board (HDB) flat in the event of death, terminal illness, or total permanent disability.

## Highlights
- Payout up to the sum assured will be made to HDB or the mortgagee directly
- Processing of claim application generally takes 5 working days upon CPF Board's receipt of requested documents

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Insurance, PWDs

## About this support
**For claims under death grounds**

- HPS benefits will be paid in a lump sum (based on the share of HPS cover) to HDB or the mortgagee directly to settle the outstanding housing loan.
  - Any excess claim amounts will be paid to the insured member's CPF Ordinary Account.
  - Thereafter, the deceased member’s CPF savings will be distributed to nominees, or next-of-kins depending on whether there is a valid nomination made.

**For claims admitted under medical grounds**

- Housing instalments (based on the share of HPS cover) may be paid by HPS for a period of up to two years, before a review of insured member's eligibility to claim the remaining insured sum in full is carried out.

## Who is this for?
CPF members who own a HDB flat and are HPS policyholders paying their monthly housing instalments using CPF savings or cash are eligible to apply for HPS coverage.

- HPS claim payout is made to:
  - Next-of-kin of HPS policyholder who is deceased, or
  - HPS policyholder who is certified by a registered medical practitioner under the Medical Registration Act to be suffering from:
    - Terminal illness: an illness that is likely to result in the death of the insured CPF member within 12 months
    - Total permanent disability: the inability to take part in any employment permanently, or the total permanent loss of physical function of any of the following:
      - Both eyes, or
      - Two limbs, or
      - One eye and one limb

## How to apply?
[Apply online for HPS coverage](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/apply-adjust-home-protection-scheme-cover) via the CPF website with your Singpass.

**Claim on death grounds**

- If the insured member has an outstanding housing loan, CPF Board will automatically assess the deceased’s claim eligibility upon Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA)'s notification.
- CPF Board will inform the co-owner(s) or the insured's next-of-kin of the outcome and if additional information is required.

**Claim on medical grounds**

- Submit your application to CPF Board directly via the [CPF website](http://cpf.gov.sg/applyrleandclaimhpsdps)

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us) 
Note: By appointment only

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/home-ownership/protecting-against-losing-your-home)

## Email / Form
[Write to us](https://cpf.gov.sg/writetous)

## Phone number
CPF Hotline: [1800 227 1188](tel:18002271188)

To avoid waiting on the line, you may book an appointment [here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/appt/oas/form).

embedding_text:
Domains: Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits, Housing and shelters

# CPF Housing Scheme 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/AboVw46N*

Enables CPF members to use their Ordinary Account (OA) savings to buy properties and pay for various housing purchase-related costs if they are owners of the property.

## Highlights
- Use CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings to buy properties or pay for housing purchase-related costs 

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** CPF, Home ownership

## About this support
- Enables members to use their OA savings to buy residential property in Singapore
- OA savings can be used to cover downpayments, housing loans, stamp and legal fees and Home Protection Scheme premiums (for HDB flats)

## Who is this for?
- The amount of OA savings members can use depends on several factors, including the remaining lease of the property, the type of housing loan you’re taking, the age of the youngest owner using CPF, and the number of properties you are using CPF for
- For detailed information on the terms and conditions, please refer to the [terms and conditions for use of CPF savings under the CPF Housing Scheme](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tnc/t-c-for-use-of-cpf-under-cpf-housing-scheme)
- Upon sale, transfer or disposal of the property (during your lifetime), you are required to refund the CPF principal amount withdrawn together with the accrued interest to your CPF account(s)
- If you are aged 55 or above and have pledged the property to make up your retirement sum, you will also be required to refund the pledged amount

## How to apply?
- To use your OA savings for the property, HDB or the lawyer acting for you in the purchase must submit an application to the CPF Board with your CPF withdrawal details, along with any required documentation
- [Know how much OA you can use](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/home-ownership/using-your-cpf-to-buy-a-home)
- Before your OA savings can be used, you may need to pay certain amounts in cash, [depending on the type of property and housing loan](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/can-i-use-my-cpf-savings-for-the-down-payment-of-my-property)
- Note that the savings withdrawn are paid to the property developer, HDB, sellers, banks, lawyers or such other entities on your behalf
- To adjust or stop your OA savings for your loan payments, log in to your HDB e-Services if you have an HDB loan or [myCPF](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/houseinstalment) if you have a bank loan

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us)

Note: By appointment only

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/home-ownership/using-your-cpf-to-buy-a-home)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://cpf.gov.sg/writetous)

## Phone number
CPF hotline: [1800-227-1188](tel:1800-227-1188)

To avoid waiting on the line, you may book an appointment [here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/appt/oas/form).

title: Shared Parental Leave  (SPL)
description: Support eligible working parents in sharing parental responsibility and caring for their infants.
highlights: Government reimbursement/payment capped at $2,500 per week
Leave may be taken in one continuous block or non-continuously
embedding_text:
Domains: Family, parenting and relationships

# Shared Parental Leave  (SPL)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/webPUlth*

Support eligible working parents in sharing parental responsibility and caring for their infants.

## Highlights
- Government reimbursement/payment capped at $2,500 per week 
- Leave may be taken in one continuous block or non-continuously 

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Paid leave, Parents

## About this support
SPL (2013)
SPL (from 1 Apr 2025)
**Amount of leave entitled**
Eligible working fathers can take up to 4 weeks of leave from their wife’s Government-Paid Maternity Leave (GPML) or Adoption Leave (AL).
Child’s birth or estimated delivery date or Formal Intent to Adopt (FIA) date:
- If between 1 Apr 2025 to 31 Mar 2026, up to 6 weeks of leave to be shared between parents
- If on or after 1 Apr 2026, up to 10 weeks of leave to be shared between parents
**Amount of government reimbursement/payment**
Government reimbursement/payment capped at $2,500 per week, up to a total of $10,000 for 4 weeks.
Government reimbursement/payment capped at $2,500 per week.
**Flexibility of leave**
Flexibility for leave to be taken in one continuous block or non-continuously, with mutual agreement between employer and employee.
**When can SPL be taken?**
Within 12 months from the child's date of birth.
- After Government-Paid Maternity Leave (GPML)/ Government-Paid Paternity Leave (GPPL)/ Adoption Leave (AL) is fully consumed; and
- Within 12 months from the child’s date of birth.

## Who is this for?
Parents whose child is born, or has an estimated delivery date (EDD), or formal intent to adopt (FIA) date **on or after 1 Apr 2025**, are entitled to the [new SPL scheme](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/schemes/shared-parental-leave) and should not be making an election for 2013-SPL.

SPL (2013) (For father)
SPL (from 1 Apr 2025) (For both father and mother)
**For live births**
- Your child is a Singapore citizen or becomes one within 12 months from birth
- Child's birth or estimated delivery date is between 1 Jul 2017 and 31 Mar 2025 (both dates inclusive)
- Wife is eligible for Government-Paid Maternity Leave or Adoption Leave and agrees to share the leave
- Married to child's mother between conception and birth or within 12 months from birth
- Your child is a Singapore citizen or becomes one within 12 months from birth
- Child’s birth or estimated delivery date:
  - If between 1 Apr 2025 to 31 Mar 2026, entitled to 6 weeks of SPL
  - If on or after 1 Apr 2026, entitled to 10 weeks of SPL
- For fathers: Lawfully married to the child’s mother between conception and birth or within 12 months from birth
- For employee: Served employer for at least 3 months before child’s birth
- For self-employed: Engaged in trade, business, profession, or vocation for at least 3 months before child’s birth
**For stillbirths**
- The date of stillbirth is between 1 Nov 2021 and 31 Mar 2025 (both dates inclusive)
- Either you or the child’s mother are Singapore citizens
NIL
**For adoptive child**
- Formal Intent to Adopt (FIA) date between 1 Jul 2017 and 31 Mar 2025 (both dates inclusive)
- Married to the adoptive mother when the election for 2013-SPL was made
- If child is not Singapore citizen (SC), either you or the adoptive mother has been SC since the child’s dependant’s pass issuance
- Formal Intent to Adopt (FIA) date:
  - If between 1 Apr 2025 to 31 Mar 2026, entitled to 6 weeks of SPL
  - If on or after 1 Apr 2026, entitled to 10 weeks of SPL
- Not the natural father or mother of child
- If child is not Singapore citizen (SC), either adoptive mother or father of child has been SC since the child’s dependant’s pass issuance
- For employee: Served employer for at least 3 months before FIA date
- For self-employed: Engaged in trade, business, profession, or vocation for at least 3 months before FIA date

## How to apply?
**For SPL (2013)**

- Discuss and agree on the leave arrangement with your wife.

- Your wife must declare her intention to share her leave through the [Share My Leave eService](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/eservices/share-my-leave) in the Government-Paid Leave (GPL) Portal no earlier than 16 weeks before your child’s estimated delivery date.

**For employees:**
Notify your employer of the leave arrangement and submit the [declaration form (SPL1)](https://go.gov.sg/spl1form) with necessary documents.
**For self-employed:**
Record your SPL dates and submit your claim online via the [GPL Portal](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/eservices/submit-a-claim) within 3 months after the last date of your SPL.
**For employers:**
- Obtain and verify the [declaration form (SPL1)](https://go.gov.sg/spl1form) and supporting documents from your employee.
- Keep the declaration form or records for 5 years from the last leave date for audit purposes.
- Verify that your employee’s wife has made a declaration to share her leave in the Government-Paid Leave (GPL) Portal. Check all supporting documents to confirm your employee’s eligibility.
Submit your claim for reimbursement online via the [GPL Portal](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/eservices/submit-a-claim) no later than 3 months after the last date of your employee’s SPL.

**For SPL (from 1 Apr 2025)**

Please refer to details on the [GPL Portal](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/schemes/shared-parental-leave/).

## Agency website
For SPL (from 1 Apr 2025), [view more details](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/schemes/shared-parental-leave).

For the SPL (2013), [view more details](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/schemes/2013-shared-parental-leave)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://go.gov.sg/contact-gpls)

## Phone number
MSFCares: [1800 111 2222](tel:18001112222)

(say ‘GPLS’ when asked for the hotline you want to reach)

Domains: Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits, Housing and shelters

# U-Save

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/U-SAVE*

Quarterly rebates to offset HDB households’ utilities expenses. In FY2026, eligible households will receive up to $760 in U-Save rebates.

## Highlights
- Up to $190 of additional U-Save rebates (Oct 2026 and Jan 2027) for eligible HDB households
- Total of $440 to $760 in U-Save rebates for eligible HDB households in FY2026
- No application needed

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Budget 2026, HDB households, Rebates

embedding_text:
Domains: Family, parenting and relationships

# Government-Paid Childcare Leave (GPCL) and Extended Childcare Leave (ECL) 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/z1YHov1e*

Provides up to 6 days of leave for eligible working parents and legal guardians with children below 7 years old, and 2 days for those with children aged 7 to 12.

## Highlights
- Up to 6 days of Government-Paid Childcare Leave (GPCL) for parents with a Singapore citizen child below 7 years old, capped at $500 per day for the 4th to 6th day, up to $1,500 per year 
- 2 days of Extended Childcare Leave (ECL) for parents with a Singapore citizen child aged 7 to 12, capped at $500 per day, up to $1,000 per year

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Child care, Paid leave, Parents

## About this support
Learn more about the [future enhancements to Childcare Leave and Government Reimbursement](https://go.gov.sg/ndr2026supportingfamilies).

**For parents with a Singapore citizen child below 7 years old**:

- Up to 6 days of Government-Paid Childcare Leave (GPCL)
- Employer pays for the first 3 days of GPCL
- Government reimburses for the 4th to 6th day, capped at $500 per day, up to $1,500 per year

**For parents with a Singapore citizen child between 7 and 12 years old:**

- 2 days of Extended Childcare Leave (ECL)
- Fully reimbursed by the Government, capped at $500 per day, up to $1,000 per year.

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizen child below 7 years old for GPCL or obtains Singapore citizenship within the calendar year
- Singapore Citizen child aged 7 to 12 years old for ECL or obtains Singapore citizenship within the calendar year
- Parent has served employer for at least 3 months or been self-employed for at least 3 months and have lost income from ceasing to be actively engaged during your GPCL/ECL period.
- Adoptive parents, eligible only after Adoption Order is passed
- Natural fathers not eligible if not lawfully married to the child's mother at conception and not married subsequently
- Foster parents eligible until they cease providing care, protection or supervision
- Legal guardians with court-appointed guardianship eligible

## How to apply?
**For employees:**

- Inform your employer of your leave plans.
- For foster parents, show your Letter of Identity to your employer as proof that a foster child has been placed under your care under the Children and Young Persons Act. Your employer can write in to the MSF Fostering Service at fostering@msf.gov.sg to verify your eligibility for GPCL/ECL
- For legal guardians, provide a copy of your Legal Guardianship document (i.e. Order of Court) to your employer, for verification on your GPCL/ECL eligibility.
- Submit a [declaration form (GPCL1)](https://go.gov.sg/gpcl1form) with necessary documents.
- Apply for leave as per your employer's procedures.

**For self-employed:**

- Record your leave dates.
- Submit your claim on the [Government-Paid Leave (GPL) Portal](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/eservices/submit-a-claim) within 3 months after the calendar year ends.

**For employers:**

- Collect and verify the [declaration form (GPCL1)](https://go.gov.sg/gpcl1form) from your employee.
- Submit your reimbursement claim on the [GPL Portal](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/eservices/submit-a-claim) within 3 months after the 12-month period ends.

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/schemes/childcare-leave)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://go.gov.sg/contact-gpls)

## Phone number
MSFCares: [1800 111 2222](tel:18001112222) 
(say ‘GPLS’ when asked for the hotline you want to reach)

Operating hours: Mon to Fri 8.30am to 6pm | Saturday: 8.30am to 1pm
(Closed on Public Holidays)

Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines

# Government-Paid Adoption Benefit (GPAB) 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/hyKt9lkY*

Provides up to 12 weeks of Government-paid income for eligible adoptive working mothers who do not qualify for Adoption Leave for Mothers (AL).

## Highlights
- Up to 8 weeks of Government-paid income for 1st and 2nd child, capped at $20,000 
- Up to 12 weeks of Government-paid income for 3rd and subsequent child, capped at $30,000 
- For adoptive mothers who do not qualify for AL due to their employment arrangements 

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Fees payable, Paid leave, Parents

## About this support
Learn more about the [future enhancements to Government Reimbursement](https://go.gov.sg/ndr2026supportingfamilies).

- Up to 8 weeks of Government-paid income for the first and second child, capped at $20,000.
- Up to 12 weeks of Government-paid income for the third and subsequent child, capped at $30,000.

## Who is this for?
- Adopting a child in accordance with any Singapore law relating to the adopting of children
- You are not the natural mother of the child
- Child is below 12 months old on Formal Intent to Adopt (FIA) date
- FIA date on or after 1 January 2021
- If child is not a Singapore Citizen on FIA date, a Dependent’s Pass has been issued and either you or your husband has been a Singapore Citizen since the Dependent’s Pass issue date
- Employed or self-employed for at least 90 days in the 12 months before FIA date
- You do not qualify for the AL scheme Adoption Leave (AL) except under specific conditions such as end of employment contract or retrenchment

## How to apply?
- Record employment contract dates or trade/business periods from the 12 months before your Formal Intent to Adopt (FIA) date.
- Submit your claim [online](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/eservices/submit-a-claim) within 15 months of your child's birth.
- An officer will contact you post-submission.

# Adoption Leave for Mothers (AL) 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/bJlTN9xt*

Provides up to 12 weeks of leave for eligible adoptive mothers to care for their adopted child.

## Highlights
- Up to 12 weeks of Adoption Leave for eligible adoptive mothers 
- Government reimbursement capped at $10,000 per 4 weeks, up to $20,000 for the first and second child orders 
- For the third and subsequent child orders, the government will reimburse up to $30,000 

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Child care, Paid leave, Parents

## About this support
Learn more about the [future enhancements to Government Reimbursement](https://go.gov.sg/ndr2026supportingfamilies).

- Up to 12 weeks of Adoption Leave (AL) for mothers to care for their adopted infant.
- For the first and second child, the employer pays for the first 4 weeks; the government reimburses the 5th to 12th week, capped at $10,000 per 4 weeks, up to $20,000 per child order.
- For the third and subsequent child, the government reimburses all 12 weeks, capped at $10,000 per 4 weeks, up to $30,000 per child order.
- Option to share up to 4 weeks of Adoption Leave (AL) with the adoptive father under the Government-Paid Shared Parental Leave scheme.

## Who is this for?
- You are not the natural mother of the child
- Adopting a child in accordance with any Singapore law relating to the adopting of children.
- Child is below 12 months old on your Formal Intent to Adopt (FIA) date
- FIA date on or after 1 July 2017
- You are employed or self-employed for at least 3 months before FIA date
- If child is not a Singapore citizen on adoption application date, he/she must have a Dependent's Pass (DP) and either parent must have been a Singapore citizen since the issue date

## How to apply?
**For employees:**

- Notify your employer about your leave arrangement early.
- Submit [declaration form (AL1)](https://go.gov.sg/al1form) to your employer with necessary documents at least one week before starting your Adoption Leave (AL), or within one week after starting your AL.
- Apply for AL as per your employer's leave application procedures.

**For self-employed:**

- Record your AL dates
- Submit your claim online via the [Government-Paid Leave (GPL) Portal](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/eservices/submit-a-claim) after starting the government-paid portion of your AL
- Claims should be submitted within 3 months after the last day of your AL

**For employers:**

- Obtain and verify the declaration form (AL1) and supporting documents from your employee
- Keep the declaration form or records for 5 years from the last AL date
- Submit your claim for reimbursement online via the [GPL Portal](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/eservices/submit-a-claim) after your employee has taken the government-paid portion of AL
- Claims should be submitted within 3 months after the last date of the employee’s AL

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/schemes/adoption-leave)

[Submit an enqury](https://go.gov.sg/contact-gpls)

# Government-Paid Maternity Benefit (GPMB)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/iq4yqplI*

Provides up to 16 weeks of income support for eligible working mothers who do not qualify for Government-Paid Maternity Leave.

## Highlights
- Up to 8 weeks of income support for 1st and 2nd child, capped at $20,000 
- Up to 16 weeks of income support for 3rd and subsequent child, capped at $40,000 
- For mothers who do not qualify for GPML due to their employment arrangements

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Cash assistance, Child care, Parents

## About this support
Learn more about the [future enhancements to Government Reimbursement](https://go.gov.sg/ndr2026supportingfamilies).

- Up to 8 weeks of income support for the first and second child, capped at $20,000.
- Up to 16 weeks of income support for the third and subsequent child, capped at $40,000.

## Who is this for?
**For live births**

- Your child is a Singapore Citizen or becomes a Singapore Citizen within 12 months from birth
- Your child's date of birth/estimated delivery date is on or after 1 Jan 2017
- Employed or self-employed for at least 90 days in the 12 months before the child's birth
- Not eligible for Government-Paid Maternity Leave (GPML) or maternity leave under the Employment Act, except under specific conditions such as end of employment contract or retrenchment.

**For stillbirths**:

Similar conditions apply, with the following additional criteria:

- The date of stillbirth is on or after 1 November 2021
- You are a Singapore Citizen at the time of stillbirth or the child’s father is a Singapore Citizen and was lawfully married to the mother at some point between conception and stillbirth

## How to apply?
- Record employment contract dates or trade/business periods from the 12 months before your Formal Intent to Adopt (FIA) date.
- Submit your claim [online](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/eservices/submit-a-claim) no later than 15 months after your child’s birth.
- An officer will contact you post-submission

# Baby Support Grant

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/BSG*

Help parents ease financial concerns about raising a child during extraordinary times.

## Highlights
- One-off cash payout of $3,000 for eligible Singaporean children
- Extended to eligible Singaporean children born from 1 Oct 2022 to 13 Feb 2023 
- No application needed if you have applied for Baby Bonus Scheme previously

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Budget 2023, Cash assistance, Families

## About this support
The SG Child Support Package announced at the 2026 National Day Rally will replace the current Baby Bonus Scheme and Large Families Scheme. Those currently on the Baby Bonus Scheme will be automatically transitioned to the Package. In the meantime, existing payouts will continue as usual. 

Learn more about the [SG Child Support Package](https://go.gov.sg/sgchildsupportpackage).

Eligible Singaporean children born from 1 Oct 2022 to 13 Feb 2023 qualify for the one-off cash payout of $3,000. The Grant will be disbursed from the second half of 2023.

## Who is this for?
- Child is a Singapore Citizen
- Children born from 1 Oct 2022 to 13 Feb 2023
- Parents are lawfully married
- Children who are already receiving the Baby Bonus Cash Gift are also eligible for the Baby Support Grant.

## How to apply?
- No application needed if you have applied for Baby Bonus Scheme previously.
- From 1 July 2024, improvements to Baby Bonus services were made easier for parents for Baby Bonus application and accounts related services:
  - All parents can apply for Baby Bonus Scheme at LifeSG:
    - [Bundled service](https://www.life.gov.sg/services/birth-registration) together with child’s birth registration
    - [Direct application](https://www.life.gov.sg/services/baby-bonus) for child who has already registered for birth

## Agency website
[Baby Bonus Scheme | LifeSG](https://www.life.gov.sg/family-parenting/benefits-support/baby-bonus-scheme)

# Baby Bonus Cash Gift

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/BB-CG*

Help parents defray child-raising costs through regular cash payouts in their child's early years.

## Highlights
- Baby Bonus Cash Gift enhanced by $3,000 for eligible Singaporean children
- Enhancements will apply to eligible Singaporean children born on or after 14 Feb 2023
- Apply online on LifeSG app/website 

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Budget 2023, Cash assistance, Families

## About this support
The SG Child Support Package announced at the 2026 National Day Rally will replace the current Baby Bonus Scheme and Large Families Scheme. Those currently on the Baby Bonus Scheme will be automatically transitioned to the Package. In the meantime, existing payouts will continue as usual. 

Learn more about the [SG Child Support Package](https://go.gov.sg/sgchildsupportpackage).

Eligible Singaporean children born on or after 14 Feb 2023 will qualify for the enhanced Baby Bonus Cash Gift announced at Budget 2023.

- Eligible Singaporean children in the first and second birth order will receive $11,000 while children in the third and subsequent birth orders will receive $13,000.
- Cash Gift will be disbursed on a regular basis, every six months until the child is six-and-a-half years old.
- The Baby Bonus Cash Gift will be paid into the new Child Savings Account (CSA), which is a joint savings account that opens automatically at the same time with the Child Development Account (CDA) when a child is enrolled for the Baby Bonus Scheme. With a savings account, it will be easier for the child to receive Government payouts, like the Baby Bonus cash gift, education awards and financial assistance.

## Who is this for?
- Child is a Singapore Citizen
- Children born on or after 14 Feb 2023
- Parents are lawfully married

## How to apply?
All parents can apply for Baby Bonus Scheme at LifeSG:

- [Bundled service](https://www.life.gov.sg/services/birth-registration) together with child’s birth registration
- [Direct application](https://www.life.gov.sg/services/baby-bonus) for child who has already registered for birth

embedding_text:
Domains: Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits, Housing and shelters

# Housing Loan from HDB 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/HOUSEL-HDB*

Provides eligible buyers with financing via housing loan to purchase or take over ownership of a HDB flat.

## Highlights
- Eligibility for up to 75% Loan-to-Value (LTV) limit for new and resale flats
- Monthly instalments capped at 30% of applicants' monthly income
- Concessionary interest rate for HDB housing loans 

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** HDB households, Home ownership

## About this support
- LTV limit of up to 75% for new and resale flats
- Monthly instalments capped at 30% of the applicants' monthly income
- Concessionary interest rate for HDB housing loans
- Option to use CPF savings to pay for the loan
- Applicants may also retain their savings or use them to pay for CPF Home Protection Insurance

## Who is this for?
- At least 1 applicant must be a Singapore Citizen (SC)
- The core member(s)* in the HFE letter application must not have previously taken 2 or more housing loans from HDB
- Singles aged 35 and above who are buying a 2-room Flexi flat on 99-year lease from HDB or a 5-room or smaller resale flat
- Senior citizens aged 55 and above who are not applying for a 2-room Flexi flat on a short lease or a Community Care Apartment (CCA)
- Your average gross monthly household income must not exceed:
  - $16,000 for families
  - $24,000 for extended families
  - $8,000 for singles buying under the Single Singapore Citizen (SSC) Scheme
- All persons listed in the application:
  - Cannot own or have an interest in any private residential property, local or overseas
  - Must not have disposed of any private residential property in the last 30 months before the application for an HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter

*Core member(s) refer to the applicant(s) and occupier(s) in an HFE letter application who enable the applicant(s) to qualify for a flat purchase under an eligibility scheme. All core members must remain in the flat application, and physically occupy the flat during the minimum occupation period (MOP) after the flat purchase. Their names cannot be removed.

**Second HDB housing loan**
You must also meet the following additional requirements:

At Point of Flat Purchase
Conditions to Take a Second HDB Housing Loan
You have disposed of the existing flat or private residential property and do not own any HDB flat
You and the essential occupier have to use up to 50% of the cash proceeds from the disposal of the last-owned HDB flat or from private residential property disposed of at least 30 months prior to the HFE letter application.

You may retain up to $20,000 in your CPF Ordinary Account (OA) and use the remaining balance to buy the flat.
You are buying a HDB flat **before** disposing of the existing one
You will be charged the commercial interest rate (pegged to the average non-promotional interest rate for HDB flats offered by the 3 local Financial Institutions (FIs)†) for the housing loan to buy the next flat.

The interest rate will be converted to the concessionary rate after you have disposed of the existing flat and used the CPF refund and up to 50% of the cash proceeds from the disposal to reduce the housing loan amount for the next flat. From the CPF monies refunded, you may retain up to $20,000 in your CPF OA.

†The 3 local FIs are DBS Bank Limited, Overseas-Chinese Banking Corporation Limited, and United Overseas Bank Limited.

Please note that your second HDB housing loan amount will be reduced by the full CPF refund and part of the cash proceeds from the disposal of the following residential properties:

- Existing or last-owned HDB flat
- Last-owned private residential property, disposed of at least 30 months prior to the HFE letter application

The manner of disposal includes the sale, transfer or surrender of a flat or private residential property, or by any other method under the Housing and Development Act or any other written law.

You may read more on how the cash proceeds from the disposal are used on [HDB InfoWEB](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/housing-loan/housing-loan-from-hdb).

## How to apply?
- Obtain a HFE letter through the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp27/PrelimHFE/)
- The HFE letter will inform you of your eligibility for purchasing a flat and the amount of housing loan and grants you can receive
- Use the [payment plan calculator](https://homes.hdb.gov.sg/home/calculator/payment-plan) to estimate your budget and payments required

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/housing-loan/housing-loan-from-hdb)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](http://go.gov.sg/hdb-write-to-us)

## Phone number
HDB Hotline: [6866-3066](tel:6866-3066)

# Priority Scheme - First-Timer (Parents & Married Couples), FT(PMC) Category 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/FTPMC-CAT*

To help young families settle down more quickly, additional support will be provided for applicants who qualify for the FT(PMC) category.

## Highlights
- Additional ballot chance for the Build-To-Order (BTO) or Sale of Balance (SBF) exercises, totalling 3 ballot chances for FT(PMC) applicants
- First priority for applicants applying for 4-room or smaller BTO flats in Standard projects under the Family and Parenthood Priority Scheme (FPPS)

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** HDB households, Homes

## About this support
- 1 additional ballot chance, on top of the 2 provided to First-Timer Families, when applying for BTO or SBF flats
- Receive first priority for flats set aside under the Family and Parenthood Priority Scheme (FPPS) when applying for a 4-room or smaller BTO flat in Standard projects
- Learn more about the additional ballot chances that you may receive as a first-timer family when applying for a flat during a [BTO or SBF exercise](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/bto-sbf-and-open-booking-of-flats/process-for-buying-a-new-flat/modes-of-sales).

## Who is this for?
Applicants must meet all of the following criteria:

- Families with at least 1 Singapore Citizen child aged 18 and below, or married couples aged 40 and below (includes married couples who are expecting and have a doctor’s certification of the pregnancy)
- Never owned or sold a residential property before, including a HDB flat
- Did not have a chance to book a BTO or SBF flat in the past 5 years prior to their flat application

## How to apply?
- Obtain a HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter through the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp27/PrelimHFE/) and apply for a flat during BTO or SBF exercises
- You need not request to be considered for FT (PMC). HDB will assess and inform you about your eligibility after you have submitted your flat application

[View more details](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/bto-sbf-and-open-booking-of-flats/process-for-buying-a-new-flat/application/priority-schemes?anchor=ftpmc)

# Step-Up CPF Housing Grant (Families) 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/SU-CPFHG-FAM*

Provides a $15,000 Step-Up CPF Housing Grant to eligible second-timer applicants buying a new or resale flat.

## Highlights
- Eligible applicants can receive a grant of $15,000 to offset the flat’s purchase price or reduce the housing loan needed

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** HDB households, Housing grants

## About this support
- Supports eligible married couples and families who have taken one housing subsidy and are buying an eligible next flat.
- The $15,000 grant is directly credited into all eligible Singapore Citizen (SC) and Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) member’s CPF Ordinary Accounts. Only core applicants may use their shares to offset the flat purchase price or reduce the housing loan required.
- Eligible resale flat buyers may also apply for the Proximity Housing Grant (Families).

## Who is this for?
Married couples or families who have taken one housing subsidy and meet the following conditions:

- You currently live in:
  - a 2-room Standard flat bought from HDB after October 2024, or bought on the open market with CPF housing grant(s); or
  - a 2-room unclassified flat in a non-mature estate bought from HDB after October 1995, or bought on the open market with CPF housing grant(s);
  and are buying a 3-room Standard/ unclassified flat in a non-mature estate, from HDB or on the open market.
- You currently live in a flat under the Public Rental Scheme and are buying:
  - from HDB: a 2-room Flexi or 3-room Standard flat, or a 2-room Flexi or 3-room unclassified flat in a non-mature estate; or
  - on the open market: a 2-room or 3-room Standard flat, or a 2-room or 3-room unclassified flat in a non-mature estate.

Non-mature estates include Bukit Batok, Bukit Panjang, Choa Chu Kang, Hougang, Jurong East, Jurong West, Punggol, Sembawang, Sengkang, Tengah, Woodlands, and Yishun.

- At least one core member must have worked continuously for at least 12 months during the assessment period ending 2 months before the HFE letter application, and be working at the time of application.
- Average gross monthly household income must not $8,000
- Must not own, have an interest in or dispose of any private residential property (local or overseas) in the last 30 months
- For resale flats, the remaining lease must be more than 20 years and be sufficient to cover the youngest core applicant and / or core occupier to the age of 95

## How to apply?
- Apply for the HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter through the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp27/PrelimHFE/) to check your eligibility for this Grant and others
- If you meet the eligibility criteria, you may apply for the grant when submitting your resale application or after you have booked a flat from HDB

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/couples-and-families/stepup-cpf-housing-grant)

[Submit an enquiry](http://go.gov.sg/hdb-write-to-us)

# CPF Housing Grant (Families) - Top-Up Grant

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/ieMs9uMO*

Provides up to $40,000 housing grants to eligible families if they had previously received CPF Housing Grant for Singles and now qualify for the CPF Housing Grant for Families.

## Highlights
- Up to $40,000 in Top-Up grant for eligible families 
- Available to those who previously received a Singles Grant or bought a 2-room Flexi flat as a single, and are now married
- Grant is directly credited into all eligible Singapore Citizen and Singapore Permanent Resident members’ CPF Ordinary Accounts

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Housing grants

## About this support
- Up to $40,000 in Top-Up Grant
- The applicant applying for the Top-Up Grant may also apply for other grants (e.g. Enhanced Housing Grant and Proximity Housing Grant), if eligible

## Who is this for?
- You must be a Singapore Citizen (SC) aged 21 and above, and your spouse or child is a SC or Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR)
- You have previously received the CPF Housing Grant for Resale Flats (Singles) or bought a 2-room Flexi flat from HDB as a single, with other single citizens, or with a non-resident spouse. You must not have taken any [**housing subsidy**](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/bto-sbf-and-open-booking-of-flats/conditions-after-buying-a-new-flat?anchor=housing-subsidy) other than the Singles Grant or the purchase of a 2-room Flexi flat from HDB.
- Your average gross monthly household income must not exceed:
  - $16,000 if you were a recipient of a Singles Grant who bought an HDB resale flat, or you bought a short-lease 2-room Flexi flat
  - $8,000 if you bought a 2-room Flexi flat on a 99-year lease
- You and your spouse, as well as other persons listed in the application, must not have ownership or interest in any private residential property, local or overseas, and no disposal of such property within the last 30 months prior to the application
- You and your spouse, as well as other persons listed in the application, must not have ownership or interest in more than one non-residential private property, local or overseas, and no disposal of such property within the last 30 months prior to the application

## How to apply?
You must [submit your application for Top-Up Grant](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/AB22AWTopUpGrantWeb/AB22PMain) within 6 months of your marriage registration or spouse/ child becoming a SC/ SPR

You must not have taken any [**housing subsidy**](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/bto-sbf-and-open-booking-of-flats/conditions-after-buying-a-new-flat?anchor=housing-subsidy) other than the Singles Grant or the purchase of a 2-room Flexi flat from HDB.
- Your average gross monthly household income must not exceed:
  - $16,000 if you were a recipient of a Singles Grant who bought an HDB resale flat, or you bought a short-lease 2-room Flexi flat
  - $8,000 if you bought a 2-room Flexi flat on a 99-year lease
- You and your spouse, as well as other persons listed in the application, must not have ownership or interest in any private residential property, local or overseas, and no disposal of such property within the last 30 months prior to the application
- You and your spouse, as well as other persons listed in the application, must not have ownership or interest in more than one non-residential private property, local or overseas, and no disposal of such property within the last 30 months prior to the application

# Executive Condominiums (ECs) 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/PURCHASE-EC*

Provides a more affordable option to eligible Singaporean households who aspire to own private housing.

## Highlights
- ECs are strata-titled and are developed and sold by private developers
- With design features and facilities similar to private condominiums

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** HDB households, Home ownership

## About this support
- Eligible households can purchase an EC unit from a property developer at a subsidised rate
- Eligible first-timer households may qualify for the CPF Housing Grant

## Who is this for?
**For fiancé or fiancée, married couples and/ or parent(s) with child(ren), orphaned siblings:**

- Applicant must:
  - Be a Singapore Citizen (SC)
  - Include at least 1 other SC or Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR)
  - Be at least 21 years old

**For 2 or more singles applying jointly:**

- All applicants must be:
  - SCs
  - At least 35 years old

**Monthly household income ceiling:**

- The total income of all persons listed in the EC application for new units in EC projects with tenders closing on or after 24 August 2026 must not exceed $18,000*
  *The income ceiling for new units in EC sites with tenders awarded before 24 August 2026 is $16,000.

**Private residential property:**

- Must not own, have an interest in or dispose of any private residential property (local or overseas) in the last 30 months

**Housing subsidies and Resale Levy:**

- If any core applicants/ occupiers have taken a housing subsidy, they are considered second-timers.
- All second-timer core applicants / occupiers will need to pay their respective [resale levies](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/bto-sbf-and-open-booking-of-flats/conditions-after-buying-a-new-flat?anchor=resale-levy) if applicable, when buying an EC unit from a property developer
- If any core applicants/ occupiers have taken 2 housing subsidies, they are not eligible to apply for or be listed as a core occupier in an EC application

## How to apply?
- Submit your [application](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/executive-condominiums/process-for-buying-an-ec) when the EC project is launched
- Contact the property developer directly for details on the application process and required documents
- The property developer will inform you of the outcome of the application

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/executive-condominiums)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](http://go.gov.sg/hdb-write-to-us)

# Experiential Learning and Mentoring Programme (ELMP)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-ELAMPE*

Supports youths through mentoring and, experiential learning. It provides youths with a safe and conducive place to hang out after school and empowers them with pro-social skills and resilience.

**Who it targets:** Families, Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Free, Mentoring

## About this support
The programme engages youth through:

- Centre-based drop-in activities like tchoukball training and small group tuitions
- Experiential learning activities and workshops
- 1 to 1 mentoring sessions with mentors

The activities are conducted once a week.

## Who is this for?
Youths aged 11 to 19 years old who are enrolled in school social work programmes, as well as those referred from school counsellors and parents.

## How to apply?
Youths or their parents can approach or call the centre directly.

## What to expect?
- An intake assessment will be conducted.
- Youths will be matched to a suitable mentor thereafter.

Domains: Family, parenting and relationships

# Government-Paid Maternity Leave (GPML) 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/NYD4HRJs*

Provides up to 16 weeks of paid leave for eligible working mothers to care for their newborns.

## Highlights
- Up to 16 weeks of Government-Paid Maternity Leave (GPML) for eligible working mothers 
- For the first and second child, the employer pays for the first 8 weeks, and the government reimburses the 9th to 16th week, capped at $10,000 per 4 weeks, up to $20,000 
- For the third and subsequent child, the government reimburses all 16 weeks, capped at $10,000 per 4 weeks, up to $40,000 

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Child care, Paid leave, Parents

## About this support
Learn more about the [future enhancements to Government Reimbursement](https://go.gov.sg/ndr2026supportingfamilies).

- Up to 16 weeks of Government-Paid Maternity Leave (GPML) for eligible working mothers.
- For the first and second child, the employer pays for the first 8 weeks, and the government reimburses the 9th to 16th week, capped at $10,000 per 4 weeks, up to $20,000 per child order.
- For the third and subsequent child, the government reimburses all 16 weeks, capped at $10,000 per 4 weeks, up to $40,000 per child order.
- Option to share up to 4 weeks of GPML with the spouse under the Government-Paid Shared Parental Leave scheme.

## Who is this for?
**For live births**:

- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- Child is a Singapore Citizen at birth or within 12 months after birth
- For employees: Served employer for at least 3 months before child's birth (GPML that is granted despite not meeting this criterion **cannot be shared** with your husband under the SPL scheme)
- For self-employed: Engaged in work for at least 3 months before child's birth and lost income during maternity leave

**For stillbirths**: 
Similar conditions apply, with additional criteria:

- The date of stillbirth is on or after 1 November 2021
- You are a Singapore Citizen at the time of stillbirth or the child’s father is a Singapore Citizen and was lawfully married to the mother at some point between conception and stillbirth

## How to apply?
**For employees**:

- Notify your employer at least one week before starting maternity leave.
- Submit the [declaration form (GPML1)](https://file.go.gov.sg/gpml1form.pdf) to your employer with necessary documents at least one week before starting your Government-Paid Maternity Leave (GPML), or within one month from your child’s birth.
- Follow your employer’s leave application process.

**For self-employed**:

- Keep a record of your GPML dates
- Submit your claim online via the [Government-Paid Leave (GPL) Portal](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/eservices/submit-a-claim) after starting the government-paid portion of your GPML
- Claims should be made within three months after the last day of your GPML

**For employers**:

- Obtain and verify the declaration form (GPML1) from your employee
- Keep the declaration form or records for five years from the last GPML date
- Submit your claim for reimbursement online via the [GPL Portal](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/eservices/submit-a-claim) after your employee has taken the government-paid portion of GPML
- Claims should be made within three months after the last day of the employee’s GPML

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/schemes/maternity-leave)

## Email / Form
[Submit your enquiry](https://go.gov.sg/contact-gpls)

## Phone number
MSFCares: [1800 111 2222](tel:18001112222) 
(say ‘GPLS’ when asked for the hotline you want to reach)

embedding_text:
Domains: Family, parenting and relationships

# Shared Parental Leave Benefit (SPB)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/JJxxRnDK*

Support eligible working parents who do not qualify for the Shared Parental Leave (SPL) scheme due to their employment arrangements.

## Highlights
- For natural or adoptive parents who do not qualify for Shared Parental Leave (SPL) due to their employment arrangement. 
- Eligible parents can receive Shared Parental Leave Benefit (SPB), capped at $2,500 per week. 

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Paid leave, Parents

## About this support
- For child born/estimated delivery date/Formal Intent to Adopt (FIA) date between 1 Apr 2025 to 31 Mar 2026, eligible parents can claim up to 6 weeks of income support.

- For child born/estimated delivery date/FIA date on or after 1 Apr 2026, eligible parents can claim up to 10 weeks of income support.

- Government payment capped at $2,500 per week.

## Who is this for?
**For natural parents with live births:**

- Child’s birth or estimated delivery date:
  - If between 1 Apr 2025 to 31 Mar 2026, entitled to 6 weeks
  - If on or after 1 Apr 2026, entitled to 10 weeks

- Your child is a Singapore citizen or becomes one within 12 months from birth

**For adoptive parents:**

- You are not the natural father or mother of the child

- Child’s Formal Intent to Adopt (FIA) date:
  - If between 1 Apr 2025 to 31 Mar 2026, entitled to 6 weeks
  - If on or after 1 Apr 2026, entitled to 10 weeks

- The child must be below 12 months old on FIA date

- If child is not a Singapore Citizen (SC), either adoptive mother or father of child has been SC since the child’s dependant’s pass issuance

**Applicable to all:**

- Employed or self-employed for at least 90 days in the 12 months before child’s birth

- For fathers: lawfully married to the child’s mother between conception and birth or within 12 months of birth

- Not eligible for Shared Parental Leave (SPL) except under specific conditions such as end of employment contract or retrenchment

## How to apply?
Please refer to details on the [GPL Portal](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/schemes/shared-parental-leave-benefit).

## Agency website
[View more details ](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/schemes/shared-parental-leave)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://go.gov.sg/contact-gpls)

- Your child is a Singapore citizen or becomes one within 12 months from birth

**For adoptive parents:**

- You are not the natural father or mother of the child

- Child’s Formal Intent to Adopt (FIA) date:
  - If between 1 Apr 2025 to 31 Mar 2026, entitled to 6 weeks
  - If on or after 1 Apr 2026, entitled to 10 weeks

- The child must be below 12 months old on FIA date

- If child is not a Singapore Citizen (SC), either adoptive mother or father of child has been SC since the child’s dependant’s pass issuance

**Applicable to all:**

- Employed or self-employed for at least 90 days in the 12 months before child’s birth

- For fathers: lawfully married to the child’s mother between conception and birth or within 12 months of birth

- Not eligible for Shared Parental Leave (SPL) except under specific conditions such as end of employment contract or retrenchment

Domains: Family, parenting and relationships

# KidSTART

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/KIDSTART*

Supports pregnant mothers and lower-income families in early childhood development, to build strong foundations for children aged 6 and below.

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income
**Citizenship:** SG
**Keywords:** Free, Lower-income, Resources and Support

## About this support
KidSTART Singapore Limited is a non-profit organisation and an Institution of a Public Character that specialises in supporting families in early childhood development.

Our specialist team partners with the government and community to empower lower-income families in building strong foundations for their children, giving them a good start in life.

## Who is this for?
You are eligible for our services if your family meets these criteria:

1. You are a pregnant mother and/or have a child who is a Singapore Citizen and aged 6 and below
2. You have a gross monthly household income of $2,500 and below, or per capita  income  of $650 and below

[Learn more about this programme and how it can help you](https://kidstart.sg/be-a-kidstart-family/?utm_source=supportgowhere&utm_medium=link&utm_campaign=supportgowhere)

## How to apply?
[Fill up the application form](https://go.gov.sg/beakidstartfamily) to sign up as a KidSTART Family.

## What to expect?
- Children achieve age-appropriate child development outcomes
- Parent-child interactions and family functioning improve

# SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/wpGyuJUN*

Provides temporary financial support of up to $6,000 over 6 months to involuntarily unemployed individuals, to support them in finding a job that makes better use of their skills and experiences.

## Highlights
- Payouts of up to $6,000 over 6 months 
- To qualify for payouts, individuals will have to apply online to participate in the scheme and take part in supported job search activities

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Budget 2025, Jobseekers

## About this support
- Payouts of up to $6,000 over 6 months
- To qualify for payouts, individuals will have to apply online to participate in the scheme and take part in supported job search activities

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, aged 21 and above
- Earned an average gross monthly income of $5,000 or less in the past 12 months*** **(excluding employer CPF contributions)
- Previously employed in Singapore for at least six months in the past 12 months
- Unemployed due to involuntary reasons such as retrenchment, cessation of business, dismissals or termination due to illness, injury or accident
- Lives in a property in Singapore with annual value of $31,000 or less
- Has not received a payout from this scheme in the past three years

*** **Average gross monthly income includes basic salary and extra wages such as overtime pay, commissions and bonuses. This includes only the period(s) where the individual is employed and earning an income.

## How to apply?
You can learn more and apply for the scheme at https://go.gov.sg/jobseekersupport

# CPF Housing Grant for Executive Condominiums (ECs)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/CPF-HG-EC*

Provides up to $30,000 subsidy for eligible first-timer applicants buying an Executive Condominium (EC).

## Highlights
- CPF Housing Grant of up to $30,000 for eligible first-timer household
- Grant can be used to offset EC purchase price or reduce required housing loan

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** CPF top-ups, Housing grants

## About this support
- Housing subsidy of up to $30,000 for eligible first-timer recipients purchasing an EC from a property developer
  - The Grant can be used to offset the EC’s purchase price or reduce the required housing loan for it

## Who is this for?
- Your core family nucleus must include at least 1 first-timer applicant who has not received any housing subsidies before
- Applicants must be Singapore Citizens at least 21 years old
- The household must include at least 1 other Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- All applicants and occupiers must have no ownership or interest in private property locally or overseas in the last 30 months
- All persons listed in the application can, as a household, own up to 1 non-residential property
- Grant amount eligibility will be [determined by your household’s average monthly household income (includes all applicants and occupiers listed in the EC application)](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/executive-condominiums/cpf-housing-grant)
- All members of the core family nucleus will receive equal shares of the grant, fully credited into their CPF Ordinary Accounts
- Only core applicants can use their grants to pay for the EC unit purchase

## How to apply?
Contact the property developer directly for details on the application process and required documents.
