# Housing Loan from Financial Institutions (FI) 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/gXSeAhba*

Supports your flat purchase through housing loans from Financial Institutions (FI) regulated by the Monetary Authority of Singapore.

## Highlights
- Loan-to-Value (LTV) limit up to 75% of the flat’s purchase price / resale price and value 
- Repayment period up to 30 years 

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** HDB households, Home ownership

## About this support
- LTV limit of up to 75% for both new and resale flats
- Repayment period of up to 30 years
- Option to use any amount in OA for flat purchase, dependent on [certain applicable limits](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/housing-loan/housing-loan-from-financial-institutions)
- Can refinance the housing loan with another loan from a different FI or a different interest rate package

## Who is this for?
- Applicants must pay at least 5% of the flat price or flat value (whichever is lower) in cash. The minimum cash payment is dependent on applicants’ age, loan period and whether there are any outstanding housing loans
- Applicants who want to purchase a unit from a property developer under the Executive Condominium Housing Scheme must take a housing loan from an FI
- LTV limit is up to 75% of the flat purchase price or flat value, whichever is lower. FIs may have restrictions on flat purchase depending on remaining lease of the flat and / or if your repayment period exceeds 25 years or you have additional housing loan(s)

## How to apply?
- [Compare housing loan packages from participating Fis](https://homes.hdb.gov.sg/home/calculator/budget)
- Apply early for an In-Principle Approval (IPA) from participating FIs through HDB’s Integrated Loan Application service on the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp28/TimeLine/my-flat-dashboard) for an indicative assessment of your loan eligibility
- You need to obtain a valid Letter of Offer (LO) to confirm the loan offer from an FI before signing Agreement for Lease for a new flat or exercising the Option to Purchase for a resale flat
- Use the integrated loan application service on the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp28/TimeLine/my-flat-dashboard) to apply for IPA and LO)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/housing-loan/housing-loan-from-financial-institutions)

# Lively Places Fund 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/L4IhetvC*

Provides funding of up to $20,000 for community-driven projects that enhance public spaces and foster community bonds.

## Highlights
- Funding of up to $5,000 for small, short-term community projects
- Funding of up to $20,000 for eligible larger projects  
- Traffic redirection support provided for street events 

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Volunteers

## About this support
The funds awarded will depend on the type and scale of the project. Please refer to the below table for a detailed breakdown:

Category
Award Sum
Description
Project fund
Up to $5,000
For smaller, short-term action plans or activities for community bonding in HDB neighbourhoods

e.g. block parties, anti-littering campaign, community recycling day
Building Fund
Up to $5,000
For projects that will involve a physical transformation of existing public spaces and have an implementation period of 6 months or less

e.g. community arts projects and short-term pop-up installations to activate spaces
Up to $20,000
For projects that will involve a physical transformation of existing public spaces and have an implementation period of more than 6 months

e.g. conversion of void decks into community living rooms and cafes, longer-term pop-up installations to activate spaces
Street Closure
N/A
For short-term projects that transform streets into active public spaces for the community

# Enhanced CPF Housing Grant (Singles) 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/ENCPFHG-SIN*

Provides up to $60,000 in Enhanced CPF Housing Grants (EHG) (Singles) for eligible first-timer applicants buying a new or resale flat on their own, or with their non-resident spouses.

## Highlights
- EHG (Singles) Grant of up to $60,000 for eligible first-timer applicants 
- Additional up to $60,000 grant for joint singles scheme (a total of up to $120,000)
- Households with lower household incomes will receive a larger grant amount

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** CPF top-ups, Housing grants, Singles

## About this support
- The EHG (Singles) Grant provides up to $60,000 to offset the purchase price of the flat / reduce the required housing loan for the flat (new or resale)
- Receive a total Grant of up to $120,000 when jointly purchasing flats with other eligible first-timer single applicants (Limited to 2, up to $60,000 each)

## Who is this for?
- First-timer applicants aged 35 or above, who are:
  - buying a HDB flat alone or with other first-timer single citizens
  - buying a resale flat alone, with other first-timer single citizens or with their parents
- First-timer applicants aged 21 or above who are buying a resale flat with their non-resident spouse
- If you are buying a flat with your parents, you and at least 1 parent must be a Singapore Citizen, and both parents must be first-timers and meet all the eligibility conditions
- Applicants have worked continuously for at least 12 months, 2 months before the HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter application, and were employed at the time of the HFE letter application
- Monthly household income not exceeding $4,500 for singles and $9,000 for joint singles, non-resident spouses or your parents (resale flats only)
- Flat has a remaining lease of more than 20 years
- To qualify for the full EHG grant, flat must have sufficient lease for the coverage of the youngest core applicant and occupier to the age of 95
- Must not own, have an interest in or have disposed of any private residential property (local or overseas) within the last 30 months
- All persons listed in the HFE letter application can, as a household, own up to 1 non-residential property at HFE letter application and up to 30 months before HFE letter application

## How to apply?
- Obtain an HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter through the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp27/PrelimHFE/) to determine your eligibility for this Grant as well as others
- If you meet the eligibility criteria, you may apply for the grant when submitting your resale application or after you have booked a flat from HDB
- The Grant will be credited to the CPF Ordinary Accounts of eligible household members
- Only core applicants can use their share of the housing grants to pay for the flat purchase

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/singles/enhanced-cpf-housing-grant)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](http://go.gov.sg/hdb-write-to-us)

## Phone number
HDB Hotline: [6866-3066](tel:6866-3066)

# Enhanced CPF Housing Grant (Families)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/ENCPFHG-FAM*

Provides up to $120,000 for eligible first-time applicants applying as a family to assist with new or resale flat purchases.

## Highlights
- Up to $120,000 Enhanced CPF Housing Grant for first-timer families
- The Grant can be used to offset the flat purchase price or reduce the required housing loan 
- Households with lower household incomes will receive larger grants 

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** CPF top-ups, Families, Housing grants

## About this support
- Up to $120,000 for applicants purchasing a new or resale flat as a family
- Up to $60,000 for couples comprising a first-time and second-time applicant
- The grant amount is based on the average gross monthly household income, with lower-income households receiving more support
- The Enhanced CPF Housing Grant (EHG) can be used to:
  - Offset the purchase price of the flat
  - Reduce the housing loan required for the flat purchase

## Who is this for?
- Applicants forming a core family nucleus, consisting of the core applicant(s) and occupier(s)
- Average gross monthly household income of $9,000 or below for first-timer households (including all applicants and occupiers)
- For mixed households (first-timer and second-timer), half of the average gross monthly household income must not exceed $4,500
- If you are buying a flat with your parents, you and at least 1 parent must be a Singapore Citizen, and both parents must be first-timers and meet all the eligibility conditions
- Have worked continuously for at least 12 months, 2 months before the HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter application, and were employed at the time of the HFE letter application
- Flat has a remaining lease of more than 20 years
- To qualify for the full grant, flat must have sufficient remaining lease to cover the youngest core applicant and/or core occupier to the age of 95
- Must not own, have an interest in or disposed of any private residential property (local or overseas) within the last 30 months
- All persons listed in the HFE application can, as a household, own up to 1 non-residential property at HFE letter application and up to 30 months before HFE letter application

## How to apply?
- Obtain a HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter through the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp27/PrelimHFE/) to determine your eligibility for this Grant and others
- If you meet the eligibility criteria, you may apply for the grant when submitting your resale application or after you have booked a flat from HDB
- The Grant will be credited to the CPF Ordinary Accounts of eligible household members
- Only core applicants can use their share of the housing grants to pay for the flat purchase

# Family and Parenthood Priority Scheme (FPPS) 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/FAM-PRIORITY*

Up to 60% of Sale of Balance Flats (SBF) and up to 40% of Build-To-Order (BTO) flats are made available for eligible first-timer buyers.

## Highlights
- Up to 40% of BTO and 60% of SBF flats reserved for first-timer buyers 
- If you qualify under the FT(PMC) category, you will be eligible for FPPS 
- Can apply for both FPPS and 1 other priority scheme simultaneously

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Families, HDB households, Parents

## About this support
- Up to 40% of BTO flats and up to 60% of SBF flats are set aside for first-timer buyers
- You can apply for the FPPS priority scheme in addition to 1 other priority scheme
- A computerised ballot is conducted for each priority scheme:
  - For example, if your ballot under the Third Child Priority Scheme is not successful, your application will be balloted again under the FPPS

## Who is this for?
- You and your spouse must be first-timer buyers
- Have a Singapore Citizen child (natural or legally adopted) aged 18 and below
- Expecting a child and have a doctor's certification of pregnancy

## How to apply?
- Obtain a HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter through the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp27/PrelimHFE/)
- If you meet the eligibility criteria during your HFE letter application, you may apply for this scheme in your flat application

# Proximity Housing Grant (Singles) 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/PHG-SINGLES*

Provides up to $15,000 for eligible singles buying a resale flat to live with, or near, their parents or children.

## Highlights
- Proximity Housing Grant (PHG) of $15,000 for singles living with parents or child 
- PHG of $10,000 for singles living near parents or child (within 4km) 
- If applicant is living near them, parents / child may be residing in either a HDB flat or private residential property to meet the PHG criteria 

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Home ownership, Housing grants, Singles

## About this support
- Receive a PHG of $15,000 if living with parents or child
- Receive a PHG of $10,000 if living within 4km of parents or child

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizen aged 35 or above, buying alone, with other single citizens or with their parents
- Singapore Citizen aged 21 or above, buying with a non-resident spouse
- The parents/child helping to qualify for the PHG must be Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident
- Applicants buying a resale flat to live with, or within 4km of, their parents or child
- If parents/child are living with you, they must be included in the resale flat as co-applicants or essential occupiers
- If your parents/child are living in a private residential property they do not own, it must be owner-occupied by immediate family members i.e. child, adopted child, parent(s) or parent(s)-in-law, or siblings
- The resale flat has a remaining lease of more than 20 years
- Applicants must not have received the PHG before

## How to apply?
- Obtain a HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter through the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp27/PrelimHFE/)
- If you meet the eligibility criteria, you may apply for the grant when submitting your resale application

Domains: Family, parenting and relationships, Housing and shelters

# Third Child Priority Scheme (TCPS)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/TC-PRIORITY*

Provides priority in flat allocation to eligible families with 3 or more children.

## Highlights
- Up to 10% of Build-To-Order (BTO) flats, and up to 10% of Sale of Balance Flats (SBF) flats allocated for eligible families with 3 or more children
- Provides an additional ballot chance to secure a flat 

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** HDB households, Home ownership

## About this support
- Up to 10% of BTO flats, and up to 10% of SBF flats allocated for eligible families
- Parent(s) expecting their third child can apply for a flat under the TCPS subject to meeting all other eligibility conditions

## Who is this for?
- You and/or your spouse are Singapore Citizens
- If you are divorced or widowed, you must be a Singapore Citizen to qualify
- Your family must consist of at least 3 children or be expecting a third child who are from a legal marriage or legally adopted
- If the family is expecting*, you must have a doctor’s certificate confirming the pregnancy
- Divorced parents must have legal custody, care, and control of their children
- Adoptive parents must provide the Adoption Order when applying for a flat
- Your third child must be born on or after 1 January 1987
- Your youngest child or the child you are expecting must be a Singapore Citizen
- Your other children must be either Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents
- You have not previously bought a flat under the TCPS

*This includes cases where the parent(s) have 1 child and are expecting 2 or more children, or where the parent(s) do not have a child yet and are expecting 3 or more children.

## How to apply?
- Obtain a HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter through the [HDB Flat Portal](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp27/PrelimHFE/)
- If you meet the eligibility criteria during your HFE letter application, you may apply for this scheme in your flat application

embedding_text:
Domains: Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits, Financial/Retirement Planning, Retirement and legacy planning

# Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/VSj0VliA*

Boost your own or loved ones’ retirement savings and payouts through voluntary cash top-ups or CPF transfer to your own or loved ones' Special Account (SA) or Retirement Account (RA).

## Highlights
- Boost CPF retirement savings and monthly payouts  
- Earn interest rates of up to 6% per annum on retirement savings
- Tax relief of up to $16,000 for cash top-ups 

**Who it targets:** Families, Seniors
**Keywords:** CPF top-ups, Tax relief

## About this support
- Receive higher monthly payouts in retirement
- Earn CPF interest rates of up to 6% per annum on retirement savings
- Grow your retirement savings through the power of compound interest for higher monthly payouts
- Enjoy tax relief of up to $16,000 for cash top-ups made to your own and loved ones' retirement savings each calendar year
- Find out more on the [conditions to qualify for tax relief](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/what-are-the-conditions-for-me-to-enjoy-tax-relief-to-special-account-or-retirement-account)

Note:

- In keeping with the objective of the scheme, cash top-ups and CPF transfers are irreversible, and cannot be withdrawn for other purposes (e.g. for housing, investment or withdrawn for immediate needs after age 55).
- Cash top-ups that attract the MRSS matching grant do not qualify for tax relief.

## Who is this for?
- You must be a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident to receive cash top-ups and CPF transfers
- You can check your top-up limits by logging in to your [Retirement Dashboard](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/ds/dashboards/retirement)
- Members aged 55 and above can top up to the Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS)
  - The ERS increases each year so you can top up more each year
- Members below 55 can top up to the Full Retirement Sum (FRS)
- CPF transfers can be made to yourself or your loved ones:

CPF transfer to
Remarks
Yourself
You can transfer your Ordinary Account (OA) savings to your SA if you are below 55. 

If you are aged 55 or above, you can transfer your OA savings to your RA. 

How much you can transfer depends on your age and CPF balances.
Loved ones 
(parents, parents-in-law, grandparents, grandparents-in-law, spouse and siblings)
Before transferring your CPF savings to your loved ones, you must first set aside enough for your own retirement. 

The amount of CPF transfers you can make to them depends on how much your loved one can receive, and the amount you can transfer.

- For more information on your [eligibility for cash transfers, CPF top-ups etc., please refer here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/growing-your-savings/saving-more-with-cpf/top-up-to-enjoy-higher-retirement-payouts)

## How to apply?
- You can make your cash top-up or CPF transfer [online](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/cash-top-ups-and-cpf-transfers-for-retirement) (CPF transfers and cash top-ups via PayNow or GIRO) or via the CPF Mobile app (CPF transfers and cash tops-ups via PayNow)
- To complete your top-up form, you will need:
  - your recipient’s NRIC, if making a cash top-up or CPF transfer to a loved one
  - additional supporting documents if making a CPF transfer to a recipient for the first time (not required for cash top-ups)
- For more information on the application process, please refer [here.](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/how-do-i-apply-to-make-a-top-up)

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us)

Note: By appointment only

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/growing-your-savings/saving-more-with-cpf/top-up-to-enjoy-higher-retirement-payouts)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/feedback)

## Phone number
CPF hotline: [1800-227-1188](tel:1800-227-1188)

To avoid waiting on the line, you may book an appointment [here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/appt/oas/form).

# Legal Aid Bureau

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/dGlR81dt*

Provides legal help for eligible individuals in various civil proceedings.

## Highlights
-  Legal representation for qualified applicants in various civil proceedings
- Assistance with drafting Wills and Deeds of Separation
- Free Legal advice for qualified applicants in various civil proceedings

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Marital and Divorce Support

## About this support
- Legal advice on Singapore law and practical steps for your case.
- Assistance in drafting simple legal documents like Wills and Deeds of Separation.
- Legal representation in various civil proceedings, subject to eligibility.

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents residing in Singapore

Eligibility Tests:

- Means Test for Legal Advice and Assistance
- Means and Merits Test for Legal Aid
- Duty Lawyer available for consultation and assessment of eligibility for legal aid.

## How to apply?
- Register case [online](https://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/labesvc/) with the [step by step guide](https://lab.mlaw.gov.sg/files/AP_Portal_Guide_09032026.pdf) on the [Applicant Portal](https://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/labesvc/?tabIndex=3)
- Attend the Legal Aid Bureau (LAB) within three working days after online registration
- Schedule an appointment via the [OneMinLaw Portal](https://go.gov.sg/omp) before visiting the Minlaw Services Centre at 45 Maxwell Road #07-11, the URA Centre (East Wing)
- If you're a minor or representing someone without mental incapacity, a parent/guardian, or Court-appointed Deputy must apply on your behalf respectively.

## Where to go
[45 Maxwell Road #07-11, The URA Centre (East Wing), Singapore 069118](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=069118)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://lab.mlaw.gov.sg)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](http://go.gov.sg/contactminlaw)

Ministry of Law Hotline: [1800 2255 529](tel:18002255529)

# PAssion Card

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/705gVCXW*

A membership programme that allows its members to enjoy great discounts on courses and activities available at all Community Clubs and other PA outlets such as PAssion Wave. Members can also enjoy exclusive discounts at more than 2,000 participating PAssion Merchant outlets.

## Highlights
- PAssion Members can earn yuu Points at various outlets and contribute to community projects 
- PAssion Silver Concession Card for seniors offers concessionary fares on public transport and merchant benefits
- PAssion POSB Debit Card functions as an ATM, NETS, Debit MasterCard, and EZ-Link card, and offers savings, rewards, and privileges 

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Public transport, Rebates

## About this support
- Exclusive privileges for courses, activities, and programmes
- Unique promotions with lifestyle merchants and partners
- PAssion POSB Debit Card offers savings, rewards, and privileges at over 2,000 places and functions as an ATM, NETS, Debit MasterCard, and EZ-Link card
- PAssion Silver Concession Card provides seniors with concessionary fares on public transport and merchant benefits
- PAssion Members get access to exclusive privileges on eCapitaVoucher and deals on the CapitaStar App
- By linking your PAssion Card to yuu Rewards Club, you can earn yuu Points from a wide-ranging coalition of diverse and market-leading brands including BreadTalk, CS Fresh, Cold Storage, Giant, Guardian Health & Beauty, 7 Eleven, Mandai.com, Toast Box and many more
- You can also earn yuu Points through participation PAssion CARES events organised by PA
- Free PAssion e-Membership for all aged 15 and above with a valid Singpass
- Auto-conversion of expiring PAssion Card to e-Membership for continuous access to benefits

## Who is this for?
- Membership available for all aged 15 and above with a valid Singpass
- PAssion POSB Debit Card for those aged 16 and above with a POSB/DBS Savings or Current account
- PAssion Silver Concession Card for Singapore Citizens aged 60 and above

## How to apply?
To sign up for a PAssion card:

- Visit any Community Clubs or [online](https://www.onepa.gov.sg/)
- The 5-year PAssion Card membership fees are:
  - $12.00 for a Principal Card (for ages between 18 and 59 years old)
  - $10.00 for a Principal Card (for ages below 18 years old, and 60 years old and above)

To sign up for a free PAssion e-Membership:

- Visit [onePA | Membership](https://www.onepa.gov.sg/membership)
- Use your Singpass to sign in to the app
- Free membership available to members of public aged 15 years and above

To sign up for PAssion POSB Debit Card, visit http://www.posb.com.sg/PAssion.

To apply for PAssion Silver Concession Card, visit this [link](https://tlcp.transitlink.com.sg/NewApplication.aspx?Web=Gk8lMWDHPiI=) or submit your application via SimplyGo Ticket Offices or SimplyGo App.

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest Community Centre (CC)](https://www.onepa.gov.sg/cc)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.pa.gov.sg/our-programmes/passion-card/)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://www.pa.gov.sg/feedback/)

## Phone number
PA Contact Centre’s Hotline: [6225 5322](tel:62255322)

Domains: Caregiving, Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits, Financial/Retirement Planning, Legacy planning, Retirement and legacy planning

# Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) Scheme

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/E-WIS*

Supplements eligible workers' income and CPF savings through cash and CPF payments.

## Highlights
- Eligible employees, platform workers and self-employed persons can receive cash and CPF payments to supplement their income and grow their CPF savings for retirement, housing and healthcare
- Employees can receive up to $4,900 per year
- Self-employed persons and Platform Workers can receive up to $3,267 per year

**Who it targets:** Low-income
**Keywords:** Budget 2024, Lower-wage workers

## About this support
**Employees**

- From Work Year 2025, eligible recipients will receive monthly payments of up to $4,900 per year, comprising 40% in cash and 60% credited to CPF Accounts

**Self-employed persons and Platform Workers**

- From Work Year 2025, eligible recipients will receive annual payments of up to $3,267, comprising 10% cash and 90% credited to MediSave Account
- Self-employed persons will receive payments annually, while Platform Workers will receive payments monthly
- From Work Year 2029, eligible Platform Workers whose CPF contribution rates fully align with that of employees will receive higher WIS payments at the same level as employees

## Who is this for?
**Eligibility criteria**

- 30 years old and above as at 31 December of the Work Year
- Singapore Citizen
- Employee, self-employed person and/or platform worker
- Gross monthly income of $500* to $3,000 (if married, assessable income of recipient's spouse must not exceed $70,000), for the month worked
- Average gross monthly income of not more than S$3,000 in the past 12 months as an employee or platform worker
- Annual value of the place of residence (as indicated on NRIC) must not exceed $21,000, as at 31 December of the preceding year
- Does not own more than 1 property (if married, recipient and spouse must not own more than 1 property)

embedding_text:
Domains: Family, parenting and relationships, Housing and shelters, Legacy planning

# Change in HDB Flat Ownership After Flat Owner's Demise

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/NGzAFA4b*

Retain your HDB flat following the demise of joint owner or sole owner/tenant-in-common.

## Highlights
- Family structures changes may affect flat retention eligibility

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Home ownership

## About this support
Take over interest in the HDB flat held under joint-tenancy, when you lodge a Notice of Death with the Singapore Land Authority (SLA), or

Register your right to administer the estate of the deceased sole owner/ co-owner of HDB flat held under tenancy-in-common as the Administrator or Executor, and effect an ownership change in the HDB flat to the beneficiaries.

## Who is this for?
As the remaining family or single occupier, you can retain the existing flat provided you:

- Are a Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident who is at least 21 years old; and
- Satisfy the eligibility rules and conditions to own a flat.

## How to apply?
**For demise of joint owner**
Lodging a Notice of Death
For flats held under joint-tenancy, the remaining joint-owners can lodge the Notice of Death personally at [SLA's FAQ](https://www.sla.gov.sg/frequently-asked-questions-faqs) ( How do I lodge a Notice of Death to inform SLA of the death of a joint owner), appoint your own solicitor to lodge the Notice of Death on your behalf or engage HDB’s services to lodge the Notice of Death.
If you wish to engage HDB’s services to handle the Notice of Death,  you must bring along these documents to lodge a Notice of Death:
- Identity cards of remaining joint-owners
- Original death certificate or e-death certificate of deceased owner
- Title document (if any)
- Pay the registration and conveyancing fees at the point of application.
HDB’s Legal Group will then prepare the Notice of Death and inform the remaining joint-owners to sign the documents at the HDB Branch managing the flat.
**For demise of sole owner/tenant-in-common**
Grant of Probate
- If there is a will, the deceased's interest in the flat will be distributed according to the will. You will need the Grant of Probate.
- The deceased’s family should engage a private solicitor to apply for this court order, which gives legal authority to the Executor (the person named in the will) to manage the deceased's estate.
Grant of Letters of Administration
- If there is no will, the deceased’s interest in the flat will be distributed according to the provisions of the Intestate Succession Act. You will need the Grant of Letters of Administration.
- The deceased’s family should engage a private solicitor to apply for this court order, which gives legal authority to the Administrator to manage the deceased’s estate.

Once the Grant of Letters of Administration or the Grant of Probate has been obtained, you can engage your own solicitors or appoint HDB's solicitors to act for you to register your legal right as the Administrator or Executor. You may also approach the HDB Branch managing the deceased’s flat to make the necessary application with the following documents:

- Original copy of the Grant of Letters of Administration and Statement for Grant of Letters of Administration or Grant of Probate and will
- Original copy of the Syariah Court Inheritance Certificate (for Muslim estates only)
- A copy of the deceased owner’s death certificate or e-death certificate
- Title document of the deceased’s flat
- Identity card(s) of all flat owner(s) and Administrator(s) or Executor(s)

If you are an Administrator/ Executor and engage HDB's services to act for you in the transaction, you will have to:

- Sign  the relevant documents
- Pay fees (stamp fees, conveyancing fees, etc.)
- Apply to HDB to effect an ownership change of the flat upon completion of the transaction either via a change of flat ownership to eligible beneficiaries or a resale of part-share, subject to the beneficiaries meeting the eligibility conditions.

## Agency website
View more details on [HDB InfoWEB](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/home-ownership/change-of-flat-owners-or-occupiers/change-in-flat-ownership-not-through-a-sale).

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://go.gov.sg/hdb-write-to-us)

# Public Rental Scheme - Family Scheme

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/PUBLICRENTAL-FAMILY*

Provides heavily subsidised rental flats for Singaporean households with no other housing options and no family support.

## Highlights
- Subsidised rental flat from HDB
- Apply online via HDB's website

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Families, Rental flats

## About this support
Subsidised rental flat from HDB

## Who is this for?
- 21 years old and above
- Singapore Citizen
- Form a family nucleus with at least another SC or SPR. A family nucleus refers to one of the following:
  - You and your spouse
  - If single, you and your parents
  - If widowed/divorced, you and your children under your legal care and control
  - If orphaned, you and your siblings
- No family support and no other housing options. HDB will assess this based on your individual circumstances such as your household income, household size and housing budget
- Not existing HDB flat owners, essential occupiers, tenants under HDB’s rental schemes or private property owners
- For families with children below 21 years old, your application comes under the ComLink+ Rental Scheme, which offers customised support from government agencies and community partners

## How to apply?
- You can apply online at the [HDB website](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/renting-a-flat/public-rental-scheme/application-process/application-and-selection-of-rental-flat)
- You will need to provide the [required supporting documents](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/renting-a-flat/public-rental-scheme/application-process/application-and-selection-of-rental-flat)

[View more details](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/renting-a-flat/public-rental-scheme)

# Integrated Shield Plan (IP)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/D3cZDpbD*

A private medical insurance plan, offered by private insurers, that provides optional additional coverage on top of what you are already covered for under MediShield Life.

## Highlights
- IPs offers optional additional coverage on top of MediShield Life, targeted at covering unsubsidised care in public hospitals or private hospital bills
- The additional private insurance component of your Integrated Shield Plan premium is payable by MediSave, up to the Additional Withdrawal Limits

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Health Insurance

## About this support
- MediShield Life component:
  - Fully payable by MediSave
  - Sized for subsidised care (e.g B2 / C wards) in public hospital
- Additional private insurance component:
  - Payable by MediSave, but only up to the Additional Withdrawal Limits
  - Covers unsubsidised care (e.g. A, B1 wards) in public hospitals or private hospital bills

## Who is this for?
Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents

## How to apply?
- There are a variety of IPs with different levels of coverage
- When deciding whether to buy an IP, you should consider what you would like to be covered for and whether you can afford the plan, especially in the long term
- You may refer to [MOH, Comparison of Integrated Shield Plans](https://www.moh.gov.sg/healthcare-schemes-subsidies/medishield-life/comparison-of-integrated-shield-plans) or [Health Insurance Planner](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/planners/cpf-planner-health-insurance) for a comparison of IP benefits and long-term IP premiums across different plans

embedding_text:
Domains: Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits, Housing and shelters

# DigitalAccess@Home

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/DIGITALACCESS-HOME-SCHEME*

Provides subsidised broadband and laptops/tablets to lower-income households to support their lifestyle needs, including work and social activities.

## Highlights
- Subsidised fibre broadband for 3 years and/or subsidised laptop or tablet
- Apply online via www.digitalaccess.gov.sg or at any SG Digital community hub 

**Who it targets:** Low-income
**Keywords:** Lower-income, Subsidies

## About this support
- Subsidised fibre broadband, with monthly payment over 36 months
- Subsidised laptop or tablet, with one-time payment

## Who is this for?
To qualify for DigitalAccess@Home, you must meet all of the following criteria:

- Staying in a HDB flat
- At least one member of your household is a Singapore Citizen
- With a monthly household income (MHI) or per capita income (PCI) meeting either of the following conditions:
  Monthly household income (MHI)
  Monthly income per capita (PCI)
  No primary school student or person with disabilities in your household
  ≤ $1,900
  ≤ $650
  If there is a primary school student or person with disabilities in your household
  ≤ $3,400
  ≤ $900

You are encouraged to check your eligibility with the [online self-assessment tool](https://go.gov.sg/digitalaccesschecker) before applying.

## How to apply?
Only one application form per household is needed.

**Online submission**

- Step 1: [Visit IMDA's Digital Access Programme site](https://eservice.imda.gov.sg/das/homepage). Click on ‘For Applicant’ at the top menu bar
- Step 2: Log in with Singpass. The form will be prefilled with your information from our records. Complete the form and submit.
- Step 3: Household members have to give their consent for data collection via Singpass upon receipt of letter/SMS/email

**Hardcopy submission**

- Step 1: [Download the hardcopy](https://go.gov.sg/digitalaccess-application-form) or obtain a copy from your nearest [SG Digital community hub](https://go.gov.sg/supportgowhere-sdohubs)
- Step 2: Complete the form. Household members have to give their consent for data collection
- Step 3: Post completed form to: Info-communications Media Development Authority, 10 Pasir Panjang Road #03-01, Mapletree Business City, Singapore 117438

You will receive an update on your application via SMS/email in 10 working days. Alternatively, you can check your application status by logging into [www.digitalaccess.gov.sg](http://www.digitalaccess.gov.sg) with your SingPass.

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest SG Digital community hub](https://go.gov.sg/supportgowhere-sdohubs)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://eservice.imda.gov.sg/das/homepage)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://go.gov.sg/imda-feedback)

## Phone number
IMDA hotline: [6377 3800](tel:63773800)

# Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/PCTS*

From 2025 to 2028, the Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) scheme provides monthly cash payments to support eligible lower-income platform workers who make increased CPF Ordinary and Special/Retirement Account contributions.

## Highlights
- Monthly cash payments from 2025 to 2028 to support lower-income platform workers who see an increase in their share of Ordinary and Special/Retirement Account contributions 
- Lower-income platform workers who qualify for PCTS will automatically receive the payments; there is no need to apply
- Payments credited directly to PayNow NRIC-linked bank accounts, registered bank accounts or via GovCash

**Who it targets:** Low-income
**Keywords:** CPF, Platform Workers

## About this support
- Monthly cash payments from 2025 to 2028 to offset part of the year-on-year increase in the platform worker’s share of CPF Ordinary and Special/Retirement Account contributions for eligible lower-income platform workers.
- An [online PCTS calculator](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/calculators/platform-workers-cpf-transition-support-calculator) is available to estimate how much you can receive.

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizen only
- Born in 1995 or later, or born before 1995 and opted in to increase CPF contributions;
- Net income from platform work (i.e. gross earnings minus the Fixed Expense Deduction Amount) and other employment sources does not exceed $3,000 per month;
- Must have an increase in platform worker’s own share of CPF contributions to the Ordinary and Special/Retirement Account compared to the previous year

## How to apply?
Assessment for PCTS is automatic, no application is required.

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us)

# ComLink+

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/a7JTjGeT*

Empower lower-income families to achieve stability, self-reliance, and social mobility.

## Highlights
- Family coaches from MSF's Social Service Offices and case workers from Family Service Centres journey with families and support them as they work towards their long-term goals
- ComLink+ families will receive financial top-ups through ComLink+ Progress Packages when they take active steps towards their longer-term goals in the areas of preschool education, employment, debt clearance, and home ownership

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Budget 2026, Families, Lower-income

## About this support
Under ComLink+ Progress Packages, families that have taken active steps to improve their circumstances can receive:

- [New – from Q3 2026] Partnership Payout of $500 per quarter for continued engagement with their family coaches or case workers at Family Service Centres
- [Revised – from Q3 2026] Up to $250 per quarter for regular preschool attendance
- [Revised – from Q3 2026] Up to $1,250 per quarter for stable employment (based on CPF records)
- 1:1 matched debt repayment up to a limit of $5,000 in total debt repaid
- 2:1 matched CPF contribution to help families save up for purchase of flat
- [Revised - from Q3 2026] Total payouts across all ComLink+ Progress Packages are subject to a lifetime cap of $50,000

## Who is this for?
Families are eligible for ComLink+ if they have children under the age of 21 and are:

- Living in public rental housing (PRH); or
- Not living in PRH, but are eligible for KidSTART or have school-going children at risk of long-term absenteeism

## How to apply?
If you are eligible for ComLink+ but have not been approached to participate in the programme, please contact MSF or visit your nearest Social Service Office

## Where to go
Visit your nearest [Social Service Office](https://www.msf.gov.sg/our-services/directories#socialtab)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.msf.gov.sg/what-we-do/help-those-in-need/article/programmes/comlink)

Read the [AskGov FAQs on ComLink+](https://ask.gov.sg/msf?topic=ComCare&subtopic=ComLink+)

Domains: Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits

# MediSave Grant for Newborns (MGN) 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/dKO0Ow30*

All Singapore Citizen newborns are eligible for the MediSave Grant for Newborns (MGN) of up to $5,000.

## Highlights
-  MediSave Grant of $5,000 for Singapore Citizen Newborns
-  4% annual interest
-  Grant can cover MediShield Life premiums, vaccinations, hospitalisation and outpatient treatments

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Families, Parents

## About this support
- Up to $5,000 credited to each Singapore Citizen newborn's CPF MediSave account
- Accounts are opened automatically for newborns
- Covers MediShield Life premiums, recommended childhood vaccinations, hospitalisation, and approved outpatient treatments

## Who is this for?
- All Singapore Citizen newborns born on or after 26 August 2012 are eligible for MGN
- Children who are Singapore Citizens at birth and born before January 1, 2015, are entitled to MGN of up to $3,000
  - For those born on or after January 1, 2015, they are eligible for MGN of $4,000
  - For those born on or after April 1, 2025, they are eligible for MGN of $5,000
- Children who are born overseas can qualify for MGN upon registering their birth with Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) or through a Singapore Overseas Mission
  - The MGN amount will depend on the date that the child becomes a Singapore Citizen
  - Children who obtain Singapore Citizenship after the age of 2 are not eligible for MGN.

## How to apply?
- No application required
- The grant is automatically credited into your newborn’s MediSave account within 1 week from birth registration / acquiring Singapore citizenship
- Once the MGN has been credited, you will receive a notification on the MGN amount
- You may also check your child’s CPF statement online by logging into your [CPF](https://cpf.gov.sg/childdashboard) with your Singpass.

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us)

Note: By appointment only

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.madeforfamilies.gov.sg/support-measures/child-raising/healthcare/medisave-grant-for-newborns)

Domains: Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits, Healthcare and well-being

# MediSave for Assisted Conception Procedures 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/QDc9ihgy*

Allows eligible couples to withdraw up to $15,000 per patient from MediSave to pay for Assisted Conception Procedures (ACP) that aid them in conceiving.

## Highlights
- Withdraw a total of $15,000 per patient to support conception 
- Available at both private and public Assisted Reproduction centres 

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Families, Medical bills, Parents

## About this support
- Covers procedures such as in-vitro fertilisation and intra-uterine insemination and is available for both private and public Assisted Reproduction centres
- MediSave withdrawal limits vary accordingly for each ACP treatment cycle:
  - Up to $6,000 for the first ACP cycle
  - Up to $5,000 for the second ACP cycle
  - Up to $4,000 for the third and subsequent ACP cycles
- The total lifetime MediSave withdrawal limit is $15,000 per patient

## Who is this for?
- Only the MediSave of the patient and her spouse can be used
- If an ACP is not completed due to non-medical reasons, MediSave cannot be used to cover the costs of the incomplete cycle

## How to apply?
- Inform the Assisted Reproduction centre which you are receiving ACP treatment(s) at that you would like to use your MediSave to pay for your expenses
- The centre will submit the MediSave claims to CPF Board on your behalf for the treatment expenses

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us)

Domains: Family, parenting and relationships

# Fostering Scheme 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/VcxSSXs5*

Provides a safe and nurturing family environment for children needing care and protection, offering love, stability, and essentials like food and shelter. Foster families create positive family experiences, demonstrating care and concern, with the aim to reunite children with their birth families once safe to do so.

## Highlights
- Allows children in need to benefit from a nurturing home environment that facilitates their growth and enables them to fulfil their potential 
- Support services are available for foster families, including fostering allowance to defray the cost of caring for the child, training for foster parents, and support and guidance from Foster Care Worker and other professionals
- Aims to continue building up a diverse pool of foster parents to meet the different needs of foster children

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Families

## About this support
- Monthly fostering allowance of $1,100 for each foster child, or $1,500 for a child with special needs
- Childcare subsidies with a monthly co-payment of $200 for full-day care and $150 for half-day care to be paid by foster parents
- Student care subsidies with a monthly co-payment of $80 to be paid by foster parents for MSF-registered centres
- Medical subsidies cover medical treatment at public healthcare institutions (polyclinics, public hospitals, and public specialist centres)
  - Foster children also receive subsidies at participating CHAS General Practitioners and dental clinics
- Support and guidance from Foster Care Worker attached to every foster parent
- Training courses conducted by Social Service Institute for new foster parents
- Immediate support via an emergency hotline available 24/7
- Support groups and respite care available
- Foster parents enjoy childcare leave benefits, just as birth parents do under the Child Development Co-Savings Act and Employment Act

## Who is this for?
- At least 25 years old
- Married and applying as a couple
- Medically fit to care for children
- Minimum secondary school education
- Minimum monthly household income of $2,000 and per capita income of at least $700 (Retirees can apply to be assessed based on non-work sources of income and saving)
- Provide a child-safe home environment, which includes commitment not to use physical punishment, and installation of window grilles for foster children below 13 years old

## How to apply?
- Apply online through the [MSF Fostering Scheme portal](https://volunteer.gov.sg/scheme-detail?code=fostering):
  - Click "Apply"
  - Register or sign in
  - Fill in the application form
  - Upload supporting documents
- MSF or an appointed agency will contact you within three working days
- The assessment include:
  - Interview session(s)
  - Home Visit
  - Medical screenings
- After approval:
  - Attend mandatory training sessions
  - Await foster child placement

## Where to go
[512 Thomson Rd](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=298136)

[#11-00 MSF Building](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=298136)

[Singapore 298136](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=298136)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.msf.gov.sg/what-we-do/fostering/be-a-foster-parent/about-the-fostering-scheme)

[Submit an enquiry](mailto:fostering@msf.gov.sg)

## Phone number
MSF Consolidated Hotline: [1800-111-2222](tel:1800-111-2222) 
To reach the Fostering division, say "Foster" when prompted by the virtual assistant.

Domains: Family, parenting and relationships

# Government-Paid Paternity Benefit (GPPB) 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/yQfF0Pj8*

Provides up to 4 weeks of income support, for eligible working fathers who do not qualify for Government-Paid Paternity Leave (GPPL).

## Highlights
- For children born or adopted before 1 Jan 2024, eligible fathers can receive up to 2 weeks of Government-Paid Paternity Benefit (GPPB) , capped at $2,500 per week. 
- For children born or adopted on or after 1 Jan 2024, eligible fathers can receive up to 4 weeks of GPPB, capped at $2,500 per week. 
- For natural or adoptive fathers who do not qualify for GPPL due to their employment arrangement

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Cash assistance, Child care, Parents

## About this support
- Up to 2 weeks of income support for eligible fathers for child born/estimated delivery/FIA date before January 1, 2024, capped at $2,500 per week.
- Up to 4 weeks of income support for eligible fathers for child born/estimated delivery date/FIA on or after January 1, 2024, capped at $2,500 per week.

## Who is this for?
**For natural fathers with live births**:

- Your child’s date of birth/estimated delivery date is on or after 1 Jan 2021.
  - Your child is a Singapore Citizen or becomes one within 12 months of birth

**For natural fathers with stillbirths**:

- The date of stillbirth is on or after November 1, 2021
- Either you or the child’s mother is a Singapore citizen

**For adoptive fathers**:

- You are not the natural father of the child
- Your FIA date is on or after 1 Jan 2021
- The child must be below 12 months old on FIA date
- If child is not a Singapore citizen, a dependent’s pass (DP) has been issued and either you or your wife are Singapore citizens.

**Applicable to all**:

- Employed or self-employed for at least 90 days in the 12 months before child's birth
- Lawfully married to the child's mother between conception and birth or within 12 months of birth
- Not eligible for Government-Paid Paternity Leave (GPPL) except under specific conditions such as end of employment contract or retrenchment

## How to apply?
- Record employment or self-employment details for the 12 months before your child's birth or Formal Intent to Adopt (FIA) date.
- Submit your claim online [here](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/eservices/submit-a-claim) within 15 months of your child's birth or FIA date.
- An officer will contact you following your submission.

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/schemes/paternity-benefit)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://go.gov.sg/contact-gpls)

## Phone number

embedding_text:
Domains: Family, parenting and relationships

# Government-Paid Paternity Leave (GPPL) 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/qgZZZ5b3*

Provides up to 4 weeks of Government-Paid Paternity Leave (GPPL), for eligible working fathers.

## Highlights
- Up to 4 weeks of Government-Paid Paternity Leave (GPPL) for eligible fathers
- Government reimbursement/payment for GPPL capped at $2,500 per week, up to a total of $10,000 

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Paid leave, Parents

## About this support
**Child born/FIA/estimated delivery date before 1 Jan 2024**:

- Up to 2 weeks of Government-Paid Paternity Leave (GPPL) for fathers, to be taken within 12 months from the child's date of birth.
- Government reimbursement for all 2 weeks of GPPL, capped at $2,500 per week, up to a total of $5,000.

**Child born/FIA/estimated delivery date between 1 Jan 2024 and 31 Mar 2025 (both dates inclusive)**:

- Up to 4 weeks of Government-Paid Paternity Leave (GPPL) for fathers, to be taken within 12 months from the child's date of birth.
- Government reimbursement for all 4 weeks of GPPL, capped at $2,500 per week, up to a total of $10,000.
- Weeks 3-4 are additional, and employers can grant on a voluntary basis

**Child born/FIA/estimated delivery date on or after 1 Apr 2025:**

- Up to 4 weeks of Government-Paid Paternity Leave (GPPL) for fathers, to be taken within 12 months from the child’s date of birth.
- Government reimbursement for all 4 weeks of GPPL, capped at $2,500 per week, up to a total of $10,000.

## Who is this for?
**For natural fathers with live births**:

- Child born or estimated delivery date on or after January 1, 2017
- Child is a Singapore Citizen or becomes one within 12 months from birth
- Lawfully married to the child’s mother between conception and birth or within 12 months from birth
- Served employer for at least 3 months before child's birth
- For self-employed: Engaged in trade, business, profession, or vocation for at least 3 months before child's birth

**For natural fathers with stillborn children**:

- Stillbirth occurred on or after November 1, 2021
- Lawfully married to the child’s mother between conception and stillbirth or within 12 months from stillbirth, and either you or the child’s mother are Singapore citizens
- Served employer for at least 3 months before the date of stillbirth
- For self-employed: Engaged in trade, business, profession, or vocation for at least 3 months before the date of stillbirth

**For adoptive fathers**:

- Formal Intent to Adopt (FIA) date on or after January 1, 2017
- Not the natural father of the child
- If child is not a Singapore Citizen, either you or your wife must be a Singapore Citizen since the child's Dependant's Pass issuance
- Served employer for at least 3 months before FIA date
- For self-employed: Engaged in trade, business, profession, or vocation for at least 3 months before FIA date

## How to apply?
**For employees**:

- Notify your employer about your leave arrangement early.
- Submit the [declaration form (GPPL1)](https://file.go.gov.sg/gppl1form.pdf) to your employer with all necessary supporting documents.
- Apply for leave according to your employer's procedures.

**For self-employed**:

- Record your leave dates.
- Submit your claim online via the [Government-Paid Leave (GPL)](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/login?redirect=eservices/submit-a-claim) Portal within 3 months after your leave.
- Check your application status on the GPL Portal.

**For employers**:

- Obtain and verify the [declaration form (GPPL1)](https://file.go.gov.sg/gppl1form.pdf) from your employee.
- Keep the declaration form or records for 5 years from the last leave date.
- Submit your claim for reimbursement online via the GPL Portal within 3 months after your employee's leave.
- Check your application status on the GPL Portal.

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.profamilyleave.msf.gov.sg/schemes/paternity-leave)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://go.gov.sg/contact-gpls)

## Phone number
MSFCares: [1800 111 2222](tel:18001112222)

(say ‘GPLS’ when asked for the hotline you want to reach)

title: Marriage Preparation Programme for Minor and Young Muslim Couples
description: Provides pre- and post-marriage support for minor and young couples.
embedding_text:
Domains: Family, parenting and relationships

# Marriage Preparation Programme for Minor and Young Muslim Couples 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-EMSEFMAYMC*

Provides pre- and post-marriage support for minor and young couples.

**Who it targets:** Families
**Citizenship:** SG, PR
**Keywords:** Free, Marital and Divorce Support

## About this support
Supports minor and young couples through premarital consultation session, marriage preparation workshops, and parents support group.

## Who is this for?
Minor Couples (Mandatory to complete Marriage Preparation Programme before applying for marriage):

- Either party is below 21 years old
- At least one party is Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- Both bride and groom are Muslims

Young Couples:

- Groom is between 21 and 24 years old and bride is aged 21 years and above
- At least one party is Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- Both bride and groom are Muslims

## How to apply?
Call, email, visit or through referrals by other agencies to apply.

## What to expect?
**For minor couples**

- Sign up (email or call) directly with the agency for the mandatory (requried by law) complimentary Marriage Preparation Programme (MPP) before proceeding with marriage application via Registry of Muslim Marriages (ROMM) website.
- Upon completion of MPP, the agency will provide casework and counselling if necessary for up to 10 years and refer couples with higher risks to FSC or SSO.
- Eligible couples will also be auto-referred to KidStart. Those who prefer not to be auto-referred, can complete an opt out form instead for the agency to follow-up with them.

**For young couples**

- Similar as above, except that the MPP is not mandatory for young couples.
- They can apply e-file for marriage (OMJ) before attending MPP.
- Upon completion of the MPP, the other services offered to minor couples are applicable to young couples too.

embedding_text:
Domains: Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits

# Life Insurance Relief

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/cVkNdnyT*

Provides tax relief of up to $5,000 for individuals who paid annual insurance premiums on their own life insurance policies.

## Highlights
- Life Insurance Relief up to $5,000

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Insurance, Tax relief

## About this support
- Tax relief for your life insurance premiums
- If you are a married man, you may also claim the life insurance premium paid for your wife
- The amount of relief is capped between the lower of:
  - Difference between $5,000 and your CPF contribution; or
  - Up to 7% of the insured value of your own / your wife's life, or the amount of insurance premiums paid

## Who is this for?
To claim Life Insurance Relief, you must meet all the following conditions:

- You have paid, and are claiming, for your own life insurance policy
- Married men may also claim for premiums paid on their wife’s life insurance policy
- The insurance company has an office or branch in Singapore
  - The Singapore office of the insurance company should perform similar activities as the overseas company where the life insurance policy was purchased
- Your / your wife’s total CPF contributions for the following were less than $5,000 in the previous year:
  - Compulsory employee's CPF contribution
  - Compulsory MediSave or voluntary CPF contribution for self-employed individuals

## How to apply?
If you were previously approved for this relief last year (and your circumstances have not changed), the amount will be pre-filled and automatically granted. Please refer to the process for first-time applicants below to update your claim if there are changes.

For e-Filing:
For paper filing:
If this is your first time claiming this relief:
- Log in with your Singpass or [Singpass Foreign user Account (SFA)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/digital-services/others/singpass-foreign-user-account-(sfa)-for-foreign-individuals) at [myTax Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/login/selection)
- Navigate to “Individuals” > “File Income Tax Return”
- Select “File” to File Income Tax Return
- Go to “4. Deductions, Tax Reliefs and Rebates”
- Select “Add New” > “Life Insurance”
- Fill in the relevant information and select “Update”
- For Form B1 & B, fill in the “Life Insurance Relief” section
- If claiming for the first time, provide details of the premiums paid in Appendix 2

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.iras.gov.sg/contact-us/locate-us)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs/life-insurance-relief)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://www.iras.gov.sg/contact-us/individual-income-tax)

IRAS hotline: [1800-356-8300](tel:1800-356-8300)

embedding_text:
Domains: Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits

# Tax Payment Support

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/I0ZPVBeU*

Supports eligible individuals in their tax payments through various payment arrangements such as longer GIRO-based instalment plans.

## Highlights
- Enables longer payment plans for applicants experiencing difficulties in paying their taxes 
- Grants retirees the Extended Giro Scheme for Residential Property (Retirees), offering longer instalment plans for tax payment

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Long-term, Tax relief

## About this support
- Longer instalment plans may be made available for individuals or businesses facing financial challenges or other extenuating circumstances
- Eligible retirees may apply for the Extended Giro Scheme for Residential Property (Retirees), which provides a longer instalment plan of up to 24 months for property tax payment

## Who is this for?
For individuals who experience unexpected or extenuating circumstances due to the following:

- Financial issues
- High medical expenses
- Loss of employment or income
- Lawsuits
  - You may be required to submit documentary evidence to support your request for a longer instalment plan

For retirees:

- To be eligible for the Extended Giro Scheme for Residential Property (Retirees), applicants must meet all the following conditions:
  - You are residing in the property (and taxed at owner-occupier tax rates)
  - Your assessable income for Year of Assessment 2023 does not exceed $34,000
  - All property owners, including yourself, are aged 65 or above in 2024
  - There is outstanding property tax payable for the property

If applicants cease to be eligible, their extended instalment plan will be reverted to the standard instalment plan

## How to apply?
For individuals:
- Apply for an extended instalment plan via the 'Apply for Payment Plan' digital service through the IRAS [myTax Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg)
  - Please note that instalment plans are only available with GIRO
- For existing GIRO users, cancel your current plan and set up a new one. You may refer to this guide on [cancelling and reactivating GIRO for detailed instructions](https://www.iras.gov.sg/media/docs/default-source/uploadedfiles/pdf/steps-to-cancel-and-reactivate-giro---enf-webpages@18feb2020.pdf?sfvrsn=fbc17716_5)
- For applicants without a GIRO arrangement for Individual Income and Property Tax, you may apply for GIRO (with a DBS / POSB or OCBC bank account) via [myTax Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg) and set up your new plan online. Refer to [this guide](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/property-tax/property-owners/payments/experiencing-difficulties-in-paying-your-tax) for detailed instructions
For businesses without an existing GIRO arrangement for Corporate Income Tax, Property Tax and Goods and Services Tax:
- Apply for GIRO with a DBS / POSB, OCBC, UOB, Bank of China or Maybank account via the IRAS [myTax Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg)
- Arrange a new plan
- Alternatively, [you may refer to this guide for the detailed steps](https://www.iras.gov.sg/media/docs/default-source/uploadedfiles/pdf/eservice-user-guide_apply-for-payment-plan_non-individuals_2023-11.pdf?sfvrsn=31c2fac6_3)

Where you do not have account with any of the participating banks listed above, you may:

- Fill up [this form ](https://form.gov.sg/673c038018eb14d441d54153)to request for GIRO application form
- View on applying GIRO [here](https://www.iras.gov.sg/quick-links/payments/giro-individual-income-tax)

Please refer to [IRAS’ site on alternative tax payment plans for more details](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/property-tax/property-owners/payments/experiencing-difficulties-in-paying-your-tax)

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.iras.gov.sg/contact-us/locate-us)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/property-tax/property-owners/payments/experiencing-difficulties-in-paying-your-tax)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://www.iras.gov.sg/contact-us/property-tax)

# Parenthood Tax Rebate (PTR) 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/N8hHgjb3*

Provides a one-off tax rebate of up to $20,000 per child to eligible parents to encourage them to have more children.

## Highlights
- Tax rebate of up to $20,000 per child for eligible parents 
- Parenthood Tax Rebate (PTR) may be shared between parents based on an agreed apportionment 
- Unutilised balance can be carried forward to offset future tax payable and / or transferred between spouses 

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Families, Tax relief

## About this support
- Rebate amount increases for each child, with $5,000 for the first, $10,000 for the second and $20,000 for all subsequent children
- Parents may share the PTR based on an agreed apportionment
- Unutilised PTR will be carried forward to offset future income tax payable
  - It may also be transferred online via myTaxPortal between spouses

## Who is this for?
- Singapore tax residents who are married, divorced or widowed in the relevant year
- Different qualifying conditions for your child will apply based on the following:
  - Children born or adopted on or after 1 Jan 2008
  - Children born or adopted before 1 Jan 2008
    - Please note that PTR is not available for your first child as well as from your fifth child onwards
  - Child is a Singapore Citizen at the time of birth/marriage/legal adoption or within 12 months thereafter
- Additional conditions determining your eligibility are as follows:
  - Children given for adoption
  - If married is dissolved under a court order
  - If spouse passes away
- For more information on the qualifying conditions, please visit [IRAS’ PTR page](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs/parenthood-tax-rebate-(ptr))
- Applicants may use the [PTR Eligibility Tool](https://www.iras.gov.sg/docs/default-source/individual-income-tax/employees/ptr-calculator.xlsm?sfvrsn=e185c04f_17) to check their eligibility

## How to apply?
**For e-Filing:**

If this is your first time claiming this relief:

- Log in with Singpass or [Singpass Foreign user Account (SFA)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/digital-services/others/singpass-foreign-user-account-(sfa)-for-foreign-individuals) at [myTax Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/login/selection)
- Navigate to “Individuals” > “File Income Tax Return”
- Select “File” to File Income Tax Return
- Go to “4. Deductions, Tax Reliefs and Rebates”
- Select “Add New” > “Child/Parenthood Tax Rebate”
- Fill in the relevant information and select “Yes” under “Claim one-time Parenthood Tax Rebate (PTR) to indicate share of PTR as agreed by you and your Spouse"
- Select “Update"

If you have claimed this relief before, any unutilised balance will be carried forward automatically to offset future tax payable

**For paper filing:**

- Complete the particulars of your child in Appendix 2 of Form B1 & B if this is your first time claiming this relief
- If you have claimed this relief before, any unutilised balance will be carried forward without further action

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.iras.gov.sg/contact-us/locate-us)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs/parenthood-tax-rebate-(ptr))

[Submit an enquiry](https://www.iras.gov.sg/contact-us/individual-income-tax)

embedding_text:
Domains: Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits

# Working Mother's Child Relief (WMCR)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/3KmPKHA7*

Provides tax relief for eligible working mothers, up to 25% of earned income per child. Encourages married women to stay in the workforce after having children, and rewards families with children who are Singapore Citizens.

## Highlights
- Relief of up to 25% of working mother’s earned income per child or $12,000 per child 
- Receive cumulative tax relief for multiple children, up to 100% of your earnable income 

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Tax relief, Workers

## About this support
- Up to 25% of the mother's earned income can be claimed as tax relief for each child
- Relief amount is cumulative for multiple children, capped at 100% of the mother's earned income
- Relief may be claimed alongside the Qualifying Child Relief (QCR) or Child Relief (Disability) on the same child
- The total relief cap is $50,000 per child for all 3 combined

## Who is this for?
To be eligible for WMCR, you must fulfil all the following conditions in the previous year :

- You are a working mother who is married, divorced or widowed
- You have taxable earned income from employment, through pensions, trade or business, or via profession or vocation
- You have cared for a child who was a Singapore Citizen as at 31 December of the previous year and qualifies for QCR / Child Relief (Disability)
- You may read more on the [QCR and Child Relief (Disability) schemes and their criteria here](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs/qualifying-child-relief-(qcr)-child-relief-(disability)))
- You may still claim WMCR even for children who have passed away in the previous year

The amount of WMCR you may claim is based on child order.

Child order
WMCR amount from YA 2025
For a Qualifying Singaporean child born/adopted before 1 Jan 2024^
For a Qualifying Singaporean
child born/adopted
on or after 1  Jan 2024
1st
15% of mother's earned income
$8,000
2nd
20% of mother's earned income
$10,000
3rd and beyond
25% of mother's earned income
$12,000

^ WMCR percentages are added together if you claim for more than one child and the total is capped at 100% of the mother's earned income.

You may claim still WMCR even if you and / or your husband or ex-husband has already claimed the QCR / Child Relief (Disability) schemes on the same child. However, you must note the following conditions:

- QCR / Child Relief (Disability) claims must be utilised first (claims may be made by you or your spouse)
- The total relief cap (i.e. QCR / Child Relief (Disability) plus WMCR) is $50,000 per child
- The WMCR is limited to the remaining balance after the QCR / Child Relief (Disability) claim is allowed

## How to apply?
**For e-Filing:**
**For paper filing:**
- If you previously claimed WMCR last year and your circumstances remain unchanged, the relief amount will be pre-filled and automatically granted
- If claiming the relief for the first time:
  - Log in to [myTax Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/login/selection) using your Singpass or [Singpass Foreign user Account (SFA)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/digital-services/others/singpass-foreign-user-account-(sfa)-for-foreign-individuals)
  - Navigate to “Individuals” > “File Income Tax Return”
  - Select “File” to File Income Tax Return
  - Go to “4. Deductions, Tax Reliefs and Rebates”
  - Select “Add New” > “Child”
  - Fill in the relevant information and select “Yes” under “Claim Working Mother’s Child Relief”
  - Select “Update”
- Complete the section on “Child Relief” in Form B1 & B
- If it’s your first time claiming WMCR, indicate 'Y' under the “Claim for WMCR” column and fill in your child's details in Appendix 2 as well

The WMCR amount will be computed and applied automatically based on your eligibility when your Income Tax Return is processed.

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.iras.gov.sg/contact-us/locate-us)

[View more details](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs/working-mother's-child-relief-(wmcr))

embedding_text:

# Stamp Duty Remissions for Transfer of HDB Flats within Family 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/G1ZJdvwf*

Provides stamp duty remission for eligible transfers of HDB flats within families.

## Highlights
- Remission on BSD and SSD for HDB flat transfers among immediate family 

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** HDB households

## About this support
Remission of Buyer's Stamp Duty (BSD) and Seller's Stamp Duty (SSD) on transfer of HDB flat between immediate family members.

## Who is this for?
- The incoming lessee must be immediate family of any remaining lessee of the flat and a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- Repayment goes to the outgoing lessee's Central Provident Fund (CPF) account
- At least 1 of the flat’s current lessee remain after the transfer. Also, they must have either:
  - acquired the flat and paid stamp duty on its initial acquisition
  - acquired the flat via mutual exchange and paid stamp duty then
  - acquired the flat by assent, distribution or being pursuant to a will
  - acquired the flat via the right of survivorship as a joint tenant

## How to apply?
- Visit the [e-Stamping Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/estamping/) to e-Stamp and obtain the remission certificate
- In order to e-Stamp, you must prepare written confirmation from HDB that confirms that the incoming lessee will form a family nucleus with the remaining lessee and is authorised by HDB to stay in the flat
- If there is no incoming lessee, HDB confirmation is not required

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.iras.gov.sg/contact-us/locate-us)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/stamp-duty/for-property/appeals-refunds-reliefs-and-remissions/common-stamp-duty-remissions-and-reliefs-for-property/transfer-of-hdb-flats-within-family)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://www.iras.gov.sg/contact-us/stamp-duty-enquiries)

## Phone number
IRAS hotline: [1800-356-8300](tel:1800-356-8300)
