embedding_text:
Domains: Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits, Housing and shelters

# Stamp Duty Remissions for Married and Divorced Couples 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/gk4nIS14*

Provides various stamp duty remissions for eligible couples buying new residential property or transferring their current one(s) as part of matrimonial proceedings.

## Highlights
- Full Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) remission for couple’s joint purchase of first residential property 
- ABSD remission for a couple’s jointly purchased second property 
- Receive Buyer’s Stamp Duty (BSD), ABSD and Seller’s Stamp Duty (SSD) remissions when transferring property due to matrimonial proceedings 

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Home ownership, Marital and Divorce Support, Tax relief

## About this support
- For married couples:
  - Full ABSD remission for married couple’s joint purchase of their first residential property
  - Partial ABSD remission for married couple’s joint purchase of a second residential property
- For couples undergoing matrimonial proceedings:
  - Potential remission of BSD, ABSD and SSD on property transfers resulting from matrimonial proceedings

## Who is this for?
Please refer to the following table for the various conditions and scenarios where a couple may receive remissions:

Joint purchase of first residential property by married couple
While ABSD will be applicable upon stamping, you may apply for the ABSD remission instead if you meet these conditions:
- Married couple with at least 1 Singapore Citizen spouse
- Property must be jointly purchased under couple’s names only
- Both spouses do not already own any residential properties at the time of purchase
Joint purchase of second residential property by married couple
- ABSD has already been paid on the second property
- Married couple with at least 1 Singapore Citizen spouse
- Property must be jointly purchased under couple’s names only
- Couple must not own or have an interest in more than 1 residential property each when purchasing second property
- Couple’s first property must be sold within 6 months after either:
  - Date of purchase of the second property (for completed property)
  - Issue date of the Temporary Occupation Permit (TOP) / Certificate of Statutory Completion (CSC), whichever is earlier, if the property was uncompleted at the time of purchase
Couples undergoing matrimonial proceedings
- Transfer of property is due to either:
  - Court-ordered division of matrimonial assets (e.g. a proceeding for a decree of divorce, judicial separation or nullity of marriage under the law or religion)
  - Result of divorce proceedings
- Property must be transferred from 1 party to another (both involved in the matrimonial proceedings)
- Property may also be transferred by any child or children of the marriage / former marriage of the parties

## How to apply?
- For partial ABSD remission for married couple’s joint purchase of a second residential property:
  - Navigate [e-Stamping Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/estamping/) to "Request" > "Apply for Refund"
  - For “Sale & Purchase – Purchase/ Acquisition” forms submitted on or after 2 Jul 2023, ABSD will be automatically refunded to the purchasers, within 6 weeks from the stamping of the first property’s sale, without needing a refund application
  - For stampings before 2 Jul 2023, you must manually provide the Stamp Duties (Spouses) (Remission of ABSD) refund application via the [e-Stamping Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/estamping/) > "Request" > "Apply for Refund"
- For full ABSD remission for married couple’s joint purchase of their first residential property:
  - e-Stamp via the [e-Stamping Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/estamping/) to obtain the remission certificate
  - Alternatively, a legal representative, where engaged, will assist with the stamping

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.iras.gov.sg/contact-us/locate-us)

## Agency website
For Remission of ABSD for a Married Couple: [View more details](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/stamp-duty/for-property/appeals-refunds-reliefs-and-remissions/common-stamp-duty-remissions-and-reliefs-for-property/remission-of-absd-for-a-married-couple) 
For Matrimonial Proceedings: [View more details](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/stamp-duty/for-property/appeals-refunds-reliefs-and-remissions/common-stamp-duty-remissions-and-reliefs-for-property/matrimonial-proceedings)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://www.iras.gov.sg/contact-us/property-tax)

## Phone number
IRAS hotline: [1800-356-8300](tel:1800-356-8300)

# Remarriage Preparation Programme for Muslim Couples 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-RASP*

Provides pre- and post-marriage support for remarrying couples.

**Who it targets:** Families
**Citizenship:** SG, PR
**Keywords:** Free, Marital and Divorce Support

## About this support
Pre- and post-marriage support for remarrying couples and their dependent children (below 21) from previous marriage.

## Who is this for?
- One or both parties are marrying for the second time or more
- At least one party is Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- One or both parties contemplating marriage or already in a stepfamily have at least one dependent child (below 21 years of age); and
- Both parties contemplating marriage or already in a stepfamily, must be a Muslim.

## How to apply?
Call, email, visit or through referrals by other agencies to apply.

## What to expect?
- Email or call the agency directly to request for more information on the Marriage Preparation Programme (MPP) and marriage support services.
- Agency worker will assess and register them for MPP if they meet the criteria
- Upon completion of MPP, agency worker will refer to FSCs or SSOs if they have higher risks.
- Agency also refers eligible couples to KidStart.

# MediSave Maternity Package  

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/myy0wYU5*

Enables applicants to claim up to $3,670 for pre-delivery medical expenses and baby delivery expenses from MediSave.

## Highlights
- Covers both pre-delivery and delivery expenses as well as hospital charges 
- Medisave claims of up to $900 and $2,770 for pre-delivery and delivery expenses (depending on procedure) 

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Families, Medical bills, Parents

## About this support
- Claim up to $900 for pre-delivery medical expenses including pre-natal consultations, ultrasound scans, medications and tests
- An additional surgical withdrawal limit ranging from $1,120 to $2,770 depending on the type of delivery procedure
- Claim $1,130 per day for the first 2 days of hospital admission and $400 from the third day onwards

## Who is this for?
- Applicants must have a MediSave account
- Services must be provided by public or private healthcare institutions in Singapore

## How to apply?
- Submit pre-delivery medical bills to the hospital where the baby was delivered and inform the hospital that you would like to use your MediSave to pay for your expenses
- The hospital will submit the MediSave claims to CPF Board on your behalf for both pre-delivery and delivery expenses
- The claimable Medisave amount is capped by the total bill or withdrawal limit, whichever is lower

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us)

Note: By appointment only

[View more details](https://www.moh.gov.sg/healthcare-schemes-subsidies/marriage-and-parenthood-schemes)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/contact-us)

## Phone number
Healthcare Hotline: [1800 222 3399](tel:18002223399)

To avoid waiting on the line, you may book an appointment [here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/appt/oas/form).

title: CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS)
description: Provides CPF members an option to invest their OA and SA savings to enhance retirement funds.
highlights: Grants multiple options to invest your Ordinary Account (OA) and Special Account (SA) savings
embedding_text:
Domains: Financial support and benefits

# CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/Whq71CAX*

Provides CPF members an option to invest their OA and SA savings to enhance retirement funds.

## Highlights
- Grants multiple options to invest your Ordinary Account (OA) and Special Account (SA) savings  

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** CPF

## About this support
CPF members can invest their OA and SA savings in a [wide range of products](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/growing-your-savings/earning-higher-returns/investing-your-cpf-savings/cpf-investment-scheme-options) to enhance their retirement savings under the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS).

## Who is this for?
- To be eligible to invest in CPFIS, you must meet all the following criteria:
  - At least 18 years old
  - Not an undischarged bankrupt
  - Have more than $20,000 in OA and / or more than $40,000 in SA
  - Completed the [CPFIS Self-Awareness Questionnaire (SAQ)](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/growing-your-savings/earning-higher-returns/investing-your-cpf-savings/cpf-investment-scheme-self-awareness-questionnaire)
- If investing in the CPFIS-OA scheme, you may only invest up to 35% of your investible savings for stocks and 10% for gold. Investible savings refers to the sum of your OA balance and the amount of CPF you have withdrawn for investment and education.
- To find out how much of your OA and SA savings can be used for investment, you may:
  - Log in to [my cpf digital services](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/ds/dashboards/investment) with your Singpass, then select “my cpf” > “My dashboards” > “Investment”
  - Log in to the [CPF Mobile app](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/cpf-mobile-app) with your Singpass, then select “Investment”
  - Visit any CPF Service Centre with your identity card
- Upon reaching age 55, you can withdraw your CPFIS-OA and CPFIS-SA investments, as well as the cash balance in your Investment Account, after setting aside the Full Retirement Sum (FRS) in your Retirement Account
  - The FRS can be set aside fully with cash / or with cash (i.e. at least the Basic Retirement Sum) and property
- Once your withdrawal application is approved, your CPFIS investments will be transferred to you. The withdrawal will not result in liquidation of your investment holdings
- Your agent bank and / or product providers will contact you about transferring your investments to you

## How to apply?
- New CPFIS investors must first take the [Self-Awareness Questionnaire (SAQ)](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/growing-your-savings/earning-higher-returns/investing-your-cpf-savings/cpf-investment-scheme-self-awareness-questionnaire) before they can start investing
- The SAQ helps you to assess if you have basic financial knowledge and whether CPFIS is suitable for you
- To start investing under CPFIS-OA, open a CPF Investment Account with one of the following CPFIS agent banks:
  - Overseas-Chinese Banking Corporation Ltd (OCBC)
  - United Overseas Bank Ltd (UOB)
  - DBS Bank Ltd (DBS)
- After opening the account, approach product providers to buy or sell investments
- For CPFIS-SA:
  - Approach product providers directly to buy or sell investments

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/growing-your-savings/earning-higher-returns/investing-your-cpf-savings)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/feedback)

## Phone number
CPF hotline: [1800-227-1188](tel:1800-227-1188)

To avoid waiting on the line, you may book an appointment [here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/appt/oas/form).

highlights: Receive CPF monthly payouts for as long as they live, under CPF LIFE
Application must be submitted within 1 year from date of completion of the second housing transaction
embedding_text:
Domains: Financial support and benefits, Financial/Retirement Planning, Housing and shelters, Retirement and legacy planning

# Silver Housing Bonus (SHB)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/SHB*

Seniors aged 55 or above may receive cash bonus when they right-size to a 3-room or smaller HDB flat, and top-up the proceeds from the sale of their existing property into their CPF Retirement Account (RA) and join CPF LIFE.

## Highlights
- Receive CPF monthly payouts for as long as they live, under CPF LIFE
- Application must be submitted within 1 year from date of completion of the second housing transaction

**Who it targets:** Seniors
**Keywords:** Cash assistance, CPF payouts

## About this support
- With effect from 1 December 2025, the SHB has been enhanced to provide greater support to seniors.
- Seniors can supplement their retirement income if they right-size from a HDB flat or private residential property with an Annual Value (AV) up to $31,000 and buy a 3-room or smaller HDB flat.
- Seniors who commit to a net increase of up to $60,000* in their CPF RA after right-sizing, with the sum going towards their retirement payouts, can qualify for an SHB amount of $30,000. They can do so using their CPF housing refunds**, if sufficient, and may no longer need to make the top-up in cash.
- They can qualify for an additional $10,000 cash bonus if they right-size to a 2-room or smaller flat, including a Community Care Apartment (CCA). This additional $10,000 bonus applies regardless of the amount they commit to their CPF RA.
- Overall, the maximum SHB amount that eligible seniors may receive is $40,000. Visit [HDB InfoWEB](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/retirement-planning/monetising-flat-for-retirement/silver-housing-bonus) for more details

* The net increase to commit in your CPF RA depends on the net sale proceeds and is capped at $60,000 per household. It is further capped by the prevailing Full Retirement Sum (FRS).

** CPF principal amount withdrawn to purchase a property and the accrued interest that needs to be refunded after selling the property.

## Who is this for?
- At least 1 owner must be a Singapore Citizen (SC)
- The SC is aged 55 or above
- Monthly household income not more than $16,000
- Existing property is an HDB flat (met minimum occupation period for resale flat), or a private residential property with an Annual Value of up to $31,000
- No concurrent ownership or interest in a private residential property or in more than 1 non-residential property

Other conditions:

- Next property you are buying is a 3-room (excluding 3-room terrace) or smaller flat from HDB or from the resale market
- You must have positive net sale proceeds
- Booking of new HDB flat or application to buy resale flat must either be before sale of existing residential property, or within 12 months of completing the sale of the existing residential property
- SHB application must be submitted within 1 year from the legal completion date of the second housing transaction (either the purchase or sale)

## How to apply?
- Learn about your eligibility for this scheme (and other housing monetisation options) and the estimated monthly payouts you can receive via [HDB’s 'Check Housing Monetisation Option' e-Service](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/BR05AWEnquireHMOptions)
- To apply:
  - Enquire with our Customer Relations Executive during the appointment for second housing transaction (either resale completion or new flat keys collection appointment)
  - HDB will then schedule a financial counselling session where all the details and information such as the CPF top-up amount, bonus and the monthly payout amount would be shared during the session

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/retirement-planning/monetising-flat-for-retirement/silver-housing-bonus)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/write-to-us)

## Phone number
HDB Hotline: [6866-3066](tel:6866-3066)

embedding_text:
Domains: Financial support and benefits

# ComCare Assistance

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/COMCARE-SMTA*

Provides financial support for individuals and families facing varied challenges, ensuring timely aid for both short-term and long-term needs.

## Highlights
- Cash assistance for lower-income individuals or families
- [If relevant] Assistance for household and medical expenses
- [If relevant] Provides other support such as employment assistance or social support services

**Who it targets:** Low-income, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Cash assistance, Lower-income, Short-to-medium term

## About this support
**Interim Assistance**

Provides immediate financial assistance for lower-income individuals or families who require urgent and temporary financial relief. Assistance provided will depend on the household situation.

Interim Assistance will be enhanced and administered by MSF and the People’s Association. Applications can be made from 17 August to 31 December 2026.

**Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance**

Provides temporary financial assistance for lower-income individuals or families who are temporarily unable to work, looking for a job or earning a low income and require assistance.

- Monthly cash assistance for living expenses
- Assistance with your household bills, i.e. rental, utilities, and/or service and conservancy charges
- Medical assistance​ at public healthcare institutions
- Employment assistance such as job search and/or training
- Referrals for other relevant services

**Long-Term Assistance**

Provides long-term support to those permanently unable to work due to old age, illness or disability, and have inadequate family support or savings to rely on for daily needs.

- Monthly cash assistance for living expenses
- Assistance with medical expenses at public healthcare institutions
- Free or highly subsidised access to social support services
- LTA assistance rates according to household size:
  **Household Size**
  **Current Rates**
  **Increased Rates**
  **(From April 2025)**
  1 person
  $640
  $760
  2 persons
  $1,080
  $1,250
  3 persons
  $1,510
  $1,760
  4 persons
  $1,930
  $2,230

## Who is this for?
- You must be a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident (at least one member in the same household must be a Singapore Citizen).
- Households with a monthly household income per capita of $800 and below.

**Interim Assistance**

- Greater flexibility will be exercised in assessing income eligibility.

**Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance**

- Have little or no family support, savings or assets to rely on for your daily needs.
- Looking for work or temporarily unable to work due to illness or needing to care for children, elderly or other dependants.
- Even if your income exceeds these guidelines, you can still approach a Social Service Office (SSO) for assessment if you face financial difficulties. The SSOs will assess each household’s needs, such as employment, family and finances, to ensure that the assistance we provide is holistic.

**Long-Term Assistance**

- Unable to work because of old age, illness or disability.
- Elderly persons who receive a small monthly payout from sources such as CPF Retirement Sum / CPF Life.
- Elderly persons whose children are low income themselves i.e. monthly household income per capita of $800 and below.

## How to apply?
**Interim Assistance**

To apply:

- Online via [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.gov.sg/grants/smta)
- Alternatively, you may approach the following Community Partners :
  - [Social Service Offices](https://www.msf.gov.sg/our-services/directories#socialtab)
  - Community Clubs / Centres

**Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance / Long-Term Assistance**

Watch this [ComCare Financial Assistance Application Instructions video ](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fRiYpEAhIhw)which provides applicants with information on the requirements of the ComCare application process and applicants' responsibilities while on assistance.

To apply:

- Online via [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.gov.sg/grants/smta)
- Alternatively, visit your [nearest Social Service Office](https://www.msf.gov.sg/our-services/directories#socialtab) to apply in person.

Each SSO administers ComCare financial assistance and helps applicants to access other forms of assistance they may need, such as employment assistance or family services.

You'll need to provide:

- Updated bank account passbooks / account summary / bank balance enquiry slips or similar for **all members**, clearly showing the latest bank balance in the last month
- Other supporting documents, **if relevant**:
  - Your identity card or birth certificate for **all members**
(Note: NRIC/FIN of main applicants will not be required for online applications as the login will be via Singpass. If applicant / household / other family member had provided these identification documents in earlier ComCare applications, they will not be required again.)
  - Latest utility bill(s) (e.g. Singapore Power (SP), private electricity retailers)
  - Latest Medical Certificate (with duration and fitness for work status)
  - Pay-slips / Employment contract (for employment without CPF contributions)
  - Latest employment / termination letter (for recent changes in employment status)
  - Insurance Letter (for lump-sum / regular payouts by private insurer)
  - Any other supporting documents

The collection, use or disclosure of personal data of relevant individuals was applied in the development of policies and services for lower-income households. In addition to the Personal Data Protection Act, there exists strict policies, processes and safeguards in place to ensure the proper use and protection of personal data by the Government.

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest Social Service Office](https://www.msf.gov.sg/our-services/directories#socialtab)

## Agency website
[ComCare Assistance](https://www.msf.gov.sg/what-we-do/comcare)

## Email / Form
[Ask_SSO@msf.gov.sg](mailto:Ask_SSO@msf.gov.sg)

## Phone number
ComCare Hotline: [1800 222 0000](tel:1800-222-0000)

# Workfare Skills Support (WSS) (Basic)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/WSS*

Provides training allowance and cash incentives to encourage lower-wage Singaporean workers to upskill via training.

## Highlights
- Provides training allowance for trainees who self-sponsor their own short training
- Provides cash award for trainees who complete sustained training
- Provides absentee payroll for employers who send eligible employees for training
- No application required for employees; self-employed persons and employers should submit claims online

**Who it targets:** Low-income
**Keywords:** Budget 2026, Trainings, Workers

## About this support
- Training Allowance (TA) of $10.50 per training hour for self-sponsored trainees
- Training commitment award of $800 for one Workforce Skills Qualification (WSQ) or Academic Continuing Education and Training Qualification
- Absentee payroll for employers sending eligible employees for training: 95% trainee’s basic hourly wage, capped at $13 per training hour
- WSS (Basic) supports short training, such as:
  - Eligible courses at the [MySkillsFuture Portal](https://www.myskillsfuture.gov.sg/content/portal/en/portal-search/portal-search.html?fq=Course_Supp_Period_To_1:[2026-06-25T00:00:00Z TO *]&fq=IsValid:true&fq={!tag=Tags_text_Filtered}Tags_text_Filtered:("Workfare_Training Commitment" "Workfare_Training Allowance")&q=*:*&filtersearch=Tags_text_Filtered:)
  - Recommended courses that meet Progressive Wage Model (PWM) training requirements

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizen;
- At least 30 years old or older as of 31 December of the preceding year, or at least 13 years old for persons with disabilities;
- Earn an average gross monthly income of not more than $3,000 for the past 12 months;
- Have declared your net trade income and made MediSave contributions in full if you are self-employed;
- Live in a property with an annual value of $21,000 and below as at 31 December of the preceding year;
- Own not more than one property; and
- If you are married:
  - you and your spouse together not own more than one property; and
  - the assessable income of your spouse does not exceed $70,000 of the preceding Year of Assessment

** **

The above is similar to the [**Workfare Income Supplement**](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/growing-your-savings/government-support/workfare-income-supplement) (WIS) criteria.

## How to apply?
**Employees**

No application needed.

** **

**Self-employed persons**

You will need to provide in the [TA claim form](https://go.gov.sg/wss-sep-ta) within 120 days of course end date:

- softcopy of your proof of self-employment (for example, contract for service or equivalent dated within 3 months after course end date, or ACRA business registration and business transaction documents dated within 3 months after course end date)
- your course details (for example, course title, course start and end dates, and training provider’s name

**Employers**

You can [apply online at Enterprise Portal for Jobs and Skills](https://sfec.enterprisejobskills.gov.sg/Callbackhandler/Prelogin.aspx)

# SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/SFC-MID-CAREER*

For Singapore Citizens aged 40 and above to pay for or offset the out-of-pocket course fees for selected courses that are oriented towards meeting industry and employment needs.

## Highlights
- Can be used on top of existing SWDA course fee subsidies
- Singapore Citizens aged 40 and above as of 1 Jan 2024 received the top-up in May 2024
- Singapore Citizens turning 40 years old after 2024 will receive their SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career) top-up of S$4,000 in end-January of the same year

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Budget 2024, Mid-career

## About this support
- Singapore Citizens aged 40 and above as of 1 Jan 2024 received the SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career) top-up of S$4,000 in May 2024. The credit will not expire. In addition, the outstanding balance from Additional SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career Support) top-up in 2020 is now merged with SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career).
- Singapore Citizens turning 40 years old after 2024 will receive their SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career) top-up of S$4,000 in end-January of the same year.
- Can be used on top of existing Skills & Workforce Development Agency (SWDA) course subsidies to pay for selected courses which are oriented towards meeting industry and employment needs

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizen
- Aged 40 and above

## How to apply?
- Starting from 1 May 2024, the SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career) top-up of $4,000, which does not expire, can further offset nett course fees for [selected courses](https://www.myskillsfuture.gov.sg/content/portal/en/training-exchange/course-directory.html?q=Tags:"SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career)"&search=true&jumpstart=false) that have better employability outcomes.

# GRaduate Industry Traineeships (GRIT)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/yYmSnTml*

Equips fresh graduates with experience and skills, easing their transition into full-time employment.

## Highlights
- Offers up to 800 structured traineeships across various sectors for 3 to 6 months
- Monthly allowance ranging from S$1,800 to S$2,400, co-funded by the government and host organisations

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Employment Support and Vocational Training, Jobseekers, Recent graduates

## About this support
Jointly introduced by the Ministry of Manpower (MOM), Skills & Workforce Development Agency (SWDA), GRIT provides fresh graduates with meaningful traineeships in both private companies and public agencies, enhancing their employability and work readiness.

## Who is this for?
All trainees must fulfil the following criteria:

- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident; and
- Graduated or graduating in 2024, 2025 or 2026 from Universities, Polytechnics, Institute of Technical Education (ITE) and other Educational Institutions (e.g. private universities and overseas institutions); or
- Graduated earlier from above institutions and completed National Service in 2024, 2025 or 2026.** **
- Applicants must have no prior working experience and must be prepared to commit to a full-time traineeship.

## How to apply?
Traineeship opportunities will be progressively made available on [MyCareersFuture.](https://www.mycareersfuture.gov.sg/)

- Full-time attachment programme of 4 to 6 months with training allowance with approved host organisations

$1,800 to $3,800

70% of the training allowance

- All Singaporeans and Permanent Residents aged 40 and above

# Staggered Downpayment Scheme

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/OAn8RIRG*

Eases home purchase by allowing eligible first-timer couples and right-sizing flat owners to pay downpayment in 2 parts.

## Highlights
- Ease home purchase by splitting flat downpayment into two parts 
- Can pay in cash and / or CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings  

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** HDB households, Home ownership

## About this support
- Downpayment split into 2 instalments for easier financial management
- First instalment is paid at the signing of the Agreement for Lease and is either 5% or 10% of the purchase price (depending on your choice of housing loan)
- Second instalment is paid at key collection and is either 20% or 35% of the purchase price (depending on your choice of housing loan and the Loan-To-Value (LTV) limit)
- Can be paid in cash and / or CPF OA savings (including CPF housing grant, if eligible), depending on loan type
- For flat applications received from young couples eligible for deferred income assessment from the Jun 2024 sales exercise:
  - First instalment is capped at 2.5% of the purchase price
  - Second instalment is either 22.5% or 42.5% of the purchase price (depending on your choice of housing loan and the LTV limit)
  - Applicants who acquire a housing loan with a 75% or 55% LTV limit from a Financial Institution will have to pay at least 5% or 10% of the purchase price or value (whichever is lower) in cash before disbursement

## Who is this for?
- First-timer couples, including those with 1 second-timer applicant
- Valid HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter obtained on or before the younger applicant's 30th birthday
- Booked an uncompleted 5-room or smaller flat in any HDB sales exercise
- Flat owners right-sizing to a 3-room or smaller flat in non-mature estates who have not completed the sale of their existing flat at the time of HFE letter application and booked an uncompleted 3-room or smaller flat in a non-mature estate in any HDB sales exercise

## How to apply?
Buyers will be informed during the flat booking appointment if they are eligible.

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/bto-sbf-and-open-booking-of-flats/process-for-buying-a-new-flat/sign-agreement-for-lease)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](http://go.gov.sg/hdb-write-to-us)

## Phone number
HDB Hotline: [6866-3066](tel:6866-3066)

# Fresh Start Housing Scheme

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/FRESH-START*

Helps families with children who are currently living in public rental flats to own a 2-room Flexi flat or 3-room flat on a shorter lease.

## Highlights
- Enhanced CPF Housing Grant of up to $120,000 for eligible first-timer families
- Fresh Start Housing Grant of $75,000 for eligible second-timer families 
- Resale levy cap of $30,000 for eligible second-timer families
- HDB Concessionary Loan is subject to credit assessment

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Budget 2025, Home ownership, Housing grants

## About this support
**Both first-timer and second-timer families**

- Purchase a 2-room Flexi or 3-room Standard flat on a shorter lease in HDB sales launches i.e. Build-To-Order (BTO) or Sale of Balance Flats (SBF) exercises, or open booking of flats
- HDB Concessionary Loan is subject to credit assessment

**First-timer families**

- Enhanced CPF Housing Grant of up to $120,000

**Second-timer families**

- Fresh Start Housing Grant of $75,000 ($60,000 will be disbursed into CPF Ordinary Accounts before key collection; $15,000 may be disbursed after key collection into CPF Ordinary Accounts over 5 years)
- Resale levy cap of $30,000

## Who is this for?
- Have at least 1 parent and 1 child who are Singapore Citizens
- Applicant and spouse (if applicable) must be aged at least 35 and below 55 years old
- Child must be aged below 21
- Household monthly income of $7,000 and below
- Stayed in public rental flat for at least 1 year
- Have occupied public rental flat for at least 1 year, without accumulating 3 or more months of rental arrears in the preceding 12 months
- Have not received any public rental tenancy discount under Relocation, Sale of Flat to Sitting Tenants, or Rent & Purchase Schemes
- Do not own other properties overseas or locally, and have not disposed of any within the last 30 months

## How to apply?
You can apply online at the [HDB website](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/AA11AWFreshStartAppWeb/AA11PFreshStartNote).

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/bto-sbf-and-open-booking-of-flats/process-for-buying-a-new-flat/application/fresh-start-housing-scheme)

# Lease Buyback Scheme

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/LEASE_BUYBACK*

Provides seniors with a steady stream of retirement income when they sell the tail-end of their flat lease to HDB while they continue to occupy the flat for the lease they retained.

## Highlights
- Receive monthly payouts and continue to stay in the flat for the lease retained when you sell the tail-end lease of your flat to HDB
- Application takes about 3 months to complete from the date of interest to proceed
- Make an e-appointment with HDB for a preliminary financial counselling session

**Who it targets:** Seniors
**Keywords:** CPF payouts, Seniors

## About this support
- Sell part of your flat's lease to HDB and choose to retain the length of lease based on the age of the youngest owner
- Proceeds from selling part of your flat's lease will be used to top up your CPF Retirement Account (RA), and you can use your CPF RA to join CPF LIFE, which will provide you with a monthly income for life

## Who is this for?
- At least 1 owner must be a Singapore Citizen
- All owners 65 years and older
- Monthly household income not more than $14,000
- No concurrent ownership of second property, and no more than 1 non-residential private property
- All owners have been living in the flat for at least 5 years, or 10 years for Plus or Prime flats
- Flat has at least 20 years of lease to sell to HDB

## How to apply?
- Learn about your eligibility for this scheme (and other housing monetisation options) and the estimated monthly payouts you can receive via [HDB’s 'Check Housing Monetisation Option' e-Service](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/BR05AWEnquireHMOptions)
- To apply:
  - Make an [appointment](http://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/BF13AWAppointmentWeb/branch) with an HDB Branch office
  - Log in with or without Singpass
  - Click on 'Make a new appointment'
  - Select 'Lease Buyback Scheme'
  - Then 'Enquiry'

[View more details](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/retirement-planning/monetising-flat-for-retirement/lease-buyback-scheme-lbs)

# GRaduate Industry Traineeships @Gov (GRIT@Gov)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/uX75MUE0*

Equips fresh graduates with experience and skills, easing their transition into full-time employment.

## Highlights
- 3 to 6-month traineeships in Public Service for fresh graduates 
- Enables fresh graduates to gain useful skills and experience through short-term traineeships
- Trainees receive a monthly training allowance ranging from S$1,800 to $2,400 

**Who it targets:** Families
**Keywords:** Employment Support and Vocational Training, Jobseekers, Recent graduates

## About this support
The GRaduate Industry Traineeships @Gov (GRIT@Gov) Programme supports fresh graduates in gaining experience and skills, to facilitate their transition into full-time employment. GRIT@Gov offers traineeships for fresh graduates within public sector agencies.

Trainees will receive a monthly training allowance ranging from S$1,800 to $2,400 for the duration of the traineeship. This training allowance may vary depending on the scope of each traineeship.

## Who is this for?
All trainees must fulfil the following criteria:

- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident; and
  - Graduated or graduating in 2024, 2025 or 2026 from Universities, Polytechnics, Institute of Technical Education (ITE) and other Educational Institutions (e.g. private universities and overseas institutions); or
  - Graduated earlier from above institutions and completed National Service in 2024, 2025 or 2026.** **
  - Applicants must have no prior working experience and must be prepared to commit to a full-time traineeship.

Trainees who complete their studies from Universities, Polytechnics, the Institute of Technical Education (ITE) or other Educational Institutions within 2026 but who will only receive their qualification/certification award in 2027 are eligible for the programme as well.

## How to apply?
Browse and apply for GRIT@Gov traineeships via [Careers@Gov](https://jobs.careers.gov.sg/?s=grit@gov&utm_source=c@gshopfront&utm_medium=click&utm_id=grit-gov).

If you are a fresh graduate who is considering a role in the Public Service, check out our [Early Careers](https://www.careers.gov.sg/join-us/early-careers/?utm_source=gritgovpage&utm_medium=website&utm_campaign=gritgovprog) page.

To view all vacancies across the Public Service (including for mid-careerists), please visit our [Careers@Gov job portal](https://jobs.careers.gov.sg/?utm_source=gritgovpage&utm_medium=website&utm_campaign=gritgovprog).

## Agency website
[View more details ](https://www.careers.gov.sg/join-us/grit-gov/)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://form.gov.sg/6603c569d4c3dae8e1eaf228)

Domains: Caregiving, Financial support and benefits, Financial/Retirement Planning, Retirement and legacy planning

# Withdrawal of CPF Savings on Reduced Life Expectancy

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/RLE*

Members with reduced life expectancy due to a medical condition, as certified by an accredited doctor (from public hospitals, polyclinics, or a specialist), may apply to withdraw some of their CPF savings. Severe medical conditions causing them to be permanently unfit for work or to lack mental capacity permanently can also be considered.

## Highlights
- Withdraw $5,000 or more, depending on extent of your reduced life expectancy 
- Lump sum as well as monthly payouts from your Retirement Account, if applicable
- Apply via CPF e-service and approach the Medical Institution to complete the Medical Assessment Report 

**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Cash assistance, CPF payouts, PWDs

## About this support
- Depending on the extent of your reduced life expectancy and your CPF balances, you may withdraw a lump sum of $5,000^ or more
- You may also need to set aside a reduced retirement sum in your Retirement Account (RA), from which you will receive monthly payouts

^ Excludes monies received under the Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme and Matched Retirement Savings Scheme, government grants and your MediSave Account savings.

## Who is this for?
Singapore Citizen (SC) and Permanent Resident (PR) who have any of the following conditions as certified by an accredited doctor:

- Severely reduced life expectancy due to medical condition
- Permanently unfit for work
- Permanently lack mental capacity to make decisions, as defined in the Mental Capacity Act

## How to apply?
**Applying for self**

- Submit [an online application](https://cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/withdraw-cpf-due-to-reduced-life-expectancy-and-claim-insurance) after logging in with your Singpass

- Download the form “Medical Assessment Report” that is provided upon submission of the online application and have it completed by an [accredited doctor](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/who-is-considered-an-accredited-doctor). Thereafter, please request the medical institution to submit the completed medical assessment report to CPF Board directly (instructions are provided within the form).
- If you are mailing your documents from overseas, all documents must be witnessed/certified true by an official of a Singapore Overseas Mission with his official seal/stamp duly affixed.

**Applying as a donee or deputy for your next-of-kin**

Submit [this form](http://cpf.gov.sg/applyrlehpsdps) with a copy of your NRIC attached and provide the following original documents to CPF Board:

- Medical report from an [accredited doctor](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/who-is-considered-an-accredited-doctor) stating that the member lacks mental capacity permanently;

- Lasting Power of Attorney or Court Order; and

- Statement for the bank account held on trust on behalf of the member.

Make [an appointment](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us) to visit any of our CPF Service Centres to submit the above original documents or mail them to:

CPF Board 
Retirement Withdrawals Department (RWD) 
Privy Box No. 920651

Singapore 929292

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us) 
Note: By appointment only

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/retirement-income/retirement-withdrawals/withdrawing-on-reduced-life-expectancy)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://cpf.gov.sg/contact-us)

## Phone number
CPF Hotline: [1800 227 1188](tel:18002271188)

To avoid waiting on the line, you may book an appointment [here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/appt/oas/form).

# Withdrawal of CPF Savings for Immediate Needs from Age 55 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/7c13MJjn*

CPF members can make withdrawals from their CPF savings starting from age 55.

## Highlights
- CPF members can make withdrawals from their CPF savings starting from age 55 
- Generally, members who turn 55 can withdraw at least $5,000 or any amount in excess after setting aside their Full Retirement Sum (FRS)
- Members who own an eligible property have the flexibility to set aside their FRS with a mixture of property and cash, and withdraw their Retirement Account savings above the Basic Retirement Sum    

**Who it targets:** Seniors
**Keywords:** Cash payouts, CPF

## About this support

## Who is this for?
Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents aged 55 and above.

# CPF LIFE 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/wEfmIVLx*

CPF Lifelong Income For the Elderly (CPF LIFE) is a national longevity insurance annuity scheme that provides you with monthly payouts no matter how long you live.

## Highlights
- Monthly payouts for life  
- Offers various plans to suit individual preferences and needs 
- Option to start payouts at a later age up to age 70, where monthly payouts will increase by up to 7% for each year of deferral

**Who it targets:** Seniors
**Keywords:** CPF payouts

## About this support
- Provides a lifelong monthly payout to protect against outliving one’s savings
- Unlike private annuity plans, which are subject to investment market returns, CPF LIFE monies are guaranteed by the government and earn a risk-free interest of up to 6% per annum
- Offers various plans to suit individual preferences and needs:

Escalating Plan
Increasing monthly payouts to help you maintain your lifestyle when prices increase.
Standard Plan
Steady monthly payouts even if you may have to keep within a fixed budget and adjust your lifestyle when prices increase.
Basic Plan
Payouts that will get progressively lower when balances fall below $60,000. You may have to lower your lifestyle further when prices increase.

- Option to start payouts at a later age to receive up to a 7% increase in monthly payout.

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident born in 1958 and after, with at least $60,000 in the Retirement Account when you start your monthly payouts, will be automatically included in CPF LIFE
- If you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident who is not automatically included in CPF LIFE, you can still choose to join CPF LIFE as long as you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, anytime from 65 to one month before you reach 80
- You can choose to be exempted from CPF LIFE if you have a pension or private annuity plan that pays the same or higher monthly payouts than as CPF LIFE

## How to apply?
- CPF Board will send you a notification three months before your 65th birthday on the options you have about your CPF savings and how you can make an informed decision using the Plan my monthly payouts service
- If you have not instructed the CPF Board regarding your payouts by then, your payouts will automatically start when you turn 70 under the LIFE Standard Plan

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us)

Domains: Financial support and benefits, Financial/Retirement Planning, Retirement and legacy planning

# Matched Retirement Savings Scheme 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/FcwgSMsK*

Helps eligible Singaporeans with lower retirement savings to save more by matching cash top-ups made to their Retirement or Special Accounts (RA/SA). This will boost their monthly payouts in retirement.

## Highlights
- Dollar-for-dollar matching grant on cash top-ups to your RA/SA of up to $2,000 per year
- Boost CPF retirement savings and monthly payouts 
-  Earn CPF interest rates of up to 6% per annum on cash top-ups

**Who it targets:** Seniors
**Keywords:** Budget 2025, CPF top-ups

## About this support
- The Government will match every dollar of cash top-ups made to the RA/SA of eligible Singaporeans of up to $2,000 per year, with a $20,000 cap over an eligible member’s lifetime
- The matching grant will automatically be credited to the RA/SA of the eligible member at the beginning of the following year
- Eligible Singaporeans will enjoy [interest rates of up to 6% per annum](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/growing-your-savings/earning-higher-returns/earning-attractive-interest) on the cash top-up and matching grant, enhancing their retirement payouts
- Cash top-ups that attract the MRSS matching grant will not qualify for tax relief

## Who is this for?
- You must meet the following criteria to be eligible:
  - Singapore Citizens only
  - Aged 55 and above as of 31st December of the assessment year, Or below 55 years old with disability status verified with the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF)
  - Your Retirement Account (RA) savings^ or Ordinary and Special Account (OSA) savings are less than $110,200^^
  - Average monthly income not more than $4,000
  - Annual Value of Residence not more than $21,000
  - Owns not more than 1 property
- Your eligibility for the scheme is automatically assessed annually at the beginning of the year, and you do not need to apply
- You can check your eligibility via your [Retirement Dashboard](http://cpf.gov.sg/retirementdashboard)

RA savings refers to the RA balances (excluding amounts such as interest earned), plus retirement withdrawals and CPF LIFE premium deducted. If you are below 55 or turning 55 in the assessment year and your RA has not been created at the time we assess your eligibility, your total Special Account and Ordinary Account savings will be used for the eligibility assessment instead.

^^ Current Basic Retirement Sum for 2026.

## How to apply?
- You do not need to apply as your[ eligibility](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/who-is-eligible-for-the-matched-retirement-savings-scheme) is automatically assessed annually at the beginning of the year
- If you are eligible, CPF Board will notify you via email or post. You can check your eligibility via your [Retirement Dashboard](http://cpf.gov.sg/retirementdashboard)
- To [receive the matching grant](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/what-conditions-must-i-meet-in-order-to-receive-and-retain-the-matching-grant) you need to receive cash top-ups in your RA/SA , within the year that you are eligible for MRSS
- You can make a cash top-up [here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/cash-top-ups-and-cpf-transfers-for-retirement)

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/sub-categories?category=P_M_GYS)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/feedback)

## Phone number
CPF hotline (within Singapore): [1800-227-1188](tel:1800-227-1188) 
CPF hotline (from overseas): [+65-6227-1188](tel:+65-6227-1188)

To avoid waiting on the line, you may book an appointment [here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/appt/oas/form).

# Mobile Access for Seniors (MAS)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/MOBILE-ACCESS-SENIORS*

Provides subsidised smartphone and mobile plans to lower-income seniors who want to go digital but cannot afford them.

## Highlights
- 2-year mobile plan at $5.10 per month and smartphone from $20.00 (one-time cost)
- For Singapore Citizens aged 60 and above who are MSF ComCare or HDB PRS beneficiaries
- Pick up at least one basic digital skill at any SG Digital community hub to qualify

**Who it targets:** Low-income, Seniors
**Keywords:** Lower-income, Seniors, Subsidies

## About this support
Eligible seniors may enjoy the following subsidised product and service:

- 2-year mobile plan at $5.10 per month
- Smartphone from $20.00 (one-time cost)

The subsidised plan will come with:

- Free SIM card registration
- Free caller ID
- Unlimited incoming local calls
- Continued mobile data connectivity with no excess data charges
- Other value-added services

## Who is this for?
- 60 years old and above (based on birth year)
- Singapore Citizen
- Current beneficiary of any of these government assistance schemes:
  - MSF’s ComCare Long Term Assistance (LTA)
  - MSF’s ComCare Short-to-Medium Term Assistance (SMTA)
  - HDB’s Public Rental Scheme
- Not an existing IMDA Home Access beneficiary who has received a smartphone

## How to apply?
For eligible seniors only:

- Step 1: Attend our [Seniors Go Digital programme](https://go.gov.sg/supportgowhere-sngd) at any [SG Digital community hub](https://go.gov.sg/supportgowhere-sdohubs)^ and pick up at least 1 basic skill. Such skills include:
  - Digital communication
  - Navigating government digital services
  - Transacting with e-payments
- Step 2: Collect the MAS redemption voucher from our Digital Ambassadors.
- Step 3: Redeem the voucher at participating telcos.

Visit the [Digital for Life website](https://go.gov.sg/supportgowhere-sdohubs) or call [6377 3800](tel:63773800) to find your nearest hub.

Only 1 registration per senior is required.

^SG Digital community hubs are located at selected Community Clubs/Centres and public libraries. Visit the [Digital for Life website](https://go.gov.sg/supportgowhere-sdohubs) or call [6377 3800](tel:63773800) to find your nearest hub. As the hubs will be closed on public holidays, please check the [Digital for Life website](https://go.gov.sg/supportgowhere-sdohubs) for updates on opening dates and hours.

Tax relief on SRS contributions
embedding_text:
Domains: Financial support and benefits, Retirement and legacy planning

# Supplementary Retirement Scheme (SRS)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/leUjvFgL*

Provides tax relief to encourage individuals to save for retirement, over and above their CPF savings. Investment returns are tax-free before withdrawal and only 50% of withdrawals are taxable at retirement.

## Highlights
-  50% tax concession on withdrawals from SRS at retirement 
- Tax relief on SRS contributions

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Tax relief

## About this support
- Provides equivalent tax relief on contributions to SRS, capped at $15,300 for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents and $35,700 for foreigners
- Investment returns on SRS contributions are tax-free before withdrawal, and only 50% of withdrawals will be taxable at retirement

## Who is this for?
- You can only have 1 SRS account at any point in time
- To open an SRS account, you must:
  - be at least 18 years old.
  - not be an undischarged bankrupt.
  - have the mental capacity to make own decisions
  - not have an existing SRS account (including suspended accounts) with the same or another operator
  - not have a pending application with another SRS operator.
  - not have a previous SRS account with all its funds withdrawn, on medical grounds or after reaching the prevailing retirement age (at time of your first contribution)
- To qualify for SRS Tax Relief:
  - You must be a tax resident for the Year of Assessment following the year of SRS contribution
  - Your SRS account was not suspended on 31 Dec of the year of contribution
  - You did not withdraw, from your SRS account, the same amount as you contributed in the same year of contribution
- Please note that the following conditions / criteria apply to SRS withdrawals:
  - SRS withdrawals can be made anytime. Withdrawals can be made in cash or in the form of investments
  - Withdrawals are subject to income tax (based on the time and circumstances of withdrawal) and will be considered part of your taxable income
  - Foreigners and Permanent Residents who make withdrawals are subject to withholding tax
  - Withdrawals made before retirement age will be subject to penalties unless they were made due to exceptional circumstances.

You may read up on the additional criteria and details on [SRS withdrawals and the relevant taxes here](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/special-tax-schemes/tax-on-srs-withdrawals).

## How to apply?
- To open an SRS account:
  - Choose 1 of 3 SRS operators (DBS Group Holdings Ltd, Overseas-Chinese Banking Corporation (OCBC) Ltd, United Overseas Bank (UOB) Ltd.) to set up an SRS account with
  - Tax relief will be provided automatically, if eligible
- For foreigners:
  - You must complete the [SRS Declaration Form](https://www.iras.gov.sg/media/docs/default-source/uploadedfiles/doc/annual-declaration-form-for-supplementary-retirement-scheme.doc?sfvrsn=e34e4cdd_22)

Note: You must update your SRS bank operator if you become a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, even if you have already contributed this year, as your maximum contribution amount will have to be recalculated and may be pro-rated.

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.iras.gov.sg/contact-us/locate-us)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/special-tax-schemes/srs-contributions)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://www.iras.gov.sg/contact-us/individual-income-tax)

  - Foreigners and Permanent Residents who make withdrawals are subject to withholding tax
  - Withdrawals made before retirement age will be subject to penalties unless they were made due to exceptional circumstances.

You may read up on the additional criteria and details on [SRS withdrawals and the relevant taxes here](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/special-tax-schemes/tax-on-srs-withdrawals).
sections.How to apply?:
- To open an SRS account:
  - Choose 1 of 3 SRS operators (DBS Group Holdings Ltd, Overseas-Chinese Banking Corporation (OCBC) Ltd, United Overseas Bank (UOB) Ltd.) to set up an SRS account with
  - Tax relief will be provided automatically, if eligible
- For foreigners:
  - You must complete the [SRS Declaration Form](https://www.iras.gov.sg/media/docs/default-source/uploadedfiles/doc/annual-declaration-form-for-supplementary-retirement-scheme.doc?sfvrsn=e34e4cdd_22)

Note: You must update your SRS bank operator if you become a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, even if you have already contributed this year, as your maximum contribution amount will have to be recalculated and may be pro-rated.

highlights: Refunds ABSD for eligible seniors who have purchased their second property
embedding_text:
Domains: Financial support and benefits, Housing and shelters

# ABSD Concession for Single Singapore Citizen Seniors 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/CCLONfhj*

Provides single Singapore Citizen seniors (aged 55 and above) a refund for the Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) on their second residential property purchase.

## Highlights
- Refunds ABSD for eligible seniors who have purchased their second property

**Who it targets:** Seniors
**Keywords:** Home ownership, Seniors, Singles

## About this support
Fully refunds the ABSD for eligible seniors on their second residential property purchase.

## Who is this for?
Eligibility for the ABSD refund is subject to the following conditions:

- You must be a single Singapore Citizen senior (aged 55 and above) who purchased a second residential property on or after 16 February 2024
- You have paid the ABSD on the second property
- Your first residential property is solely owned by you (single Singapore Citizen aged 55 and above) / co-owned by you and your immediate family members^ (all are single Singapore Citizens aged 55 and above)
- The owners of the first residential property must also be owners of the second
- Any additional owners purchasing the second residential property with the owners of each first residential property must also be single Singapore Citizens aged 55 and above who are immediate family members
- The buyer(s) can only own up to 1 residential property each when purchasing the second property
- All buyers must not have purchased or acquired any other residential property since the purchase of the second residential property
- The first residential property must be sold or disposed of within 6 months of either:
  - the date of purchase of the second property (for completed property)
  - the date of issue of the Temporary Occupation Permit / Certificate of Statutory Completion whichever is earlier (for incomplete property)
- No change in ownership of the second property at the time of the first property's sale
- The value^^ of the second property must be less than each of the first properties that were sold
- The application for ABSD refund must be made within 6 months after the date of sale of the first property

^ Immediate family members refer to one's parent, child, or sibling.

^^ The “value” refers to the higher of the property’s purchase price or market value. The second property’s value is calculated as at its date of purchase. The first property is as at its date of sale.

## How to apply?
- Apply for the ABSD refund online through the [e-Stamping Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/estamping/) with these steps:
  - Select "Request" then "Apply for Assessment / Appeal"
  - Select "Assessment (including remission and penalty)"
  - If the document is stamped, select "Yes" and enter the Document Ref No., then click “Continue” to fill in the rest of the details and submit the form
  - If the document has not been stamped, please stamp it and pay the ABSD before applying for the ABSD Concession
  - To stamp the document, select “Stamping” > “Sale & Purchase – Purchase/Acquisition” then select the relevant form (e.g. For purchase of residential property, select the “Sale and Purchase Agreement” or “Acceptance to Option to Purchase” document description and fill in the details)
- At the “Supporting Documents” page, under “Additional Information”, please key in “ABSD Concession for Single SC Seniors”
- Please also submit both the following supporting documents with your application:
  - Copy of the exercised Option to Purchase / Sale and Purchase Agreement (if applicable) for the purchase of the second residential property
  - Copy of the exercised Option to Purchase / Sale and Purchase Agreement (if applicable) for the sale of the first residential properties
- For successful applicants, the refund will be made to the party liable for payment of stamp duty.

## Where to go
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.iras.gov.sg/contact-us/locate-us)

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/stamp-duty/for-property/appeals-refunds-reliefs-and-remissions/common-stamp-duty-remissions-and-reliefs-for-property/absd-concession-for-single-singapore-citizen-(sc)-seniors)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://www.iras.gov.sg/contact-us/stamp-duty-enquiries)

## Phone number
IRAS hotline: [1800-356-8300](tel:1800-356-8300)

embedding_text:
Domains: Active Ageing, Healthcare and well-being

# Active Ageing Centres (AAC)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-AACAAACHASACS*

A centre for seniors to build strong social connections, take part in recreational activities, access community health services, and contribute to the community.

**Who it targets:** Seniors
**Citizenship:** SG, PR
**Keywords:** Day Care

## About this support
Provide opportunities for seniors to stay physically and mentally active, explore interests and meet other seniors, such as:

- Active ageing activities to keep seniors engaged within the community
- Befriending services for vulnerable seniors who require additional social support
- Making referrals for care services when required
- Providing assistance as a social connector for social and lifestyle interventions to support seniors in adhering to their health plan recommendations
- Supporting seniors in the measurement of their vital signs in adherence to their health plan

Active Ageing Centre (Care), or AAC (Care), provides AAC services and additional care services, such as day care and community rehabilitation.

## Who is this for?
Seniors aged 60 and above who are Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.

## How to apply?
You may:

- Drop by an AAC in your neighbourhood to sign up
- Find out more at any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)

Visit [AIC’s website](https://www.aic.sg/Care-Services/Active-Ageing-Centres) to search for AACs by** **postal code, address or your device’s current location.

For further assistance, you can contact AIC via the hotline[1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060) or [submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg).

- Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines in Singapore.
- Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.

## What to expect?
- Active ageing programmes:
  - Organise a variety of activities such as karaoke, arts & craft, cooking and exercise
- Befriending & buddying:
  - Provide social support to seniors through house visits and phone calls
- Information and referral to care services:
  - Provide information on schemes, grants and support
  - Raise referrals to appropriate services
  - Management of emergency alert response calls
- Social connector for social and lifestyle interventions:
  - Assist seniors with recommendations in adherence to their health plan (e.g. registering for active ageing programmes)
- Community screening:
  - Help seniors measure their vital signs as required in adherence to their health plan

Domains: Financial/Retirement Planning, Housing and shelters

# Community Care Apartments (CCAs)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/CCA*

Senior-friendly housing integrated with care and social services that can be scaled according to care needs and social activities to support seniors who are 55 and above to age independently within the community.

## Highlights
- Homes with pre-installed fittings and senior-friendly design features
- Mandatory Basic Service Package (BSP) that provides support from CCA staff, including 24-hour emergency response
- Optional paid care and support services that residents may take up based on their needs 

**Who it targets:** Seniors
**Keywords:** Home ownership

## About this support
- Each CCA unit comes with senior-friendly design features such as easy-to-slide partitions for privacy, built-in wardrobe and cabinets for storage, and a wheelchair-accessible bathroom with slip-resistant flooring and grab bars.
- Flexibility to choose a lease ranging from 15 to 45 years (in 5 year increments) as long as it lasts the applicant(s) and their spouse(s) (if any) until at least age 95.
- Eligible first-timers may apply for the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant ([Families](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/couples-and-families/enhanced-cpf-housing-grant) or [Singles](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/singles/enhanced-cpf-housing-grant)) for the flat purchase.
- All residents must subscribe to the Basic Service Package (BSP), which includes the help from a CCA staff with simple home fixes, arranging add-on care and support services, and 24-hour emergency response.
- Residents can add on optional services for assistance with Activities of Daily Living (ADL), as well as fall monitoring, housekeeping and meal services.
- Eligible CCA applicants who require permanent assistance with at least one ADL may qualify for means-tested subsidies for relevant BSP components. More details on BSP fees and subsidies are available at [Vanguard Healthcare’s website](https://www.vanguardhealthcare.com.sg/our-services/assisted-living/basic-service-package).

## Who is this for?
- Applicant must be a Singapore Citizen (SC)
- If you are applying with your spouse, or parent(s)/child(ren), at least one of them must be a SC or Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR)
- If your spouse is not an SC or SPR, they must be included as a core occupier
- All applicant(s) and their spouse(s) (if any) must be at least 55 years old at the time of HFE letter application
- Monthly household income should not exceed $16,000

**Other conditions**

- If any person listed in the application owns or has an interest in any HDB flat or private residential property, the property must be disposed of within 6 months from the completion of the flat purchase.
- Applicant(s) and their spouse(s) (if any) are not eligible to buy a CCA if they had previously enjoyed 2 or more housing subsidies, one of which was a Studio Apartment, or a short-lease 2-room Flexi flat or CCA.

**Additional amount payable**

Some applicants will have to make an additional payment on top of the flat price e.g. resale levy. Visit [HDB InfoWeb](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/bto-sbf-and-open-booking-of-flats/finding-a-new-flat/types-of-flats/community-care-apartments) for more details.

## How to apply?
- Apply for an [HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp27/PrelimHFE/) early to be informed of your eligibility to buy a CCA and the amounts of CPF housing grants you are eligible for.
- Visit the [**HDB Flat Portal**](http://homes.hdb.gov.sg/) for details on the flats to be offered on our upcoming Build-To-Order (BTO) exercise. For Sale of Balance Flats (SBF) exercise, details on the flats for sale will only be made available during the sales exercise.
- With a valid HFE letter indicating your eligibility for CCA, apply online via the [HDB Flat Portal](https://homes.hdb.gov.sg/home/landing) during the application period of a sales exercise.
- From 4 weeks after the release of the ballot results, you will be invited to book a flat.
- Within 9 months after booking a flat, you will be invited to sign the Agreement for Lease.
- When your booked flat is ready, you will be invited to sign the BSP Agreement and collect the keys.

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/bto-sbf-and-open-booking-of-flats/finding-a-new-flat/types-of-flats/community-care-apartments)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/write-to-us)

# Short-lease 2-room Flexi Flats

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/SL-TR-FLEXI*

An affordable housing option for senior citizens (and their spouses) aged 55 and above who wish to right-size and continue living independently.

## Highlights
- Monetisation option to supplement retirement needs
- Flexibility to choose a lease ranging from 15 to 45 years (in 5-year increments) as long as it lasts the applicant(s) and their spouse(s) (if any) until at least age 95

**Who it targets:** Seniors
**Keywords:** HDB households, Home ownership, Seniors

## About this support
- Comes with pre-installed senior-friendly fittings such as grab bars and easy-to-slide partitions to separate living and bedroom spaces for privacy
- Applicant(s) may apply for 1 priority scheme to enhance their chances in the computer ballot for a short-lease 2-room Flexi flat:
  - [Senior Priority Scheme (SPS) (near existing home)](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/bto-sbf-and-open-booking-of-flats/process-for-buying-a-new-flat/application/priority-schemes?anchor=sps)
  - [Family Care Scheme (FCS) (Proximity)](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/bto-sbf-and-open-booking-of-flats/process-for-buying-a-new-flat/application/priority-schemes?anchor=fcs-proximity)
  - [Family Care Scheme (FCS) (Joint Balloting)](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/bto-sbf-and-open-booking-of-flats/process-for-buying-a-new-flat/application/priority-schemes?anchor=fcs-joint-balloting)
- Eligible first-timers may apply for the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant ([Families](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/couples-and-families/enhanced-cpf-housing-grant) or [Singles](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/singles/enhanced-cpf-housing-grant))
- Eligible buyers may apply for the [Silver Housing Bonus (SHB)](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/retirement-planning/monetising-flat-for-retirement/silver-housing-bonus) if they are selling their current flat or private housing with an Annual Value not exceeding $21,000 and buying a 3-room or smaller flat

## Who is this for?
- Applicant must be a Singapore Citizen (SC)
- If you are applying with your spouse, or parent(s)/child(ren), at least one of them must be a SC or Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR)
- If your spouse is not an SC or SPR, they must be included as a core occupier
- All applicant(s) and their spouse(s) (if any) must be at least 55 years old at the time of HFE letter application
- Monthly household income should not exceed $16,000

**Other conditions**

- If any person listed in the application owns or has an interest in any HDB flat or private residential property, the property must be disposed of within 6 months from the completion of the flat purchase.
- Applicant(s) and their spouse(s) (if any) are not eligible to buy a short-lease 2-room Flexi flat if they had previously enjoyed 2 or more housing subsidies, one of which was a Studio Apartment, or a short-lease 2-room Flexi flat or Community Care Apartment (CCA).

**Additional amount payable**

Some applicants will have to make an additional payment on top of the flat price e.g. resale levy. Visit [HDB InfoWeb](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/seniors) for more details.

## How to apply?
- Apply for an [HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp27/PrelimHFE/) early to be informed of your eligibility to buy a short-lease 2-room Flexi flat and the amounts of CPF housing grants you are eligible for.
- Visit the [HDB Flat Portal](http://homes.hdb.gov.sg/) for details on the flats to be offered on our upcoming Build-To-Order (BTO) exercise. For Sale of Balance Flats (SBF) exercise, details on the flats for sale will only be made available during the sales exercise.
- With a valid HFE letter indicating your eligibility for a short-lease 2-room Flexi flat, apply online via the [HDB Flat Portal](https://homes.hdb.gov.sg/home/landing) during the application period of a sales exercise.
- From 4 weeks after the release of the ballot results, you will be invited to book a flat.
- Within 9 months after booking a flat, you will be invited to sign the Agreement for Lease.
- When your booked flat is ready, you will be invited to collect the keys.

- Applicant(s) and their spouse(s) (if any) are not eligible to buy a short-lease 2-room Flexi flat if they had previously enjoyed 2 or more housing subsidies, one of which was a Studio Apartment, or a short-lease 2-room Flexi flat or Community Care Apartment (CCA).

**Additional amount payable**

Some applicants will have to make an additional payment on top of the flat price e.g. resale levy. Visit [HDB InfoWeb](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/seniors) for more details.
sections.How to apply?:
- Apply for an [HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/web/bp27/PrelimHFE/) early to be informed of your eligibility to buy a short-lease 2-room Flexi flat and the amounts of CPF housing grants you are eligible for.
- Visit the [HDB Flat Portal](http://homes.hdb.gov.sg/) for details on the flats to be offered on our upcoming Build-To-Order (BTO) exercise. For Sale of Balance Flats (SBF) exercise, details on the flats for sale will only be made available during the sales exercise.
- With a valid HFE letter indicating your eligibility for a short-lease 2-room Flexi flat, apply online via the [HDB Flat Portal](https://homes.hdb.gov.sg/home/landing) during the application period of a sales exercise.
- From 4 weeks after the release of the ballot results, you will be invited to book a flat.
- Within 9 months after booking a flat, you will be invited to sign the Agreement for Lease.
- When your booked flat is ready, you will be invited to collect the keys.

# New/Resale Flats (Singles) 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/PUR-NRSF-SIN*

Helps eligible singles decide if new or resale flats would be suitable for their consideration and provides them a holistic understanding of their housing and financing options for these flats.

## Highlights
- Eligible singles may apply for a 2-room Flexi flat from HDB or a resale flat on the open market
- Various housing grants are available in addition to the housing loan. Eligible first-timer singles may receive housing grants of up to $60,000 for new flats, and up to $115,000 for resale flats.

**Who it targets:** Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** HDB households, Housing grants, Singles

## About this support
Eligible singles may:

- Apply for new 2-room Flexi flats (99-year lease) in all locations, across Standard, Plus and Prime projects
- Buy an Unclassified/ Standard or Plus resale flat of any size, excluding 3Gen flats
- Buy a 2-room resale Prime flat
- Access to various housing grants for eligible singles

## Who is this for?
**Singles/ Two or more singles**

All applicant(s) must:

- Be Singapore Citizen (SC) or include at least 1 other co-applicant who is an SC (if applying jointly).

**If buying a new flat**

- At least 35 years old
- Monthly household income ceiling not exceeding $8,000
- Have not taken any housing subsidy
- Must not own, or have an interest in or dispose of any private residential property (local or overseas) in the last 30 months
- An additional amount is payable if you are buying a new flat alone
- Flat types available: 2-room Flexi flat (99-year lease)

**If buying a resale flat**

- At least 21 years old (widowed or an orphan) or at least 35 years old (unmarried or divorced)
- For Unclassified/ Standard flat: No income ceiling (Income ceiling applies to qualify for HDB housing loan and CPF housing grants [excluding Proximity Housing Grant])
- For Plus flat: Monthly household income ceiling not exceeding $16,000
- For Prime flat: Monthly household income ceiling not exceeding $8,000
- Must not own, or have an interest in or dispose of any private residential property (local or overseas) in the last 30 months if you are buying a resale flat with CPF housing grants
- Flat types available:
  - All flat types (excluding 3Gen flats) in any location
  - Up to 5-room if applying for CPF housing grants

## How to apply?
- Apply for a HFE letter by visiting the [HDB Flat Portal](https://homes.hdb.gov.sg/home/landing)
- The letter will support you to acquire a holistic understanding of your housing and financing options, inform you on your eligibility to purchase new or resale flats and determine the amount of CPF housing grants and HDB housing loan you are eligible for

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/buying-a-flat/flat-grant-and-loan-eligibility/singles)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](http://go.gov.sg/hdb-write-to-us)

## Phone number
HDB Hotline: [6866-3066](tel:6866-3066).
