# Renting Out of HDB Flats

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/K450UIdj*

Enables eligible Singapore Citizen flat owners to rent out their HDB flat after meeting the Minimum Occupation Period.

## Highlights
- Only Singapore Citizens can rent out HDB flats
- Fulfill Minimum Occupation Period (MOP) before renting out (Prime and Plus flats cannot be rented out)
- Non-Citizen Quota applies for non-Malaysian tenants
- Approval from HDB required before renting out

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** HDB households, Home ownership

## About this support
- Receive rental income through renting out your flat where necessary

- Provide an option to seniors to monetise your flat and move to live with family members

## Who is this for?
- Owner must be a Singapore Citizen to rent out the HDB flat. Singapore Permanent Residents are not allowed to do so.
- Fulfill a Minimum Occupation Period (MOP) of 5 years, or 3 years for non-subsidised flats purchased before 30 August 2010. Non-subsidised flats refer to those purchased from the open market without a housing grant. Owners of Prime and Plus flats are not allowed to rent out the flat even after the 10-year MOP. Owners of 2-room Flexi flats, Studio Apartments and Lease Buyback Scheme (LBS) flats are also not eligible to rent out their flat.
- MOP is calculated from the date of purchase or the effective date of transfer of flat ownership.
- Do consider the Non-Citizen Quota, if owners are renting to tenants who are non-Malaysian non-citizens (Singapore Permanent Residents or foreigners). Use [HDB’s e-Service](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/BR12AWNCQuota/) to check if your flat can be rented out to non-Malaysian non-citizens.

## How to apply?
- Flat owners must ensure that they comply with the regulations listed on [HDB’s website](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/home-ownership/renting-out-a-flat-or-bedrooms/renting-out-a-flat/eligibility) before renting out their flats. These include the number of tenants and their legal residency status.
- 'Apply/ Manage Application to Rent Out Flat' [e-Service](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/BR12AWFlatRentOutApplication) or [MyHDB mobile app](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/myhdb-mobile-app). An administrative fee of $18 applies for each application.
- Notify HDB of any changes in rental details (e.g. changes to your tenants’ particulars or if your tenants move out of the flat) within 7 days, and obtain approval for new tenants before they move in.

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/home-ownership/renting-out-a-flat-or-bedrooms/renting-out-a-flat)

## Email / Form
[Submit an enquiry](http://go.gov.sg/hdb-write-to-us)

# Rise to Wellness - Integrated Wellness Recovery Programme (RTW-I)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/S8Qtkqge*

RTW-I is an integrated, structured wellness recovery programme which aims to improve and sustain the mental health recovery of persons with mental health condition (PMHCs) and/or addiction issues

**Who it targets:** Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, PR
**Keywords:** Free

## About this support
The programme consists of:

- Peer Support Groups
- Anonymous Groups
- Recovery talks/workshops/activities
- Befriending
- 1-to-1 peer support
- Counselling/therapy (on a needs basis)
- Coaching
- Short-term crisis respite

## Who is this for?
Singaporean residents, 18 years old and above, either current or new members of PSALT Care, with a formal diagnosis of a mental health condition (self-declaration). Individuals who do not have a formal diagnosis but are interested to receive RTW-I services will be assessed by PSALT Care staff, clinicians or collaboration partner.

## How to apply?
For further queries:
•  WhatsApp: +65 6205 5538; 9628 5608
•  Email: [support@psaltcare.com](mailto:support@psaltcare.com)
•  Website: [www.psaltcare.com.sg](http://www.psaltcare.com.sg)

## What to expect?
RTW-I is a 9 to 12 months programme and you will be paired with a dedicated supporter who will journey with you 1-to-1 to understand your recovery needs and recommend curated recovery resources to benefit you. Together, you'll make a personal wellness recovery plan to chart your progress, while there will be opportunities to take part in activities that support and empower your recovery, while strengthening your sense of social connection, inclusion and overall wellbeing.

# Our HEALing Voice

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-OHV*

Clients may be referred by healthcare professionals, social workers or come in through self-referral.

Structured 12 session training to equip clients with the skills to share their lived experience and provide peer mentoring/support. Clients who completed OHV programme can join the OHV network to share their lived experience at Club HEAL’s outreach platforms and/or provide peer support to other PMHCs/individuals in distress.

# Mental Health GP Partnership/ Polyclinic

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/VelRMbGu*

Partnership with General Practitioners (GPs) and polyclinics to provide care for both mental and physical health with a single GP or polyclinic.

**Who it targets:** Seniors
**Citizenship:** SG, PR
**Keywords:** Intervention and Therapy, Seniors, Suicide Intervention

## About this support
- Manage both your physical and mental health conditions with a single GP or polyclinic
- Provides early identification, assessment, diagnosis, treatment, and stabilisation of mental health conditions and dementia at participating GP and polyclinics.
- Works with community mental health teams who can provide support such as counselling and psychotherapy.

## Who is this for?
Anyone who prefers to have both their mental and physical health conditions managed by the same GP or polyclinic.

## How to apply?
Visit the [AIC’s website](https://www.aic.sg/Care-Services/Mental-Health-GP-Partnership-Polyclinic) to search for participating GPs and polyclinics by** **postal code, address or your device’s current location.

For further assistance, you can contact AIC via the hotline[1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060) or [submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg).

- Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines in Singapore.
- Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.

## What to expect?
- Costs will vary between clinics.
- Singapore Citizens can use CHAS and Medisave for outpatient treatment at participating GPs and polyclinics.

Domains: Mental health

# Cognitive Intervention Programme (CIP)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/Nqhtnjri*

Centre-based programme for seniors with mild to moderate dementia.

**Who it targets:** Seniors
**Citizenship:** SG, PR
**Keywords:** Dementia support, Seniors, Social-emotional Support

## About this support
A weekly centre-based programme that helps seniors with dementia improve their cognitive functions and stay socially engaged, through:

- Activities that simulate the brain and memory functions, e.g. word and memory games
- Physical exercises, e.g. resistance training, silent disco, etc
- Social group-based activities, e.g. art and music

## Who is this for?
- Singapore Citizen (SC) or Permanent Resident (PR)
- Senior who is diagnosed by a doctor to have mild to moderate dementia and is suitable for group-based activities

## How to apply?
- Visit the [AIC’s website](https://www.aic.sg/Care-Services/Cognitive-Intervention-Programme) to search for service providers by** **postal code, address or your device’s current location.
- Contact the service provider directly to find out more.

For further assistance, you can contact AIC via the hotline[1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060) or [submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg).

- Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines in Singapore.
- Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.

## What to expect?
- CIP runs for 7 weeks, with 3-hour sessions held twice a week.
- Subsidies are available depending on the [means-test result](https://www.aic.sg/Care-Services/Cognitive-Intervention-Programme#faq).
  - Only applicable to SCs and PRs
- Transport to and from the centre and home is available at an additional cost.

# Psychiatric Rehabilitation and Re-integration

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/Ic7eUpmo*

Long-term support for persons with stable, chronic mental health conditions who are in recovery.

**Who it targets:** Seniors
**Citizenship:** SG, PR
**Keywords:** Seniors, Social-emotional Support, Suicide Intervention

## About this support
Provides long-term support for persons in recovery to improve their quality of life and live in the community, such as:

- Life skills training
- Social and emotional rehabilitation
- Recovery support (e.g. symptom management, follow-up appointments etc)
- Psychological support (e.g. counselling, family engagement etc)
- Assistance with job skills training and placements
- Finding housing services

## Who is this for?
Anyone who is diagnosed by a doctor to have a stable and long-term mental health condition.

## How to apply?
- You can apply through the doctor you are currently receiving care from, as you will need to be assessed for the services required.
- If you are interested to view a list of providers, visit the [AIC’s website](https://www.aic.sg/Care-Services/Psychiatric-Rehabilitation-and-Re-Integration).

- Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines in Singapore.
- Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.

## What to expect?
- Services are provided at either a stay-in facility or a day centre.
- Subsidies are available depending on the [means-test](https://aic.sg/care-services/home-medical#faq) result.
  - Only applicable for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents

# Budget 2026 CPF Top-Up 

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/WOuv5ZHU*

Provides additional support to boost the retirement adequacy of eligible Singaporeans with CPF retirement savings below prevailing Basic Retirement Sum (BRS) through a CPF top-up in 2026.

## Highlights
- Eligible seniors can receive up to $1,500 in CPF top-up
- No application needed - eligibility will be automatically assessed

**Who it targets:** Seniors
**Keywords:** Budget 2026, CPF top-ups, Seniors

## About this support
$500 to $1,500 in CPF top-up for eligible Singaporean seniors, tiered by CPF retirement savings and Annual Value of the place of residence

## Who is this for?
**Eligibility criteria**

- Singapore Citizen
- 50 years old and above in 2026
- CPF LIFE/Retirement Account or Ordinary/Special Account balances below prevailing BRS in 2026 of $110,200 as at 31 December 2025
- Tiered by annual value of the place of residence (as indicated on NRIC), as at 31 December 2025
- Does not own more than 1 property

## How to apply?
No application needed – eligibility will be automatically assessed

## Agency website
[View more details](https://www.govbenefits.gov.sg/)

## Phone number
CPF hotline: [1800 222 2888](tel:18002222888)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/JOBSKLINT*

Targeted at companies building industry-relevant skills and individuals seeking relevant jobs and skills matches.

## Highlights
- Pilot for Jobs-Skills Integrator in Precision Engineering, Retail, and Wholesale Trade sectors

- Individuals receive careers advisory and job matching services

- Training courses with integrated career services that can equip you with in-demand skills to help you transit into or within the sector

# Career Conversion Programme (CCP) for Individuals

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/CCPIND*

Support mid-career new hires or existing employees seeking to transition into growth job roles with good longer-term prospects.

## Highlights
- Undergo on-the-job training to take up new growth job roles
- Salary support of up to 90% for mid-career individuals
- Apply through CCP-supportable jobs on MyCareersFuture

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Employment Support and Vocational Training, Mid-career, Workers

## About this support
- Access on-the-job training to switch careers into growth sectors with long-term prospects
- Salary support of up to 90% for mid-career workers
- Embark on a new career with CCPs across around 30 sectors

## Who is this for?
Mid-career individuals should meet the following criteria:

- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- Aged 21 or above
- Graduated or completed National Service, for at least 2 years
- Career conversion is required:
  - New Hire: New job role trained for under the CCP should be substantially different from previous job role before joining CCP
  - Existing Employee: New job role should be growth job roles identified under the Jobs Transformation Maps (JTMs)
- Able to commit to full-time employment or attachment in a participating company

Beyond the general eligibility criteria, different CCPs may have additional course-specific entry requirements, and employers may apply their own -specific shortlisting process. In general, individuals applying for CCPs should also not be shareholders, immediate ex-staff, or related to owners/decision-makers of the CCP participating company or its related entities.

## How to apply?
Apply for CCPs here through CCP-supportable jobs on [MyCareersFuture](https://www.mycareersfuture.gov.sg/).

## Agency website

description: Aims to equip out-of-school youths and youths-at-risk with job competency as well as specific vocational skills.
embedding_text:
Domains: Work and employment

# YMCA Vocational and Soft Skills Programme (VaSSP)

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-YVASSPV*

Aims to equip out-of-school youths and youths-at-risk with job competency as well as specific vocational skills.

**Who it targets:** Vulnerable
**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS
**Keywords:** Referral required, Youths at risk

## About this support
The YMCA Vocational and Soft Skills Programme (VaSSP), also known as Project Bridge, aims to equip out-of-school youths and youths-at-risk of dropping out (who are absent from school for a long period) with essential soft skills and vocational expertise, enabling them to enhance their employability to integrate into the workforce or to reintegrate to education.

Conducted over 6 months, the programme consists to three phases: Core Training, Vocational Training, and Monitoring Phase. Service users engage in soft skills training, covering crucial areas such as goal setting, resume writing, interview skills, and communication and conflict resolution.

Subsequently, youths can select one out of 14 vocational tracks and receive certified training in the chosen industry. Thereafter, YMCA staff will continue to monitor the service users for a period of time before completion of the programme by supporting them in aspects such as career counselling or academic support in the service users' journey to either obtain employment or reintegrate back into education.

## Who is this for?
- Unemployed youths or school leavers between 15 and 21 years old
- Educational attainment of 'N' levels or below
- Pass the admission interview
- Able to commit and attend full-time training, and achieve 75% attendance and above

## How to apply?
- Email - projectbridge@ymca.org.sg
- Students can be referred by school counsellor or other social service agencies

## What to expect?
- Interested parties can write in to VaSSP and a staff will be in touch within 3 working days
- Youths will need to go through admission interview and meet the criteria of the programme

# Company-Led Training (CLT) Programme

*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/CLT*

Deepen your tech and media skills through on-the-job training in emerging tech and media areas such as artificial intelligence, cyber security, data analytics and virtual production.

## Highlights
- On-the-job training for in-demand tech and media skills
- Work on projects guided by experienced mentors
- Enhance your employability and career pathways in tech and media roles

**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable
**Keywords:** Technology, Workers

## About this support
- Gain employment and receive a salary while being equipped with in-demand tech and media skills
- Work on projects guided by experienced mentors
- Gain in-depth industry exposure
- Enhance your employability and career pathways in tech and media roles

## Who is this for?
Participating organisations must:

- Be a Singapore-registered company.
- Employ professionals in tech and media job roles that are in demand by the industry.
- Have the capability and capacity to deliver training programmes, with a good track record in human resource development.
- Commit resources including practical projects and qualified mentors to support trainees’ learning.
- Provide structured career progression pathways based on skills and competencies.
- Ensure that Singapore Permanent Residents (SPRs) do not exceed 15% of total trainees who have completed training.

## How to apply?
You can visit the [list of eligible companies](https://www.imda.gov.sg/How-We-Can-Help/TechSkills-Accelerator-TeSA/Company-Led-Training-Programme-CLT/Full-List-of-Job-Roles) and apply via the partners' website.
